title: Event Hooks System
description:
## Overview

Implement SQLAlchemy-style event hooks for models.

## Event Types

### Instance Events
- before_insert - Before INSERT executed
- after_insert - After INSERT executed
- before_update - Before UPDATE executed
- after_update - After UPDATE executed
- before_delete - Before DELETE executed
- after_delete - After DELETE executed
- load - After loading from database
- refresh - After refresh from database

### Attribute Events
- set - When attribute value changes
- append - When item added to collection
- remove - When item removed from collection

### Session Events
- before_flush - Before flush begins
- after_flush - After flush completes
- before_commit - Before commit
- after_commit - After commit
- after_rollback - After rollback

## Rust Implementation

Use traits and callbacks:
```rust
pub trait ModelEvents {
    fn before_insert(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> { Ok(()) }
    fn after_insert(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> { Ok(()) }
    fn before_update(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> { Ok(()) }
    fn after_update(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> { Ok(()) }
    fn before_delete(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> { Ok(()) }
    fn after_delete(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> { Ok(()) }
}
```

Or use attribute-based hooks:
```rust
#[derive(Model)]
struct User {
    #[sqlmodel(on_insert = "hash_password")]
    password: String,
}
```

## Use Cases

- Audit logging
- Password hashing
- Timestamp updates (created_at, updated_at)
- Validation that requires DB access
- Cache invalidation
- Notification triggers

title: Implement hybrid properties
description:
## Description

Properties that work both in Python/Rust AND in SQL queries.

## Python Behavior

```python
from sqlalchemy.ext.hybrid import hybrid_property

class User(SQLModel, table=True):
    first_name: str
    last_name: str
    
    @hybrid_property
    def full_name(self):
        return self.first_name + ' ' + self.last_name
    
    @full_name.expression
    def full_name(cls):
        return cls.first_name + ' ' + cls.last_name

# Works in Rust:
print(user.full_name)

# Works in SQL:
session.exec(select(User).where(User.full_name == 'John Doe'))
# Generates: WHERE first_name || ' ' || last_name = 'John Doe'
```

## Rust Implementation

```rust
#[derive(Model)]
struct User {
    first_name: String,
    last_name: String,
}

impl User {
    // Rust-side computation
    pub fn full_name(&self) -> String {
        format\!("{} {}", self.first_name, self.last_name)
    }
}

// SQL expression for query
impl User {
    pub fn full_name_expr() -> Expr {
        Expr::col("first_name")
            .concat(" ")
            .concat(Expr::col("last_name"))
    }
}

// Usage in query
select\!(User)
    .filter(User::full_name_expr().eq("John Doe"))
```

### With macro
```rust
#[derive(Model)]
struct User {
    first_name: String,
    last_name: String,
    
    #[sqlmodel(hybrid, sql = "first_name || ' ' || last_name")]
    full_name: Hybrid<String>,
}
```

title: Implement OperationProgress bar for determinate operations
description:
## Purpose
Create a progress bar renderable for operations where we know the total count, showing completion percentage, throughput, and ETA.

## Background
Bulk operations (batch inserts, data exports, migrations) need progress feedback. Users want to see:
- How much is done vs remaining
- Current throughput
- Estimated time to completion
- Running elapsed time

## Implementation Details

### File Location
crates/sqlmodel-console/src/renderables/operation_progress.rs

### Core Struct
OperationProgress holds:
- completed: u64
- total: u64
- started_at: Instant
- operation_name: String
- theme: Theme
- width: Option<usize>
- show_eta: bool
- show_throughput: bool

### Rendering (Rich Mode)
Uses rich_rust ProgressBar with customizations:
- Colored bar based on completion percentage
- Percentage display
- Items processed counter
- Throughput calculation
- ETA based on current rate

Format: Inserting rows [===>    ] 42% (420/1000) 50.2/s ETA: 12s

### Throughput Calculation
rate = completed / elapsed_seconds
eta_seconds = (total - completed) / rate

### Style Variations
- Standard: Blue bar
- Success (100%): Green bar
- Warning (slow): Yellow bar
- Error (stalled): Red bar

### Plain Text (Agent Mode)
Inserting rows: 42% (420/1000) 50.2 rows/s ETA: 12s

## API Design
OperationProgress::new(name, total)
  .completed(n)  // or .increment() / .add(n)
  .theme(theme)
  .show_eta(true)
  .show_throughput(true)
  .width(60)
  .render(width) / .render_plain()

### Update Pattern (for live progress)
let mut progress = OperationProgress::new("Inserting", 1000);
for batch in batches {
    // do work
    progress.add(batch.len());
    console.update_progress(&progress);
}

## Verification Steps
1. Test at 0%, 50%, 100%
2. Verify throughput calculation accuracy
3. Verify ETA reasonableness
4. Test with very fast operations (sub-second)
5. Test with very slow operations (minutes)
6. Verify plain text parseable format
7. Test width constraints

## Dependencies
- rich_rust ProgressBar component
- Theme from this crate
- std::time::Instant for timing
acceptance_criteria:
OperationProgress shows percentage completion
Progress bar respects terminal width
Progress shows elapsed time and ETA
Plain mode outputs percentage updates
All unit tests verify progress calculation
Performance tests confirm low overhead

title: Create shared quote_ident() utility in sqlmodel-core

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## What

Create a single, well-tested `quote_ident()` function that all crates use for SQL identifier quoting.

## Where

Add to: crates/sqlmodel-core/src/types.rs (or a new identifiers.rs module)
Re-export from: crates/sqlmodel-core/src/lib.rs

## Current State

create.rs already has a private quote_ident:
```rust
fn quote_ident(name: &str) -> String {
    format!("\"{}\"", name.replace('"', "\"\""))
}
```

This is correct for ANSI SQL double-quoting. We need to:
1. Move it to sqlmodel-core so all crates can use it
2. Add a `quote_ident_backtick()` variant for MySQL
3. Make it public
4. Add comprehensive tests

## Implementation

```rust
/// Quote a SQL identifier using ANSI double-quoting.
/// Embeds double-quotes are escaped by doubling ("" → """").
/// Safe against SQL injection for any input string.
pub fn quote_ident(name: &str) -> String {
    format!("\"{}\"", name.replace('"', "\"\""))
}

/// Quote a SQL identifier using MySQL backtick quoting.
/// Embedded backticks are escaped by doubling.
pub fn quote_ident_mysql(name: &str) -> String {
    format!("`{}`", name.replace('`', "``"))
}

/// Sanitize a SQL identifier by removing non-alphanumeric/underscore chars.
/// Use when quoting is not possible (PRAGMA, SHOW commands).
pub fn sanitize_identifier(name: &str) -> String {
    name.chars()
        .filter(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || *c == '_')
        .collect()
}
```

## Tests Required

- Empty string → `""`
- Simple name → `"users"`
- Embedded double quote → `"user""name"`
- SQL reserved word → `"select"` (quoting makes it safe)
- Unicode characters → properly quoted
- Null bytes → handled (stripped or error)
- Very long names → handled
- Backtick variant: same cases

## Acceptance Criteria

- Functions are public in sqlmodel-core
- At least 10 tests covering edge cases
- cargo clippy clean

title: ORM Patterns: Identity Map, Unit of Work, Lazy Loading
description:
## Overview

Implement core ORM patterns from SQLAlchemy that were previously 'excluded'.

## Identity Map

The identity map ensures each database row is represented by exactly one Python/Rust object within a session.

### Behavior
- When querying, check identity map first
- If object with same PK exists, return cached instance
- Prevents inconsistencies from multiple representations

### Rust Implementation
```rust
struct IdentityMap {
    // TypeId -> (PrimaryKey -> Weak<dyn Model>)
    cache: HashMap<TypeId, HashMap<PrimaryKeyValue, Weak<dyn Any>>>
}
```

## Unit of Work

Tracks all changes within a session and flushes them atomically.

### Object States
- Transient: Not attached to session
- Pending: Newly added, will be INSERTed
- Persistent: Attached and tracked
- Dirty: Modified, will be UPDATEd
- Deleted: Marked for DELETE
- Detached: Was persistent, now outside session

### Required Tracking
- new: Set of objects to INSERT
- dirty: Set of objects to UPDATE
- deleted: Set of objects to DELETE

## Lazy Loading

Relationships load on first access.

### Rust Approach
Since Rust doesn't have implicit lazy loading like Python, implement:
- LazyRelated<T> wrapper that defers loading
- Explicit .load() method
- Session context for loading
- Configurable eager vs lazy per relationship

title: Migrate session/flush.rs to shared quote_ident utility

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## What

Audit and update sqlmodel-session/src/flush.rs to use the shared quoting utility for all SQL identifier interpolation.

## Where

File: crates/sqlmodel-session/src/flush.rs

## Current State

flush.rs constructs SQL with double-quoted identifiers:
```rust
format!("INSERT INTO \"{}\" (\"{}\", \"{}\") VALUES ($1, $2)", table, local_column, remote_column)
format!("DELETE FROM \"{}\" WHERE \"{}\" = $1 AND \"{}\" = $2", table, local_column, remote_column)
```

The quoting is correct for simple names but doesn't escape embedded double-quotes. If a table name contains a literal `"`, the SQL is broken.

## Changes

Replace all `\"{}\"` patterns with `{}` using quote_ident():
```rust
format!("INSERT INTO {} ({}, {}) VALUES ($1, $2)",
    quote_ident(table), quote_ident(local_column), quote_ident(remote_column))
```

## Scope

Search: `rg '"\\"{}\\"' crates/sqlmodel-session/` to find all sites.

Also check UPDATE and DELETE SQL generation in the same file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All identifier interpolation in flush.rs uses quote_ident()
- No raw format!("\"{}\"") patterns remain

title: Implement fields_set tracking for exclude_unset support
description:
## Overview

Add compile-time tracking of which fields were explicitly set during model construction, enabling the exclude_unset option in model_dump().

## Background

Pydantic's exclude_unset differs from exclude_defaults:
- exclude_defaults: Excludes fields whose current value equals the default
- exclude_unset: Excludes fields that were never explicitly provided

Example: User(age=0).model_dump(exclude_unset=True) keeps age (explicitly set)
         User().model_dump(exclude_unset=True) removes age (using default)

## Implementation

1. Macro changes: Generate fields_set: HashSet<String> field
2. Track which fields are provided via builder or constructor
3. Update SqlModelDump to check fields_set when exclude_unset is true

## Complexity

Significant undertaking requiring proc macro modifications and serde integration.

Decision needed (tracked in bd-si4u.3): (a) accept TrackedModel as the exclude_unset mechanism, document it in FEATURE_PARITY, and close this bead; or (b) implement construction-time fields_set in the derive macro for wrapper-free Pydantic parity. Recommendation: (a) unless a consumer needs exclude_unset on plain structs; (b) costs a generated field on every model.

title: Implement schema extraction from Model definitions
EPIC: Pool Lock Poisoning Safety — eliminate all expect() from pool crate

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Background

The connection pool crate (sqlmodel-pool/src/lib.rs) contains 22 instances of `.expect("pool lock poisoned")` on Mutex::lock() calls. Per AGENTS.md, using unwrap()/expect() in library code is FORBIDDEN because:

1. If ANY thread panics while holding the pool mutex, the mutex becomes poisoned
2. All 22 sites then panic on their next access, causing cascading failures
3. The entire application crashes instead of gracefully degrading

## Scope

All 22 call sites in sqlmodel-pool/src/lib.rs need to be converted from:
```rust
let inner = self.shared.inner.lock().expect("pool lock poisoned");
```
to returning a Result type that propagates the error.

## Approach

This is an API-breaking change because pool methods like config(), stats(), at_capacity(), etc. currently return plain values. They need to return Result<T, PoolError> or similar. This cascades to callers.

**Strategy:** Introduce a PoolError::Poisoned variant, change public methods to return Result, update all internal callers, then update downstream crates (sqlmodel-session, sqlmodel facade).

## Why P1

Connection pools are fundamental infrastructure. A single panic in any pooled connection operation can take down an entire application server. This is a reliability/availability issue that affects every user of the library.

title: Implement Session.expunge_all()
description:
## Description

Remove all objects from session without deleting from database.

## Python Behavior

```rust
impl Session {

        self.dirty.clear();

}
```

title: Performance evidence: measure the PLAN success criteria (binary size, startup, row conversion, SQLite throughput) and guard them
description:
## Why this epic exists (reality check 2026-09-01)

PLAN_TO_PORT_SQLMODEL_TO_RUST.md "Success Criteria" (L201-207) sets four measurable targets: code size 10-20x smaller than Python SQLModel, binary size < 5 MB with LTO, startup < 10 ms, query latency competitive with native drivers. README's "Zero-cost abstractions" section claims "The generated code is as fast as hand-written implementations" and the comparison table gives SQLModel Rust ✅ on dependencies. None of this has been measured: the only benchmark in the workspace is `crates/sqlmodel-console/benches/console_bench.rs` (console rendering overhead). The release profile (`opt-level = "z"`, LTO, `panic = "abort"`, strip) is tuned for size, which makes the "as fast as hand-written" claim worth checking rather than assuming.

## Goal

Every PLAN target has a measured value, a benchmark that produces it, and a CI guard that catches large regressions; the README/PLAN report numbers, not adjectives.

## Children
- Criterion benches: SQL emission, row conversion, SQLite throughput vs a rusqlite baseline, pool acquire, Session flush.
- CI binary-size and startup-time checks against the PLAN thresholds.
- Record measurements in CHANGELOG/PLAN with dates; replace targets with measured values.
- Regression thresholds (generous, catch 2x) in CI.

title: Criterion benches: SQL emission, to_row/from_row vs hand-written, SQLite throughput vs rusqlite, pool acquire, Session flush
description:
## Context

No benchmarks exist for the ORM's hot paths. The claims to test: derive-generated `to_row`/`from_row` are "as fast as hand-written" (README); query builders are zero-cost; the drivers are "competitive with native drivers" (PLAN). `criterion` is an acceptable dev-dependency (not tokio-based); asupersync also ships benchmark adapters (`benchmark-adapters`, `criterion-benches` features) if async benches need a runtime.

## What to build (benches in `crates/sqlmodel-e2e/benches/` to keep dev-deps out of published crates; or per-crate `benches/` where the code lives — choose per bench, document)

1. `sql_emission`: `select!(Hero).filter(...).order_by(...).limit(...)` `to_sql` for each dialect; a 5-join eager select; a polymorphic_joined3 select; a 100-row `insert_many!`; report ns/op and allocations (use `criterion` + an allocation counter such as a custom global allocator in the bench binary).
2. `row_conversion`: `to_row` and `from_row` for a 12-column model vs a hand-written baseline implementation of the same struct (the README claim, measured directly); include `Option` fields and `Value::Text` cloning cost.
3. `sqlite_throughput`: 10k inserts (single statements, `insert_many!` batches of 100, inside one transaction), 10k point selects by PK, 1 full scan of 100k rows via `select!(...).all()` — on `sqlmodel-sqlite` vs a `rusqlite` baseline (dev-dep only; same bundled SQLite) doing the equivalent raw operations; report ratio. Same on `sqlmodel-frankensqlite` (no external baseline; report absolute and vs C-SQLite).
4. `pool_acquire`: acquire/release p50/p99 under 1, 4, 16 concurrent tasks with a mock connection and with real SQLite.
5. `session_flush`: flush of 1k new objects, 1k dirty objects, 1k deletes with cascade planning.
6. Run with `cargo bench -p sqlmodel-e2e` locally; CI runs `cargo bench --no-run` (compile check only) plus a short `--bench ... -- --quick` smoke on ubuntu to keep benches compiling.

## Success criteria
- All benches run and produce a results table (criterion HTML + a text summary printed by a tiny `--summary` mode or copied into the bead comment).
- Row-conversion ratio vs hand-written and SQLite ratio vs rusqlite are recorded with the machine spec; anything > 1.5x slower gets a follow-up bead with the profile attached (see profiling/optimization skills).

## Why
The performance sections of README and PLAN are currently adjectives; this produces the numbers and finds the hot spots if the adjectives are wrong.

title: CI size-and-startup job: minimal example binary asserts <5MB release size and <10ms median startup; cargo bloat report
description:
## Context

PLAN targets: binary < 5 MB with LTO; startup < 10 ms. The release profile is size-tuned (`opt-level = "z"`, LTO, `codegen-units = 1`, `panic = "abort"`, `strip = true`). Nothing builds a binary to check either number; the library has no example binary that exercises the full stack.

## What to build

1. `crates/sqlmodel-e2e/examples/minimal_app.rs` (or under the facade's examples with the `c-sqlite-tests` feature): open an in-memory SQLite, create a table from a derived model, insert one row, select it, print JSON; exits 0. Uses `sqlmodel` + `sqlmodel-sqlite` only. A second variant `minimal_app_franken` for the pure-Rust driver (nightly).
2. CI job `size-and-startup` (ubuntu, release): `cargo build --release --example minimal_app`; assert `stat -c %s` < 5 MiB (fail with the actual size); `hyperfine`-style measurement without extra tooling: run the binary 20 times with `/usr/bin/time -f %e` (or `perf stat`) and assert the median wall time < 10 ms (fail with the distribution). Print both numbers always so the log is a time series.
3. Also record the size of the two SQLite driver variants and `sqlmodel-postgres`/`-mysql` `--features tls` in a static-link-free `cargo bloat`-style report (`cargo bloat --release --crates`, dev tool installed in CI) attached as a job artifact — shows where bytes go (rustls, sqlite3, regex).
4. Document in PLAN's success-criteria table: the measured values with the CI job link, replacing the untested targets.

## Success criteria
- CI job green with printed size/startup values; thresholds equal the PLAN targets.
- If a threshold fails today, the bead comment records the actual value and a decision (raise the target with justification, or optimize) — do not silently loosen.

## Why
Two of the four PLAN success criteria become one CI job; the numbers either validate the size-tuned release profile or start an informed conversation about it.

title: Record measured performance in PLAN/CHANGELOG/README; replace adjectives with numbers (incl. honest code-size comparison)
description:
## Context

Once the benches and the size/startup job exist, the measurements must land where readers look, and the PLAN's targets table must stop presenting untested numbers as goals.

## What to do

1. PLAN_TO_PORT_SQLMODEL_TO_RUST.md "Success Criteria": add columns `Measured` and `Date / commit`; fill from the bench summary and CI job; keep the original targets as the `Target` column; add "Code size" measured as non-test Rust lines vs the Python SQLModel+Pydantic+SQLAlchemy line counts in `legacy_*` (compute both with `tokei` or `wc -l` and state the method; the 10-20x claim is almost certainly false given ~93k lines of Rust — record the truth).
2. CHANGELOG.md: a "Performance" subsection in the next release entry with the same numbers and the bench commands.
3. README: replace "The generated code is as fast as hand-written implementations" with the measured ratio sentence and a link to the bench; keep the claim only if the ratio is ≤ 1.1x.

title: Bench regression guard in CI with committed thresholds (2x margin) and monthly full-suite artifact
description:
## Context

title: Implement Decimal precision validation (max_digits, decimal_places)
description:
## Description

Add full Decimal type support with precision and scale validation.

## Python Behavior

```python
from decimal import Decimal

class Product(SQLModel, table=True):
    price: Decimal = Field(max_digits=10, decimal_places=2)
    # SQL: DECIMAL(10, 2) or NUMERIC(10, 2)
```

## Current Status

We have a workaround using sql_type attribute:
```rust
#[sqlmodel(sql_type = "DECIMAL(10,2)")]
price: Decimal,
```

But need native support matching Python.

## Rust Implementation

### Macro Attributes
```rust
#[derive(Model, Validate)]
struct Product {
    #[sqlmodel(max_digits = 10, decimal_places = 2)]
    price: rust_decimal::Decimal,
}
```

### SQL Generation
Generate correct DDL:
- PostgreSQL: NUMERIC(10, 2)
- MySQL: DECIMAL(10, 2)
- SQLite: TEXT (with validation)

### Validation
- Check total digits <= max_digits
- Check decimal places <= decimal_places

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] max_digits and decimal_places parsed from attributes
- [ ] Correct SQL type generated for each dialect
- [ ] Validation enforces constraints
- [ ] Works with rust_decimal crate

## Testing Requirements

### Unit Tests (crates/sqlmodel-macros/src/field.rs)
- [ ] Test max_digits parsed correctly
- [ ] Test decimal_places parsed correctly
- [ ] Test validation rejects too many digits
- [ ] Test validation rejects too many decimal places
- [ ] Test edge cases (0, negative, very large)

### E2E Tests (tests/e2e/decimal_validation.rs)
- [ ] price with max_digits=10, decimal_places=2
- [ ] Valid: 12345678.99 (10 digits, 2 decimal)
- [ ] Invalid: 123456789.99 (11 digits)
- [ ] Invalid: 12345678.999 (3 decimal places)
- [ ] Database roundtrip preserves precision

### Logging
- [ ] DEBUG: Decimal validation parameters
- [ ] TRACE: Digit counting

title: Implement discriminator for union types
description:
## Description

Support tagged unions with discriminator field.

## Python Behavior

```python
from typing import Union, Literal

class Cat(SQLModel):
    pet_type: Literal['cat'] = 'cat'
    meows: int

class Dog(SQLModel):
    pet_type: Literal['dog'] = 'dog'
    barks: int

class Pet(SQLModel):
    pet: Union[Cat, Dog] = Field(discriminator='pet_type')
```

## Rust Implementation

Use Rust enums with serde tag:
```rust
#[derive(Model, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "pet_type")]
enum Pet {
    #[serde(rename = "cat")]
    Cat { meows: i32 },
    #[serde(rename = "dog")]
    Dog { barks: i32 },
}
```

Or with structs:
```rust
#[derive(Model)]
struct Owner {
    #[sqlmodel(discriminator = "pet_type")]
    pet: PetUnion,
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] discriminator attribute parsed
- [ ] Correct serde tag generated
- [ ] Works with nested unions
- [ ] Validation of discriminator values

## Testing Requirements

### Unit Tests (crates/sqlmodel-macros/src/discriminator.rs)
- [ ] Test discriminator field parsing
- [ ] Test union type resolution
- [ ] Test discriminator in validation
- [ ] Test discriminator in serialization

### E2E Tests (tests/e2e/discriminator.rs)

title: Unreachable headline features: chrono/uuid/decimal mapping, FrankenSQLite BEGIN CONCURRENT, retry-on-conflict, Outcome invariant
description:
## Why this epic exists (reality check 2026-09-01)

Three headline capabilities exist in code or docs but cannot be reached through the ORM API as a user would use it:

1. **chrono/uuid/decimal type mapping.** README "Automatic Type Mapping" lists `chrono::NaiveDate -> DATE`, `chrono::NaiveDateTime -> TIMESTAMP`, `uuid::Uuid -> UUID`. `crates/sqlmodel-macros/src/infer.rs` maps those type NAMES to `SqlType`, but the generated `to_row` (`lib.rs` `generate_to_row`, ~L537-556) emits `sqlmodel_core::Value::from(self.field.clone())`, and `crates/sqlmodel-core/src/value.rs` has no `From<chrono::*>` / `From<uuid::Uuid>` / `From<rust_decimal::Decimal>` (no such optional dependencies exist anywhere in the workspace). A model with a `NaiveDate` field does not compile. AGENTS.md documents "i64 microseconds for timestamps — not chrono::NaiveDateTime". The README promises what the code refuses.

2. **FrankenSQLite MVCC concurrent writers.** AGENTS.md: "FrankenSQLite adapter — pure-Rust SQLite with MVCC (BEGIN CONCURRENT)". `crates/sqlmodel-frankensqlite/src/connection.rs` `begin_sync` (~L587-612) maps `IsolationLevel::{Serializable, RepeatableRead|ReadCommitted, ReadUncommitted}` to `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE | BEGIN IMMEDIATE | BEGIN DEFERRED`. `BEGIN CONCURRENT` appears only in the adapter's tests via `execute_raw`. `Session`, `Pool`, and the builders can never start a concurrent transaction. Furthermore `Error::is_retryable()` (`error.rs` L424) exists but nothing in session/pool/query consumes it: there is no retry-on-conflict combinator anywhere. The driver's defining advantage is unrealized.

3. **API invariant deviation.** `MysqlConnection::close_async(mut self, _cx: &Cx) -> Result<(), Error>` (`async_connection.rs` ~L1963) returns `Result` while PROPOSED_RUST_ARCHITECTURE §3.3 makes "all async DB APIs accept &Cx and return Outcome" an architectural invariant.

## Goal

Every README/AGENTS claim in this list becomes reachable from `use sqlmodel::prelude::*;` with tests on real drivers.

## Children
- Optional `chrono` / `uuid` / `decimal` features in sqlmodel-core with bidirectional Value conversions.
- Driver round-trip tests, trybuild compile-fail diagnostics, README type table with a feature column.
- Expose `BEGIN CONCURRENT` through Connection/Session/Pool as a transaction mode.
- Cancel-correct `retry_transaction` combinator + `Session::commit_with_retry`.
- `MysqlConnection::close_async` returns Outcome.

title: sqlmodel-core optional chrono/uuid/decimal features: bidirectional Value conversions with strict precision policy
description:
## Context

README's type table promises `chrono::NaiveDate`, `chrono::NaiveDateTime`, `uuid::Uuid` mappings; `infer.rs` recognizes those names (and `rust_decimal::Decimal`, L82) for `SqlType`, but `Value` (`crates/sqlmodel-core/src/value.rs`) only has `From` impls for bool, i8..i64, u8..u32, f32/f64, String/&str, &[u8], serde_json::Value, and `[u8;16]` (L272-390), and `FromValue`/`TryFrom<Value>` for the same primitive set (`row.rs` L250-560, `value.rs` L435-807). So a model field of those external types fails at `to_row`/`from_row` codegen. `Value` already has the right wire variants: `Date(i32 days)`, `Time(i64 us)`, `Timestamp(i64 us)`, `TimestampTz(i64 us)`, `Uuid([u8;16])`, `Decimal(String)`.

## What to build (sqlmodel-core, features re-exported by the facade)

1. `Cargo.toml` (workspace deps + core): `chrono = { version = "0.4", optional = true, default-features = false, features = ["std"] }`, `uuid = { version = "1", optional = true }`, `rust_decimal = { version = "1", optional = true, default-features = false }`. Features on core: `chrono`, `uuid`, `decimal`; facade passthroughs `chrono = ["sqlmodel-core/chrono"]` etc. Nothing enabled by default (keeps "lean dependencies" true).
2. `value.rs` (behind cfgs): `From<NaiveDate>` -> `Value::Date(days since 1970-01-01)`; `From<NaiveTime>` -> `Time(us since midnight)`; `From<NaiveDateTime>` -> `Timestamp(us since epoch, UTC-naive)`; `From<DateTime<Utc>>` and `From<DateTime<FixedOffset>>` -> `TimestampTz(us since epoch UTC)`; `From<Uuid>` -> `Uuid(bytes)`; `From<Decimal>` -> `Decimal(normalized string, scale preserved)`. Reverse: `TryFrom<Value>` and `FromValue` for each, accepting the structured variant AND the `Text` form (drivers sometimes deliver ISO-8601 text: MySQL text protocol, SQLite) using strict parsers; out-of-range (e.g. `Date(i32::MAX)`) -> `TypeError` with the value shown. Precision policy: nanoseconds beyond microseconds are REJECTED, not truncated (consistent with the crate's existing refusal of lossy i64->f64, see bd-21wb), documented on the impls.
3. `timestamps.rs` helpers already convert i64 <-> components (schema/migrate.rs L55 mentions avoiding chrono); reuse them for the `Text` fallbacks so the two code paths agree; add cross-check tests (component helper vs chrono for 10k sampled instants including leap days, year 1, year 9999, negative epochs).
4. Macro: no change needed for inference; add `Option<chrono::NaiveDate>` etc. to the macro's inference tests to lock the names.
5. `sqlmodel-core/src/lib.rs`: re-export the external types under `sqlmodel_core::types::{chrono, uuid, decimal}` modules (or document `use chrono::...` directly) so users have one import story.

## Success criteria
- `cargo test -p sqlmodel-core --features chrono,uuid,decimal` passes new unit tests: round trip of boundary values, Text-form parsing, rejection cases with messages.
- `cargo check -p sqlmodel-core` (no features) still compiles with zero new deps in `cargo tree`.
- A facade doctest with `#[derive(Model)] struct Event { when: chrono::NaiveDateTime, id: uuid::Uuid }` compiles under `--features chrono,uuid`.

## Why
Makes README's type table true instead of deleting it; the i64-microsecond core stays the wire format (AGENTS.md decision preserved) while users get the ergonomic types they expect from an ORM.
close_reason: DONE. sqlmodel-core optional features chrono / uuid / decimal (facade forwards them): From/TryFrom/FromValue for NaiveDate, NaiveTime, NaiveDateTime, DateTime<Utc>, DateTime<FixedOffset>, uuid::Uuid, rust_decimal::Decimal in core/src/external_types.rs with strict precision (no silent truncation; errors carry the offending value), unit tests; README type table gained a Feature column. Evidence: core lib tests 346 passed (step 8), GATES (final tree, 2026-09-02, self-verified): fmt clean; clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo doc --workspace --no-deps 0 warnings; cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast 61 suites 2041 passed 0 failed; doctests 52 passed; cargo audit --deny warnings clean; cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources ok. Driver round-trip matrix and trybuild feature-off diagnostics remain in bd-7wal.2.

title: chrono/uuid/decimal driver round-trip matrix, trybuild feature-off diagnostics, README type table with feature column
description:
## Context

Follow-up to the `chrono`/`uuid`/`decimal` feature bead. Conversions in sqlmodel-core prove nothing about what each driver actually stores and returns: SQLite stores dates as TEXT/REAL/INTEGER depending on the column affinity the DDL chose; MySQL's text protocol returns DATETIME as text while the binary protocol returns structured values (both decoders exist in `sqlmodel-mysql/src/types.rs`, per SESSION_TODO items 1.1 and E2); Postgres returns `date`/`timestamp`/`timestamptz`/`uuid`/`numeric` in binary or text depending on the statement path.

## What to build

1. In `crates/sqlmodel-e2e` (or the facade's sqlite tests if the e2e crate is not yet present), a round-trip matrix per driver: for each of `NaiveDate`, `NaiveTime`, `NaiveDateTime`, `DateTime<Utc>`, `Uuid`, `Decimal`: insert via `insert!(model)` with boundary values (epoch, 1900-01-01, 9999-12-31, 00:00:00.000000, 23:59:59.999999, negative decimals, 28-digit decimals, nil UUID, max UUID), read back via `select!(...).all()`, assert equality; also read via raw `query()` and assert the `Value` variant the driver delivered (documents the wire form per driver).
2. DDL check: `SchemaBuilder` for such models emits the correct dialect types (`DATE`, `TIME`, `TIMESTAMP`/`DATETIME`, `TIMESTAMPTZ`/`TIMESTAMP`, `UUID`/`CHAR(36)`/`BINARY(16)`, `NUMERIC(p,s)`/`DECIMAL(p,s)`) — decide and document the MySQL UUID representation (`BINARY(16)` recommended; `CHAR(36)` alternative via `sql_type` override) and the SQLite affinity choices.
3. `trybuild` dev-dependency (facade): compile-fail test showing the exact diagnostic when a model uses `chrono::NaiveDate` without the `chrono` feature; ensure the message points at the feature (add a `compile_error!`-style hint in the macro when it infers a chrono/uuid/decimal type name and the corresponding `sqlmodel_core` cfg is absent — the macro can emit a call to a feature-gated marker fn so the error names the feature).
4. README: type table gets a "Feature" column (`chrono`, `uuid`, `decimal`) and one sentence on the i64-microsecond wire format; AGENTS.md "Key Design Decisions" timestamp bullet updated to mention the optional adapters.

## Success criteria
- Round-trip matrix passes on C-SQLite, FrankenSQLite, Postgres, MySQL (MariaDB where types exist).
- trybuild test passes with a stored `.stderr` snapshot naming the feature flag.
- README table verified by the doc-truth guard test (docs epic).

## Dependencies
Blocked by the core conversions bead; uses the e2e crate skeleton when available.

title: Expose BEGIN CONCURRENT: TransactionOptions/TransactionMode through Connection, FrankenConnection, Session, builders
description:
## Context

`crates/sqlmodel-frankensqlite/src/connection.rs` `begin_sync` (~L587-612) issues `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` (Serializable), `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (RepeatableRead/ReadCommitted), or `BEGIN DEFERRED` (ReadUncommitted). FrankenSQLite's page-level MVCC with Serializable Snapshot Isolation is entered with `BEGIN CONCURRENT`, which the adapter never emits outside its own tests (L2037-2100 use `execute_raw("BEGIN CONCURRENT")`). `sqlmodel_core::Connection::begin_with(cx, IsolationLevel)` has no way to ask for it, so `Session`, `Pool` users, and the query builders' internal transactions (joined-inheritance DML uses `conn.begin`) always serialize writers. The driver's raison d'être is unreachable.

## Design

1. `sqlmodel-core/src/connection.rs`: add `TransactionOptions { isolation: IsolationLevel, mode: TransactionMode }` with `enum TransactionMode { Default, Concurrent, Immediate, Exclusive, Deferred }` (SQLite-family semantics; Postgres/MySQL map `Concurrent` to their default MVCC behavior, which already is concurrent, and `Immediate/Exclusive` to `LOCK TABLE`-free no-ops or explicit errors — document per driver). Add `fn begin_with_options(&self, cx, TransactionOptions) -> impl Future<Output = Outcome<Self::Tx<'_>, Error>> + Send` to the `Connection` trait with a default impl delegating to `begin_with(cx, options.isolation)` so existing drivers keep compiling; also on `TransactionOps` for nested savepoints nothing changes.
2. FrankenSQLite: implement `begin_with_options`: `Concurrent` -> `BEGIN CONCURRENT`; map `WriteConflict`/`SerializationFailure` (already matched in `franken_to_query_error`) to `QueryErrorKind::SerializationFailure` so `Error::is_retryable()` is true (verify: `is_retryable` L424 must include that kind; add if missing). Also add a sync helper `begin_concurrent_sync()` matching the existing sync family, and a `FrankenExclusiveTransaction` counterpart if the strict-durable profile needs it (respect the `StrictDurableControlPlane` profile rules: concurrent mode may be disallowed there — decide and test).
3. C-SQLite driver: `Concurrent` is not supported by stock SQLite -> return `Error::Query(Unsupported...)` with a message pointing at sqlmodel-frankensqlite, or downgrade to `IMMEDIATE` behind an explicit `TransactionMode::ConcurrentOrImmediate`? Decision: return an error (no silent downgrade; AGENTS.md "no hidden behavior"), and add `Dialect`/driver capability `supports_concurrent_transactions()` so callers can choose.
4. Session: `SessionConfig.transaction_mode: TransactionMode` (default `Default`); `flush`/`commit` paths use `begin_with_options`. Pool: pass-through (pool hands out connections; nothing to do beyond docs) — but add `PoolConfig.default_transaction_mode` if `Pool` wraps transaction helpers; verify.
5. Query builders: the joined-inheritance internal transactions accept the mode via the builder (`.transaction_mode(...)`) or via a connection-level default (`Connection::default_transaction_options()` with a driver default) — prefer the connection-level default so users set it once when opening the FrankenSQLite connection (`FrankenConnection::open_concurrent(...)` convenience constructor or `.with_default_transaction_mode(Concurrent)`).
6. Facade re-exports `TransactionOptions`, `TransactionMode`.

## Tests
- Adapter unit: `begin_with_options(Concurrent)` emits `BEGIN CONCURRENT` (assert via a second connection observing WAL/lock state or via the SQL recorder used in existing tests); two connections both in Concurrent mode writing disjoint rows commit without error; overlapping writes yield a retryable error on the second commit.
- Core: default-impl delegation compiles for MockConnection; `is_retryable` truth table includes SerializationFailure/WriteConflict.
- C-SQLite: Concurrent -> clear Unsupported error.
- Session: config plumbing test with the mock recorder asserting the BEGIN statement text.

## Success criteria
- `Session::<FrankenConnection>` configured with `TransactionMode::Concurrent` runs flush inside `BEGIN CONCURRENT` (SQL recorder proof) and the e2e MVCC contention bead can build on it.

## Why
Without this, "MVCC concurrent writers" is a property of a dependency, not of SQLModel Rust.
close_reason: DONE. TransactionMode {Default, Concurrent, Immediate, Exclusive, Deferred} + TransactionOptions in sqlmodel-core; Connection::supports_transaction_mode / begin_with_options (default impl refuses unsupported modes with TransactionErrorKind::UnsupportedMode); FrankenConnection issues BEGIN CONCURRENT (+ begin_concurrent_sync), C SQLite maps the locking modes and refuses Concurrent, Postgres/MySQL accept Concurrent as Default; SessionConfig::transaction_mode / Session::begin; facade + prelude re-exports; README section 4. Evidence: franken tests two_concurrent_writers_on_disjoint_pages_both_commit / conflicting_concurrent_writers_surface_a_retryable_error / explicit_locking_modes_map_to_their_begin_forms; e2e concurrent_writers on frankensqlite, postgres, mysql (run #8); GATES (final tree, 2026-09-02, self-verified): fmt clean; clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo doc --workspace --no-deps 0 warnings; cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast 61 suites 2041 passed 0 failed; doctests 52 passed; cargo audit --deny warnings clean; cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources ok. Builders need no change (they do not open transactions).

title: Cancel-correct retry_transaction combinator (RetryPolicy, budget-aware backoff) plus Session::commit_with_retry
description:
## Context

`sqlmodel_core::Error::is_retryable()` (`error.rs` L424: deadlock, serialization failure, pool exhausted, timeouts) exists and is tested, but no code in session/pool/query/facade calls it. Every MVCC database (Postgres SERIALIZABLE, MySQL InnoDB deadlocks, FrankenSQLite `BEGIN CONCURRENT`) requires callers to retry serialization failures; today each user must hand-roll a loop that is easy to get wrong under cancellation (retrying after the Cx was cancelled, or losing the `Panicked` outcome). The joined-inheritance DML path and `Session::flush` (which already "restore pending_new for retry", `session/lib.rs` ~L1864-1971) would benefit immediately.

## What to build (sqlmodel-core, re-exported by the facade)

1. `sqlmodel_core::retry` module:
   - `RetryPolicy { max_attempts: u32 (default 5), base_delay: Duration (10ms), max_delay: Duration (500ms), jitter: Jitter::Full, retry_on: fn(&Error) -> bool (default Error::is_retryable) }` with a builder.
   - `pub async fn retry_transaction<C, T, F, Fut>(cx: &Cx, conn: &C, options: TransactionOptions, policy: &RetryPolicy, body: F) -> Outcome<T, Error>` where `F: FnMut(&Cx, &C::Tx<'_>) -> Fut`, `Fut: Future<Output = Outcome<T, Error>>`. Semantics: begin -> body -> commit; on `Err(e)` with `policy.retry_on(&e)` from body OR from commit: rollback (ignore rollback errors after a failed commit but log them), sleep with backoff using asupersync's timer through the Cx (budget-aware: never sleep past `cx.budget()` deadline; if the remaining budget is smaller than the delay, return the last error as `Err`, or `Outcome::Timeout`-equivalent per the crate's convention), then retry. On `Cancelled` or `Panicked` from anywhere: rollback best-effort and propagate immediately — NEVER retry a cancelled attempt. Non-retryable errors propagate after rollback. Attempts exhausted -> return the last error wrapped so callers can distinguish (`Error::Transaction(TransactionError::RetriesExhausted { attempts, last })`, add the variant).
   - The body must be re-entrant: document that side effects outside the transaction (in-memory mutations) are the caller's responsibility; provide `retry_transaction_with_state` that hands the body a fresh clone of caller state per attempt.
2. `Session::commit_with_retry(cx, policy)` and `Session::flush_with_retry` that wrap the existing flush/commit inside `retry_transaction`, reusing the existing "restore pending_* for retry" bookkeeping so the identity map is consistent after a failed attempt. `SessionConfig.retry_policy: Option<RetryPolicy>` makes it automatic when set.
3. Builders: joined-inheritance `execute()` paths that open internal transactions honor a connection-level or builder-level policy (`.retry(&policy)`), default none (opt-in).
4. Tracing: DEBUG per attempt (attempt number, error kind, delay), WARN when exhausted.

## Tests (sqlmodel-core, mock connection with scripted failures + LabRuntime virtual time)
- Retries exactly `max_attempts` on persistent SerializationFailure, then `RetriesExhausted` with `attempts == max_attempts`.
- Succeeds on attempt 3 when the mock fails twice; body invoked 3 times; rollback called twice; commit once.
- Cancelled Cx during the backoff sleep -> `Outcome::Cancelled`, no further attempts (virtual time proves no sleep completed).
- Budget smaller than next delay -> returns without sleeping past the deadline.
- Non-retryable error -> single attempt, rollback called once.
- Panicked body -> `Outcome::Panicked`, rollback attempted, no retry.
- Backoff sequence deterministic under a seeded jitter for the test (inject the RNG).
- Session integration: mock connection fails first commit with SerializationFailure; `commit_with_retry` succeeds; pending sets are empty afterwards; identity map has the flushed objects exactly once.

## Success criteria
- All above tests pass; `cargo doc` renders an example in the module docs; the e2e MVCC bead uses this combinator unchanged.

## Why
Retry-on-conflict is the missing half of "cancel-correct" for MVCC databases: correctness under contention without violating cancellation. This closes the loop that `is_retryable` opened.
close_reason: DONE. retry_transaction (earlier) plus Session::with_retry(cx, &RetryPolicy, async |cx, session| ...): begins the transaction, runs the closure, commits, and on a retryable failure rolls back, clears the identity map, backs off (RetryPolicy::after_failure / RetryDecision, shared with retry_transaction) and re-runs the whole unit of work; cancellation is never retried; Session::into_connection added. The bead title said commit_with_retry; the closure form is what makes replay possible and is documented as such in CHANGELOG/README. EVIDENCE (self-verified): local Docker-backed run #11 on 2026-09-02 (scratchpad test_e2e_local_run11.log): sqlmodel-e2e concurrent_writers, migrations, pool, session, smoke pass on c-sqlite(memory), c-sqlite(file), frankensqlite, postgres (16, scram), mysql (8.4, caching_sha2); driver suites postgres 7/7 and mysql 7/7 (run #10). Remote run g2_run4: the same e2e scenarios plus types on the three SQLite drivers. concurrent_writers: two OS threads each running Session::with_retry around get_with_options(FOR UPDATE on pg/mysql) + mark_dirty: final=50 exactly on frankensqlite (retries observed), postgres, mysql.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: PARTIAL 2026-09-02: DONE - sqlmodel-core/src/retry.rs: RetryPolicy (max_attempts 5, base 10ms, max 500ms, full jitter via xorshift seeded from cx, retry_on = Error::is_retryable by default), retry_transaction(cx, conn, TransactionOptions, policy, AsyncFnMut body) that begins a transaction per attempt, rolls back on retryable failure, sleeps with budget-aware backoff (never past cx.budget().deadline), never retries Cancelled/Panicked, and returns Error::retries_exhausted(attempts, last) (new TransactionErrorKind::RetriesExhausted); 8 unit tests with a scripted connection; re-exported from the facade + prelude; e2e concurrent_writers proves it on FrankenSQLite with two OS threads. NOT DONE - Session::commit_with_retry: a commit-time failure after flush would need the identity map / pending-changes snapshot to replay; TrackedObject holds Box<dyn Any>, so a faithful replay needs a clone-able change log. Left open for that half; do not close on the combinator alone.

title: MysqlConnection::close_async returns Outcome and honors Cx (only deviation from the Outcome invariant)
description:
## Context

PROPOSED_RUST_ARCHITECTURE §3.3 and §10 (invariant 1): "All async database APIs accept `&Cx` and return `Outcome<_, Error>`". Audit on 2026-09-01 (`rg 'pub async fn .*-> (sqlmodel_core::)?Result<'` over the driver/session/pool crates) found exactly one deviation: `crates/sqlmodel-mysql/src/async_connection.rs` ~L1963 `pub async fn close_async(mut self, _cx: &Cx) -> Result<(), Error>`. It also ignores its `Cx` (no checkpoint before the network write of COM_QUIT).

## What to do

1. Change the signature to `-> Outcome<(), Error>`; call `cx.checkpoint()` (or the crate's equivalent guard) before sending COM_QUIT so a cancelled Cx yields `Outcome::Cancelled` without touching the socket; map I/O errors to `Outcome::Err`.
2. Update all call sites (`rg close_async`), including `SharedMySqlConnection`/`Connection::close` wrappers and tests; keep `Drop` best-effort behavior unchanged.
3. Add a unit test: pre-cancelled Cx -> `Cancelled` and the connection state is still `Open` (or `Closed` by explicit choice — document); normal path -> `Ok`.
4. Re-run the audit command and add it as a comment in PROPOSED_RUST_ARCHITECTURE §10 next to invariant 1 so the check is repeatable (one-liner, no script file).

## Success criteria
- `rg -n 'pub async fn .*-> (sqlmodel_core::)?Result<' crates/sqlmodel-{postgres,mysql,sqlite,frankensqlite,session,pool}/src` prints nothing.
- `cargo test -p sqlmodel-mysql` passes.

## Why
Small, but it is the only hole in an invariant the architecture doc calls out by number; closing it keeps "invariant" meaning invariant.
close_reason: Re-scoped on inspection 2026-09-02: the deviation is by design, not an oversight. sqlmodel_core::Connection::close(self, cx) is declared as -> impl Future<Output = Result<()>> (connection.rs L317) and every driver (postgres L1606, sqlite L988, frankensqlite L1022, pool mock L1616) implements it that way; MysqlConnection::close_async mirrors the trait. Closing is best-effort teardown that must complete even under cancellation, so an Outcome::Cancelled result would be meaningless. Recorded as the one documented exception to invariant 1 in PROPOSED_RUST_ARCHITECTURE.md section 9, with the audit command adjusted to allow close_* methods. No code change.

title: Phase 7: Database Driver Console Integration
description:
## Purpose
Integrate the console output system into each database driver crate, providing rich feedback for connection establishment, query execution, and driver-specific operations.

## Background
Each driver (PostgreSQL, SQLite, MySQL) has unique operations that benefit from rich output:
- Connection establishment with progress/status
- Authentication feedback (especially multi-step like SCRAM)
- Query timing and explain plan visualization
- Driver-specific features (PostgreSQL COPY, SQLite pragmas, MySQL procedures)

## Key Deliverables

### 1. sqlmodel-postgres Console Integration
- Connection establishment progress (DNS resolve -> TCP connect -> SSL -> Auth)
- SCRAM authentication step visualization
- Query timing display
- EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE visualization with tree rendering
- COPY progress for bulk operations

### 2. sqlmodel-sqlite Console Integration
- Database file operations (open, create, attach)
- PRAGMA visualization
- Transaction state indicator
- WAL checkpoint progress

### 3. sqlmodel-mysql Console Integration
- Connection establishment with capability negotiation
- Authentication plugin feedback
- Query timing
- SHOW commands formatting

## Integration Pattern
Each driver implements ConsoleAware trait:
- fn set_console(&mut self, console: Option<Arc<SqlModelConsole>>)
- Operations check if console is Some and output mode is Rich
- All output goes to stderr (non-semantic)
- Plain mode outputs nothing or minimal text

## Agent Safety
All driver console output:
1. Goes to stderr only (stdout reserved for query results)
2. Can be disabled via output mode
3. Plain mode emits parseable text only

## Dependencies
- Phase 2 (Core Infrastructure) - SqlModelConsole
- Phase 6 (Pool & Operations) - progress components
- Respective driver crates must be ready

## Verification
- Test each driver with console enabled/disabled
- Verify agent mode produces no rich output
- Performance test (console output must not slow queries)

MySQL driver implements ConsoleAware trait

title: FrankenSQLite: last_insert_rowid() drifts after a failed INSERT and after INSERT ... RETURNING (report upstream to fsqlite)
description: Found by the C SQLite vs FrankenSQLite differential oracle (crates/sqlmodel-e2e/tests/sqlite_differential.rs, 2026-09-03, fsqlite 0.3.14 vs C SQLite 3.53.2, cross-checked with the sqlite3 CLI 3.46). Reference semantics: a failed INSERT (constraint violation) and both UPSERT paths leave last_insert_rowid() unchanged; INSERT ... RETURNING sets it to the new rowid. FrankenSQLite: after a failed INSERT into a table whose key is not a rowid alias (BIGINT ... PRIMARY KEY (id)), last_insert_rowid() moves to the rowid that would have been assigned (12 -> 13 in the script), and after INSERT ... RETURNING it reports 14 while the row's actual rowid is 12 (a freed rowid was reused). A successful plain insert reports the correct rowid on both drivers, so insert!(..).execute() is right in the common path; the stale value surfaces in what an UPSERT's execute() returns and when the counter is read without a successful insert in between. Also: fsqlite stores the CREATE TABLE text verbatim in sqlite_master (keeps IF NOT EXISTS) where C SQLite normalizes it. The divergences are pinned in KNOWN_DIVERGENCES with reasons; when an fsqlite release fixes them the test fails as 'stale divergence' and the entries must be removed. Action: report to the fsqlite repository with the script's minimal reproduction (create table t(id bigint not null, primary key(id)); insert 1..12; delete 12; failing insert; select last_insert_rowid()), then track the fix through the dependency refresh.

title: EPIC: Value Type Safety — fix silent data corruption in numeric conversions

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Background

The `Value` enum in sqlmodel-core/src/value.rs has several lossy type conversions that silently corrupt data:

1. **`From<u64> for Value`** (line 254): Casts u64 to i64 via `as i64`. For values > i64::MAX (9,223,372,036,854,775,807), this silently wraps to negative numbers. This is a DATA CORRUPTION bug.

2. **`TryFrom<Value> for f32`** (lines 411-416): Converts f64/i32/i64 to f32 via `as f32`. For i32 > 16,777,216 or f64 values outside f32 range, precision is silently lost.

3. **`TryFrom<Value> for f64`** (line 436): Converts i64 to f64 via `as f64`. For i64 > 2^53, precision is silently lost.

4. **`FromValue for f32`** in row.rs (lines 408-425): Same lossy conversions when reading from database rows.

## Why This Matters

These conversions happen in the core data path — every value read from or written to a database flows through `Value`. Silent data corruption in this layer is catastrophic:
- Financial amounts could be wrong
- IDs could collide
- Timestamps could wrap
- Users would never know their data is corrupted

## Strategy

For u64→i64: Either add a `Value::UBigInt(u64)` variant or change `From<u64>` to `TryFrom<u64>`. The TryFrom approach is less invasive but removes the ergonomic From impl.

For f32/f64 precision: Add range checks that return errors instead of silently truncating.

## Why P1

Data integrity is non-negotiable for a database library. Silent corruption is worse than a crash — at least a crash is noticed.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
EPIC complete. All 4 child tasks closed:
- bd-1epw: Fixed From<u64> silent overflow with saturating conversion
- bd-31ed: Fixed lossy f32 conversions with precision-loss detection
- bd-21wb: Fixed lossy i64-to-f64 conversion with precision-loss detection
- bd-1bt4: Added comprehensive conversion boundary tests

comments.text: ROOT CAUSE: MySQL sends TEXT/TINYTEXT/MEDIUMTEXT/LONGTEXT on the BLOB wire types (0xF9-0xFC) and CHAR/VARCHAR vs BINARY/VARBINARY on the same string types; only ColumnDef.charset (63 = binary) distinguishes them. decode_text_value / decode_binary_value / decode_binary_value_with_len (types.rs) mapped every BLOB wire type to Value::Bytes and ignored the charset, so every TEXT column came back as BLOB: mysql_integration roundtrip 'name TEXT' failed with TypeError expected String actual BLOB, and Introspector::mysql_check_constraints silently dropped every row because CHECK_CLAUSE (LONGTEXT) failed get_named::<String>().ok(). title: Create TableInfo panel for single-table details
description:
## Purpose
Implement a Panel-based renderable that displays comprehensive information about a single database table, including columns, indexes, foreign keys, and statistics.

## Background
When users want to inspect a specific table in detail (similar to psql \d tablename), they need:
- Table name and metadata in a header
- Column details in a formatted table
- Index information
- Foreign key relationships
- Table statistics (row count, size if available)

This is complementary to SchemaTree - SchemaTree shows the overview, TableInfo shows the details.

## Implementation Details

### File Location
crates/sqlmodel-console/src/renderables/table_info.rs

### Key Components
1. TableStats struct - holds optional runtime statistics
2. TableInfo struct - main renderable with schema reference
3. Builder methods for theme, width, stats
4. Internal helpers to build columns table, indexes section, FK section
5. render() method for rich mode using Panel + Table
6. render_plain() method for agent mode

### Features
- Columns displayed in a rich_rust Table within a Panel
- Shows column name, type, nullable, default, constraints
- Indexes section with UNIQUE/INDEX type and columns
- Foreign keys showing local->remote.column relationships
- Optional stats: row count (with thousand separators), size (formatted as KB/MB/GB)

### Helper Functions
- format_number(): Add thousand separators to numbers
- format_bytes(): Convert bytes to human-readable KB/MB/GB

## Usage Example
let table_info = TableInfo::new(&user_table_schema)
    .with_stats(TableStats {
        row_count: Some(10_000),
        size_bytes: Some(2_500_000),
        ..Default::default()
    })
    .width(80);
console.print_renderable(&table_info);

## Verification Steps
1. Test with table having all features (indexes, FKs, defaults)
2. Test with minimal table (just columns)
3. Verify plain text output is parseable
4. Test width constraints
5. Verify stats formatting
6. Test with empty table schema

## Dependencies
- sqlmodel-schema for TableSchema types
- rich_rust Panel and Table components
- Theme from this crate

title: Create Agent Compatibility Guide for AI coding tools
description:
## Purpose
Write detailed documentation for AI coding agent authors and users, explaining how sqlmodel-console maintains compatibility with automated tools.

## Background
AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI) are primary users of sqlmodel_rust. This guide ensures:
- Agent authors understand the output contract
- Users know how to configure for agents
- Developers know how to maintain compatibility

## Implementation Details

### File Location
docs/console/agent-compatibility.md

### Document Structure

#### 1. Why Agent Compatibility Matters
- AI agents parse stdout/stderr
- Rich formatting breaks parsing
- Agent detection prevents issues
- Stream separation preserves semantics

#### 2. How Auto-Detection Works
Environment variables checked (in order):
1. CLAUDE_CODE - Claude Code CLI
2. CODEX_CLI - OpenAI Codex CLI
3. CURSOR_SESSION - Cursor IDE
4. GEMINI_CLI - Google Gemini CLI
5. CODY_AGENT - Sourcegraph Cody
6. AIDER_MODE - Aider
7. CI - Generic CI environment

Detection logic:
- If any agent env var set: Plain mode
- If not a TTY (piped): Plain mode
- Otherwise: Rich mode

#### 3. Stream Separation Contract
stdout (semantic):
- Query results (rows, columns)
- Success/failure status codes
- Structured data (JSON if requested)

stderr (decorative):
- Progress indicators
- Connection status
- Timing information
- Formatted errors (visual version)

#### 4. Plain Text Output Format
Errors:
ERROR: Connection timeout (SQLMODEL-E001)
  Host: localhost:5432
  Timeout: 30s

Progress:
Inserting rows: 50% (500/1000) 123 rows/s

Results:
id | name  | email
1  | Alice | alice@example.com
2  | Bob   | bob@example.com
(2 rows)

#### 5. Environment Variables Reference
| Variable | Values | Effect |
|----------|--------|--------|
| CLAUDE_CODE | any | Force plain mode |
| SQLMODEL_PLAIN | 1 | Force plain mode |
| SQLMODEL_FORCE_RICH | 1 | Force rich mode |
| SQLMODEL_NO_COLOR | 1 | Disable colors |

#### 6. Testing Agent Compatibility
# Run in plain mode
SQLMODEL_PLAIN=1 cargo run --example query

# Simulate Claude Code
CLAUDE_CODE=1 cargo run --example query

# Verify no ANSI codes
SQLMODEL_PLAIN=1 cargo run --example query 2>&1 | cat -v

#### 7. For Agent Authors
Recommended detection:
- Set your unique env var
- Register it with us (open issue)
- Document for your users

Parsing recommendations:
- Read stdout for data
- Optionally display stderr to user
- Handle both rich and plain gracefully

#### 8. Maintaining Compatibility (for contributors)
Rules:
1. Never put semantic data in stderr
2. Plain mode must have zero ANSI codes
3. All new features need plain output
4. Test in CI (non-TTY environment)

## Verification Steps
1. All env vars documented
2. Stream contract clear
3. Plain format parseable
4. Agent detection accurate
5. Testing instructions work
6. Contributor guidelines clear

## Dependencies
- OutputMode detection finalized
- All agent env vars known
- Stream separation tested

description:
## Description

Full JSON type support with querying capabilities.

## Python Behavior

```python
from sqlalchemy import JSON
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import JSONB

class Config(SQLModel, table=True):
    settings: dict = Field(sa_type=JSON)
    metadata: dict = Field(sa_type=JSONB)  # PostgreSQL
```

```rust
}

// JSON path queries

    .filter(Config::settings.json_extract("key").eq("value"))
```

title: SchemaBuilder/CreateTable emit SQLite-only DDL for every dialect (double quotes, INTEGER PRIMARY KEY): never worked on MySQL, auto-increment never worked on Postgres/MySQL
close_reason: FIXED. EVIDENCE (self-verified; no independent verifier available): local Docker-backed run #8 on 2026-09-02 (scratchpad test_db_backed_local_run8.log; RCH_SHIM_LOCAL_IDE=1 escape hatch because remote workers cannot reach the local containers postgres:16 @127.0.0.1:55432 scram-sha-256 and mysql:8.4 @127.0.0.1:53306 caching_sha2_password): sqlmodel-mysql lib 100 passed, tests/mysql_integration 7 passed 0 failed; sqlmodel-postgres lib 59 passed, tests/postgres_integration 7 passed 0 failed; sqlmodel-e2e concurrent_writers/migrations/smoke each 1 passed, exercising c-sqlite(memory), c-sqlite(file), frankensqlite, postgres, mysql. GitHub Actions runs for the pushed commits were still queued (never started) when checked, so CI itself has not been observed running these. Before the fix (run #5) e2e smoke on mysql failed on the DDL 'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "e2e_smoke_gadgets"'; run #8 passes the smoke scenario on mysql and postgres via SchemaBuilder::new().dialect(driver.dialect()). Unit test create_table_is_dialect_aware added; README example corrected.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE: sqlmodel-schema create.rs CreateTable::build / SchemaBuilder used sqlmodel_core::quote_ident (ANSI double quotes) unconditionally and spelled a single-column auto-increment PK as SQLite's INTEGER PRIMARY KEY. MySQL rejects double-quoted identifiers outright (e2e smoke: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "e2e_smoke_gadgets" ... failed on Docker mysql:8.4), and on PostgreSQL/MySQL 'INTEGER PRIMARY KEY' is a plain key with no auto-assignment, so any auto_increment model created through SchemaBuilder could not insert without an explicit id. FIX: CreateTable and SchemaBuilder carry a Dialect (default Sqlite = unchanged historical output; .dialect(conn.dialect()) otherwise): Dialect::quote_identifier everywhere, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT + no CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS, PostgreSQL GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY (skipped when the type already says SERIAL); STI ALTER TABLE path and create_index follow the dialect. Unit test create_table_is_dialect_aware; README example corrected (it showed output the builder never produced: 'BIGINT AUTOINCREMENT'). FOUND BY: sqlmodel-e2e tests/smoke.rs against Docker mysql:8.4. Proof: e2e smoke on Postgres+MySQL (to be posted).

title: Session API: Complete All Methods
description:
## Overview

Implement ALL Session methods from Python SQLModel/SQLAlchemy.

## Required Session Methods

### Core CRUD
- add(instance) - Add object to session ✅
- add_all(instances) - Add multiple objects
- delete(instance) - Mark for deletion ✅
- get(entity, ident, ...) - Get by primary key
- merge(instance, load=True) - Merge detached instance

### Transaction Control
- commit() - Commit transaction ✅
- rollback() - Rollback transaction ✅
- flush(objects=None) - Flush pending changes ✅
- begin() - Begin transaction ✅
- begin_nested() - Savepoint ✅
- close() - Close session

### State Management
- refresh(instance, attribute_names=None) - Refresh from DB
- expire(instance, attribute_names=None) - Expire instance cache
- expire_all() - Expire all instances
- expunge(instance) - Remove from session ✅
- expunge_all() - Remove all from session
- is_modified(instance, ...) - Check if modified

### Query Execution
- exec(statement, ...) - Execute and return models
- execute(statement, ...) - Low-level execute (deprecated in Python)
- scalars(statement, ...) - Return scalar values

## Missing/Incomplete Methods

1. **add_all** - Bulk add
2. **get** - Primary key lookup (different from query)
3. **merge** - Merge detached objects back
4. **expire/expire_all** - Cache invalidation
5. **is_modified** - Dirty checking
6. **refresh** - Reload from database

## Unit of Work Pattern

Python SQLAlchemy tracks:
- New objects (pending insert)
- Dirty objects (pending update)
- Deleted objects (pending delete)
- Identity map (object cache by PK)

We need to implement this fully for proper ORM behavior.

# Epic: Rich Rust Integration

## Executive Summary

Integrate the `rich_rust` library throughout sqlmodel_rust to provide stunning, professional

## Background & Motivation

### The Problem
Currently, sqlmodel_rust has no standardized console output. When users or observers watch

title: Implement Session.expire() and expire_all()
description:
## Description

Expire cached object attributes, forcing reload on next access.

## Python Behavior

```python
# Expire specific attributes
session.expire(user, ['name', 'email'])

# Expire all attributes
session.expire(user)

# Expire all objects in session
session.expire_all()
```

After expiring, next attribute access reloads from DB.

## Rust Implementation

```rust
impl Session {
    pub fn expire<M: Model>(&mut self, model: &M, attributes: Option<&[&str]>) {
        let pk = model.primary_key_value();
        if let Some(state) = self.get_state_mut::<M>(&pk) {
            match attributes {
                Some(attrs) => state.expire_attributes(attrs),
                None => state.expire_all(),
            }
        }
    }
    
    pub fn expire_all(&mut self) {
        for state in self.all_states_mut() {
            state.expire_all();
        }
    }
}
```

## Identity Map State

Each tracked object needs state:
```rust
struct ObjectState {
    expired_attrs: HashSet<String>,
    fully_expired: bool,
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] expire() marks specific attributes as expired
- [ ] expire(model) marks all attributes expired
- [ ] expire_all() expires all session objects
- [ ] Expired attributes reload on access
- [ ] Works with lazy relationships

## Testing Requirements

### Unit Tests (crates/sqlmodel-core/src/session/expire.rs)
- [ ] Test expire marks object stale
- [ ] Test expire_all expires all objects
- [ ] Test expire with attribute subset

## Description

Add validation for collection (Vec, array) fields.

```python
class Order(SQLModel):
```

```rust
if self.items.len() < 1 {
    errors.add_min_items("items", 1, self.items.len());
```
