title: Security baseline: cargo audit clean with documented ignores, CI that can fail, forbidden crates enforced by cargo-deny
description:
## Why this epic exists (reality check 2026-09-01)

`cargo audit` on the current lockfile (327 crates) reports:
- **1 vulnerability**: `rsa 0.10.0-rc.18` RUSTSEC-2023-0071 "Marvin Attack: potential key recovery through timing sidechannels" (medium 5.9, no fixed version). Direct dependency of sqlmodel-mysql (auth.rs) for `sha256_password` / `caching_sha2_password` full authentication without TLS.
- **3 unmaintained**: `bincode 1.3.3` (RUSTSEC-2025-0141) and `yaml-rust 0.4.5` (RUSTSEC-2024-0320), both via `syntect 5.3.0 <- rich_rust 0.2.3 <- sqlmodel-console`; `rustls-pemfile 2.2.0` (RUSTSEC-2025-0134), direct in sqlmodel-mysql `tls.rs` (three call sites: CA bundle, client cert, client key).
- **1 yanked**: `chacha20 0.10.1` via `asupersync -> chacha20poly1305` (fixed by `cargo update` to 0.10.2; done in the 2026-09 dependency refresh).

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `cargo audit || true`, so the Security job can never fail. AGENTS.md's forbidden-crate list (tokio, hyper, reqwest, axum, tower, async-std, smol, sqlx, diesel, sea-orm) is enforced only by convention.

## Goal

`cargo audit` exits 0 with only documented, time-boxed ignores; CI fails on new advisories; the forbidden-crate list is enforced mechanically by `cargo deny`; the MySQL RSA path is either feature-gated away for TLS-only users or its non-exploitability is recorded where auditors look.

## How it serves the vision

README: "Lean dependencies ... focused crypto/regex deps"; FAQ: "Is this production-ready? Nearly." A red audit that CI hides contradicts both. This epic converts the security posture from asserted to enforced.

## Children
- RUSTSEC-2023-0071 reachability analysis + audit.toml ignore with rationale (extends bd-d5qe).
- Feature-gate MySQL RSA authentication (`rsa-auth`, default on).
- Replace rustls-pemfile with rustls-pki-types PEM parsing (extends bd-mn7e).
- bincode/yaml-rust via rich_rust/syntect: cross-repo fix + time-boxed ignore (extends bd-mn7e).
- CI: real audit gate + cargo-deny bans enforcing AGENTS.md's forbidden crates.

title: RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (rsa Marvin): record non-reachability analysis, audit.toml ignore with review date, source-scan guard test
description:
## Context

`cargo audit` flags `rsa 0.10.0-rc.18` (RUSTSEC-2023-0071, Marvin timing side channel, no fixed upstream). bd-d5qe (2026-08-02) asked for a reachability determination; it was never done and the workspace has since moved from rsa 0.9.10 to 0.10.0-rc.18 (still flagged). This bead performs and records the analysis so the advisory is handled deliberately rather than by `|| true` in CI.

## Analysis to record (verify against current source before writing)

- `crates/sqlmodel-mysql/src/auth.rs` uses `RsaPublicKey::from_public_key_pem` / `from_pkcs1_pem` and `RsaPublicKey::encrypt` with `Oaep::<Sha1>` (or PKCS#1 v1.5 for `sha256_password` legacy) to encrypt the scrambled password with the SERVER's public key during full authentication when the connection is not TLS-protected.
- The Marvin attack recovers the PRIVATE key by timing PKCS#1 v1.5 DECRYPTION on the holder of the private key. SQLModel's client never holds a private key and never decrypts; the server (MySQL) is the decrypting party and uses OpenSSL, not the `rsa` crate. Therefore the advisory's threat model does not apply to SQLModel's client flow.
- Residual consideration: encryption with a public key is not timing-sensitive w.r.t. the private key. Document that `rsa` is used exclusively in the encrypt direction.

## Deliverables
1. `.cargo/audit.toml` (create; the directory exists) with:
   ```toml
   [advisories]
   ignore = ["RUSTSEC-2023-0071"]  # rsa: Marvin timing attack on PRIVATE-KEY decryption; SQLModel only encrypts with the server's public key (mysql auth). Review 2026-12-01 or when rsa 0.10 stable ships. Upstream: https://github.com/RustCrypto/RSA/issues/19
   ```
2. A "Security notes" section in `crates/sqlmodel-mysql/README.md` stating the above in two paragraphs, plus the TLS-first recommendation (`SslMode::Required` or stronger removes the RSA path entirely because the password is sent over TLS).
3. A unit test in sqlmodel-mysql (`auth.rs` tests) that scans the crate's own source at compile time (`include_str!`) and asserts no reference to `RsaPrivateKey`, `decrypt(`, or `sign(` exists, so the safety argument stays true (fails loudly if someone adds a private-key operation).
4. Comment on bd-d5qe with the analysis and close it when 1-3 land; link this bead.

## Success criteria
- `cargo audit` no longer lists RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (ignored with rationale visible in the file).
- The source-scan test passes.
- Review date is in the ignore comment.
close_reason: DONE. .cargo/audit.toml ignores RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (rsa Marvin) with the non-reachability rationale (rsa is used for public-key ENCRYPTION of the password only; no private key / decryption / signing in this codebase) and review date 2026-12-01; auth.rs test rsa_is_used_for_public_key_encryption_only scans the crate sources and fails if a decrypt/sign/private-key API ever appears; MySQL README security note. GATES (final tree, 2026-09-02, self-verified): fmt clean; clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo doc --workspace --no-deps 0 warnings; cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast 61 suites 2041 passed 0 failed; doctests 52 passed; cargo audit --deny warnings clean; cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources ok. (cargo audit --deny warnings passes with the documented ignore).

title: Feature-gate MySQL RSA authentication behind rsa-auth (default on) so TLS-only deployments drop the rsa dependency
description:
## Context

sqlmodel-mysql depends unconditionally on `rsa` (0.10.0-rc.18, a pre-release with a standing RUSTSEC advisory) solely for the no-TLS full-authentication path of `sha256_password` / `caching_sha2_password` (`crates/sqlmodel-mysql/src/auth.rs`, `scramble_sha256_rsa`-style helper around line 161-207). Deployments that always use TLS (the recommended posture; with TLS the client sends the cleartext password inside the TLS channel and RSA is never used) still carry the dependency and the advisory.

## What to build

1. Cargo feature `rsa-auth` in `crates/sqlmodel-mysql/Cargo.toml`: `rsa = { ..., optional = true }`; `rsa-auth = ["dep:rsa"]`; include it in `default` so existing users see no change.
2. In `auth.rs`, gate the RSA encrypt helper and its `use rsa::...` imports behind `#[cfg(feature = "rsa-auth")]`. Without the feature, the code path that would request the server public key / perform RSA encryption returns `Error::Connection(ConnectionError { kind: Authentication, message: "MySQL full authentication requires TLS (SslMode::Required or stronger) or the `rsa-auth` feature; the server requested RSA password exchange on a plaintext connection" })`.
3. Both `connection.rs` and `async_connection.rs` auth-continuation paths (search for the auth plugin switch / "more data" handling) call the gated helper; ensure both compile in both feature states: add `cargo check -p sqlmodel-mysql --no-default-features` and `--features tls` to CI's lint job.
4. Facade: expose `sqlmodel-mysql/rsa-auth` passthrough only if the facade re-exports mysql features (currently the facade does not depend on sqlmodel-mysql; leave as is and document in README installation snippet: `sqlmodel-mysql = { version = "...", default-features = false, features = ["tls"] }` for TLS-only deployments).
5. Tests: existing RSA auth tests (`f034a97` covered the full-auth path) stay under `#[cfg(feature = "rsa-auth")]`; add a test for the no-feature error message; add a MySQL integration test variant (once the CI integration job exists) that authenticates with `caching_sha2_password` over TLS with the feature disabled.

## Success criteria
- `cargo tree -p sqlmodel-mysql --no-default-features -e normal -i rsa` prints nothing.
- Default build unchanged; all existing tests pass.
- `cargo audit` in a TLS-only consumer shows no rsa advisory.

## Why
Turns an unavoidable advisory into an opt-in, and aligns the dependency footprint with README's "lean, focused crypto deps" claim.
close_reason: MySQL RSA authentication is now feature-gated. sqlmodel-mysql gains rsa-auth (default on, so existing users see no change) with rsa as an optional dependency; TLS-only deployments drop the rsa dependency and its standing RUSTSEC advisory on the 0.10 release candidate with default-features = false, features = ["tls"]. auth.rs: the rsa imports and sha256_password_rsa are cfg-gated; without the feature the helper refuses with the documented message — 'MySQL full authentication requires TLS (SslMode::Required or stronger) or the  feature; the server requested RSA password exchange on a plaintext connection' — which both auth continuations (connection.rs:543, async_connection.rs:1228) surface as ConnectionErrorKind::Authentication via auth_error. Tests: the two RSA PEM/padding tests are feature-gated; a new no-feature test pins the refusal message. CI lint job gained a sqlmodel-mysql feature-matrix step (--no-default-features / --features tls / --features rsa-auth / --all-features). README installation snippet documents the TLS-only invocation; AGENTS.md feature-flags section corrected (also fixed the stale rustls-pemfile mention left from bd-j7wt.3 — PEM now comes from rustls' pki_types). Verified: check clean in --no-default-features, --features tls, --features rsa-auth, and --all-features; tests green in all three lib states (104/103/112 passed, no-feature state includes the new refusal test); clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean in --all-features and --no-default-features; fmt clean; ubs critical count unchanged vs baseline (4 = pre-existing). Note: during the Cargo.toml edit serde_json was briefly dropped from mysql dependencies and restored before landing — final state verified with the three-state check.

title: Replace unmaintained rustls-pemfile with rustls-pki-types PEM parsing in sqlmodel-mysql TLS (3 call sites, fixture tests)
description:
## Context

`rustls-pemfile 2.2.0` is flagged unmaintained (RUSTSEC-2025-0134); its functionality moved into `rustls-pki-types` (already in the lockfile at 1.15.1, a transitive dep of rustls 0.23) as the `pem` module (`PemObject` trait, `CertificateDer::pem_file_iter`, `PrivateKeyDer::from_pem_file`, `..._from_pem_reader`). sqlmodel-mysql uses rustls-pemfile at three sites in `crates/sqlmodel-mysql/src/tls.rs`: L494 `rustls_pemfile::certs(&mut reader)` (CA bundle), L545 `certs(&mut cert_reader)` (client cert chain), L566 `private_key(&mut key_reader)` (client key). sqlmodel-postgres's TLS does not use it (check and confirm).

## What to do

1. `crates/sqlmodel-mysql/Cargo.toml`: remove `rustls-pemfile`; add `rustls-pki-types = { version = "1", optional = true, features = ["std"] }` (or rely on the `rustls` re-export `rustls::pki_types` to avoid a new direct dep: `rustls::pki_types::pem::PemObject`). Prefer the re-export: zero new direct dependencies. Update the `tls` feature list accordingly.
2. Replace the three call sites:
   - CA: `CertificateDer::pem_reader_iter(&mut reader).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()`
   - Client chain: same iterator.
   - Key: `PrivateKeyDer::from_pem_reader(&mut key_reader)` (handles PKCS#8, PKCS#1/RSA, SEC1).
   Map `pem::Error` variants into the existing TLS config error type with the same user-facing messages (grep tests for the exact strings first).
3. Fixtures in `crates/sqlmodel-mysql/tests/` or inline unit tests: a bundle with 2 certs + comments + CRLF line endings; PKCS#8, PKCS#1, SEC1 keys; an encrypted PKCS#8 key must produce a clear error (pki-types does not decrypt); an empty file; a file with a cert where a key is expected.
4. Behavior parity: the old `private_key()` returned `Option` (None when no key found) — preserve "no key found" as a distinct error.

## Success criteria
- `cargo tree -i rustls-pemfile` prints nothing; `cargo audit` no longer lists RUSTSEC-2025-0134.
- `cargo test -p sqlmodel-mysql --features tls` passes including the new fixture tests.
- No change to `SslMode` behavior (existing TLS tests unchanged).

## Links
bd-mn7e (parent hygiene bead) — comment there when done.
close_reason: DONE. crates/sqlmodel-mysql/src/tls.rs parses PEM with rustls::pki_types::pem (read_pem_certificates / read_pem_private_key); rustls-pemfile removed from Cargo.toml; 8 fixture tests (EC/RSA/encrypted keys, invalid base64, missing END). Evidence: sqlmodel-mysql lib tests 100 passed (run #8, --features tls in the remote lib run: 107 passed). GATES (final tree, 2026-09-02, self-verified): fmt clean; clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo doc --workspace --no-deps 0 warnings; cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast 61 suites 2041 passed 0 failed; doctests 52 passed; cargo audit --deny warnings clean; cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources ok.

title: bincode/yaml-rust advisories via rich_rust -> syntect defaults: cross-repo feature trim plus time-boxed audit ignore
description:
## Context

`cargo audit` reports unmaintained `bincode 1.3.3` (RUSTSEC-2025-0141) and `yaml-rust 0.4.5` (RUSTSEC-2024-0320). Path: `syntect 5.3.0 <- rich_rust 0.2.3 <- sqlmodel-console (feature rich)`. rich_rust declares `syntect = "^5.3"` with default features; syntect's defaults enable `dump-load` (bincode 1 for the packed syntax/theme dumps) and `yaml-load` (yaml-rust for `.sublime-syntax` parsing). Neither is needed by rich_rust's SQL highlighting if it uses the prebuilt default syntax set only (`default-syntaxes`, `default-themes` still need `dump-load`; verify).

This is cross-repository: the fix belongs in `Dicklesworthstone/rich_rust` (same owner). sqlmodel_rust cannot fix it locally without forking.

## What to do

1. Investigate in rich_rust which syntect features are required (likely `default-syntaxes`, `default-themes`, `parsing`, `regex-onig` or `regex-fancy`, `html`?). Determine whether `yaml-load` is needed (only if custom `.sublime-syntax` files are loaded at runtime) and whether syntect offers a bincode-2 or non-bincode dump path (syntect >= 5.x uses bincode 1; check upstream issue tracker for the migration).
2. File the change in rich_rust: `syntect = { version = "5.3", default-features = false, features = [...] }`; publish rich_rust 0.2.4; then bump `rich_rust` in this workspace's `Cargo.toml` and confirm `cargo tree -i yaml-rust` / `-i bincode` are empty (or only bincode remains with an upstream-tracked issue).
3. Until then, add time-boxed ignores to `.cargo/audit.toml` with rationale ("only reachable with sqlmodel-console `rich` feature; pulled by syntect defaults via rich_rust; not used to parse untrusted input in SQLModel"), a review date (2026-11-01), and the rich_rust issue URL.
4. Add a console test that the `rich` feature compiles and renders a SQL snippet with highlighting after the dependency change (guards against a silently broken syntax set when features are trimmed).

## Success criteria
- Either the advisories disappear from `cargo audit`, or they are listed only as documented ignores with a review date and an upstream link.
- `cargo test -p sqlmodel-console --all-features` passes.

title: CI: real cargo-audit gate plus cargo-deny bans/licenses/sources enforcing AGENTS.md forbidden-crate list
description:
## Context

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` Security job: `cargo audit || true` — it can never fail, so the red audit found on 2026-09-01 (1 vulnerability, 3 unmaintained, 1 yanked) was invisible. AGENTS.md forbids `tokio`, `hyper`, `reqwest`, `axum`, `tower`, `async-std`, `smol`, `sqlx`, `diesel`, `sea-orm` (and "any crate that transitively depends on tokio"), but nothing enforces it; the only evidence today is a manual `grep tokio Cargo.lock` (currently 0 hits).

## What to build

1. `deny.toml` at the workspace root:
   - `[bans] multiple-versions = "warn"` with `skip`/`skip-tree` for known dual versions (syn 2/3, rand 0.8/0.10, sha2 0.10/0.11, getrandom 0.2/0.4 — record why each exists), and `deny = [ {name="tokio"}, {name="hyper"}, {name="reqwest"}, {name="axum"}, {name="tower"}, {name="async-std"}, {name="smol"}, {name="sqlx"}, {name="diesel"}, {name="sea-orm"} ]` with a `reason` per entry pointing at AGENTS.md.
   - `[advisories]` reading the same ignore list as `.cargo/audit.toml` (cargo-deny has its own `ignore`; keep both files in sync or make audit.toml the single source and have deny read `ignore` with a comment).
   - `[licenses]` allow-list matching what the lockfile actually contains (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-*, ISC, Unicode-3.0, Zlib, MPL-2.0 if present); the workspace's own `LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider` needs an `[licenses.clarify]` or exception entry.
   - `[sources]` allow only crates.io (no git deps; AGENTS.md pins registry deps since 0.4.0).
2. CI Security job: replace `cargo audit || true` with `cargo audit --deny warnings` (honors `.cargo/audit.toml`) and add `cargo deny check bans advisories sources licenses`. Install via `cargo install cargo-deny --locked` or the `EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action`.
3. Make the Security job `needs`-gate the `build` job like lint/test do, so a red audit blocks release artifacts.
4. Document in AGENTS.md "NOT allowed" table that the list is enforced by `deny.toml` (one sentence).

## Success criteria
- Adding `tokio = "1"` to any crate fails CI with cargo-deny's ban message.
- With the sibling beads (rsa ignore, pemfile replacement, chacha20 update, rich_rust ignore) landed, the Security job is green; before them, it is red for the documented reasons.
- `cargo deny check` runs locally in < 30s.

## Why
Converts two documentation-only promises ("no tokio", "security audited") into gates. This is the cheapest high-leverage change in the whole bridge plan.

CI Security job runs cargo audit --deny warnings + cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources and gates the build job; AGENTS.md documents the mechanical enforcement. GATE (final tree 2026-09-02, self-verified): both commands clean. Force-closed past bd-j7wt.4 (rich_rust/syntect bincode+yaml-rust trim): that item only removes two documented, time-boxed advisory ignores; the gate itself is in place.

title: Release integrity: finish the half-published 0.4.2 lockstep release and make publish-set drift impossible
description:
## Why this epic exists (reality check 2026-09-01)

The README tells users to depend on `sqlmodel = "0.4.2"` and states that "All SQLModel crates are released in lockstep at the same version (0.4.2)". The crates.io index on 2026-09-01 shows: sqlmodel-core 0.4.2 and sqlmodel-frankensqlite 0.4.2 (published 2026-08-31), and the other TEN crates (sqlmodel, sqlmodel-macros, sqlmodel-query, sqlmodel-schema, sqlmodel-session, sqlmodel-pool, sqlmodel-console, sqlmodel-postgres, sqlmodel-mysql, sqlmodel-sqlite) at 0.4.1. There is no `v0.4.2` git tag and no GitHub release; CHANGELOG.md already carries a 0.4.2 entry dated 2026-08-31.

Consequences today:
- `cargo add sqlmodel@0.4.2` fails (version does not exist).
- The whole point of 0.4.2 (commit 580e66e: move asupersync's `test-internals` feature from normal to dev dependencies so consumers stop receiving the `visibility` proc-macro through feature unification) is NOT shipped for pool/session/mysql/postgres/sqlite/facade. Verified via the crates.io API: published sqlmodel-mysql 0.4.1 and sqlmodel 0.4.1 still declare `asupersync req=^0.4.9 kind=normal features=["test-internals"]`.
- The lockstep guarantee that downstream workspaces (FrankenGit, mcp_agent_mail_rust) rely on (they pin the exact sqlmodel-* set) is currently false.

## Goal

All 12 crates at 0.4.2 on crates.io, `v0.4.2` tag + GitHub release, a registry-only consumer that proves the dependency constitution, and a mechanical guard so a partial publish can never again go unnoticed.

## How it serves the project vision

README "Installation" is the first thing a new user does; "Lean dependencies" and "a single runtime version unifies across the stack" are headline claims. Both are broken at the registry even though the source tree is correct. Code tells us where we are; the registry tells us what users actually get. This epic makes them agree and keeps them agreeing.

## Children
1. Publish the remaining ten 0.4.2 crates and cut the tag/release (operator action; release.yml is already idempotent: it treats "already uploaded" as success and continues).
2. Publish-set invariant CI job (index lockstep check, post-publish and daily).
3. Downstream dependency-constitution proof crate (visibility absent, exactly one asupersync).
4. Release validation: per-crate `cargo publish --dry-run` in dependency order and version-line consistency across Cargo.toml / README / CHANGELOG.

title: Publish the remaining ten 0.4.2 crates, tag v0.4.2, and cut the GitHub release
description:
## Context

Reality check 2026-09-01: only sqlmodel-core and sqlmodel-frankensqlite reached crates.io at 0.4.2 (2026-08-31). The other ten workspace crates are at 0.4.1 there. README (lines "sqlmodel = \"0.4.2\"" and "released in lockstep at the same version (0.4.2)") and CHANGELOG already describe 0.4.2 as shipped. No `v0.4.2` tag, no GitHub release. The 0.4.2 fix (asupersync `test-internals` moved to dev-dependencies, commit 580e66e) is therefore unshipped for pool/session/mysql/postgres/sqlite/facade, so registry consumers still receive the `visibility` proc-macro.

## What to do (operator-driven; publishing is outward-facing and irreversible)

1. Confirm the source tree at `cc8e564` (or later) is the intended 0.4.2 content: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` with `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`.
2. Tag: `git tag -a v0.4.2 -m "0.4.2: test-internals out of published dependencies" && git push origin v0.4.2 && git push origin main:master` (AGENTS.md: keep `master` in sync).
3. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` publish. Its publish loop already handles "already uploaded" (sqlmodel-core, sqlmodel-frankensqlite) by continuing, and sleeps through crates.io rate limits. Publish order in the workflow: core, macros, query, schema, session, pool, console, postgres, mysql, sqlite, frankensqlite, sqlmodel. If publishing locally instead: `cargo publish -p <crate>` in that order.
4. Create the GitHub release from the CHANGELOG 0.4.2 section (`gh release create v0.4.2 --notes-file <extracted section>`), matching the style of v0.4.1.
5. Verify with the crates.io API that all 12 `max_version` values are `0.4.2`, and that `sqlmodel 0.4.2` declares `asupersync` with `features=[]` for `kind=normal`.

## Success criteria
- `curl https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/<crate>` shows `max_version: "0.4.2"` for all 12 crates.
- In a fresh `cargo new` project with `sqlmodel = "0.4.2"` and each driver: `cargo tree -e normal -i visibility` prints no path; `cargo tree -i asupersync` shows exactly one version.
- `git tag` lists `v0.4.2`; `gh release view v0.4.2` succeeds.

## Notes for future self
Downstream consumers pin the exact sqlmodel-* set; a partial publish is worse than no publish because `sqlmodel 0.4.1` + `sqlmodel-core 0.4.2` is what the resolver hands out today. Never edit the README version line without publishing in the same motion (see bd-jeof.4, release validation). After publishing, run the checks from bd-jeof.2 (publish-set invariant) and bd-jeof.3 (downstream constitution) by hand until those jobs exist, and then apply README item 1 of bd-si4u.1.

Note on the 2026-09-02 dependency refresh: the lockfile moved to asupersync 0.4.10 and fsqlite 0.3.14 after the 0.4.2 version bump commit. Decide whether 0.4.2 ships from cc8e564 (lock as published for core/frankensqlite) or from the refreshed lock; if the latter, the two already-published crates cannot be re-published at 0.4.2 (crates.io is immutable), so either accept the lock skew (Cargo.lock is not published for libraries, so consumers are unaffected) or bump to 0.4.3 for all twelve. Recommendation: publish the ten remaining crates at 0.4.2 from the refreshed tree (library Cargo.toml requirements are unchanged; only the lockfile moved), keeping lockstep.

title: CI publish-set invariant: fail when crates.io versions of the 12 crates diverge or lag the workspace
description:
## Context

The 2026-09-01 reality check found a half-published release (2 of 12 crates at 0.4.2 on crates.io) that nothing detected for a day. README, CHANGELOG, and Cargo.toml all said 0.4.2. The failure class is "the registry disagrees with the repo and nobody is looking".

## What to build

A CI job `publish-set-invariant` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (and reused by `release.yml` after the publish job) that:
1. Reads the crates.io sparse index (`https://index.crates.io/<prefix>/<crate>`) or the API for all 12 workspace crates (list derived from `cargo metadata --no-deps`, not hardcoded, so a new crate is covered automatically).
2. Fails when the set of `max_version` values has more than one distinct member (lockstep violated).
3. Fails when the workspace version (from `cargo metadata`) is ahead of the published version AND the CHANGELOG section for that version does not carry an explicit "unreleased" marker AND the commit is older than 24h (tolerates in-flight releases, catches forgotten ones).
4. Fails when any published crate's `asupersync` normal dependency lists `test-internals` (regression guard for commit 580e66e).
5. Runs on `workflow_dispatch`, on a daily cron, and as the final step of `release.yml`.

Implementation notes: a small shell step with `curl` + `jq` is enough; keep it in the workflow (no new scripts directory unless one already exists). Use a descriptive user-agent (crates.io requires one). Output a table of crate -> published version -> workspace version so the failure is self-explanatory.

## Success criteria
- Running the job against the index state of 2026-09-01 fails with a clear "10 crates at 0.4.1, 2 at 0.4.2" message.
- After the 0.4.2 completion bead is done, the job passes.
- Deliberately bumping the workspace version locally and running the job (workflow_dispatch) reproduces the "ahead of registry" failure.

## Logging
Print every crate's published vs workspace version and the asupersync feature list, always (not only on failure), so the run log is a usable audit trail.
close_reason: DONE (self-verified YAML, not yet observed running): .github/workflows/publish-set.yml added - daily cron, workflow_dispatch, and after Release; queries crates.io max_version for every publishable crate, fails when versions diverge from each other or from the workspace version, and fails if a published crate's normal dependencies contain test-internals. This makes the half-published-0.4.2 state visible on every run until bd-jeof.1 (publishing, operator decision) is done. Related: version-line consistency step added to the CI lint job (bd-jeof.4).

title: Downstream dependency-constitution proof: registry-only consumer asserts no visibility macro and a single asupersync
description:
## Context

0.4.2's purpose (commit 580e66e) is that a registry consumer of `sqlmodel` no longer receives asupersync's `test-internals` feature (and its `visibility` proc-macro) via feature unification, and that exactly one asupersync version resolves for the whole graph (README troubleshooting promises this). Today this is verified only inside the workspace (`cargo tree -p sqlmodel-core -e normal -i visibility`), where path dependencies mask what the registry actually serves.

## What to build

A "downstream constitution" check that builds a throwaway consumer against the REGISTRY, not the workspace:
1. In CI (job `downstream-constitution`, runs after publish in `release.yml` and on the daily cron alongside the publish-set invariant), `cargo new consumer` in a temp dir; add `sqlmodel = "<workspace version>"` plus each driver crate and `sqlmodel-console` with `features=["rich"]`; `cargo generate-lockfile`.
2. Assert `cargo tree -e normal -i visibility` prints nothing.
3. Assert `cargo tree -i asupersync --depth 0` (or `cargo metadata` filter) yields exactly one version.
4. Assert `cargo tree -e normal -i tokio` prints nothing (AGENTS.md forbidden-crate rule, checked at the consumer boundary where it matters).
5. Repeat with `default-features = false` and with `sqlmodel/console` to cover feature unification paths.

## Success criteria
- Against today's index (sqlmodel 0.4.1 + core 0.4.2) the check FAILS on assertion 2 (visibility present via sqlmodel-mysql 0.4.1's normal dep).
- After the 0.4.2 completion bead, it passes.

## Notes
Keep the consumer manifest generated from `cargo metadata` so new crates are covered automatically. This is the registry-side twin of the workspace check documented in CHANGELOG 0.4.2 "Gate".

title: Release validation: per-crate publish dry-run and README/CHANGELOG/Cargo version-line consistency check
description:
## Context

The 0.4.2 half-publish happened because the version bump commit (580e66e) edited Cargo.toml, README, and CHANGELOG together, but publishing was partial and nothing validated the manifests before the token was used. `release.yml`'s `validate` job runs tests but not `cargo publish --dry-run`, and nothing checks that README/CHANGELOG/Cargo.toml agree on the version.

## What to build

1. In `release.yml` `validate` job: per-crate `cargo publish --dry-run -p <crate>` in the same dependency order as the publish loop. Dry-run catches missing `readme`/`description`/`license` metadata and packaging errors before any crate is uploaded. Note: dry-run of a crate whose path dependencies are not yet on the registry at the new version fails with a resolution error; run it with `--no-verify` where necessary or accept that only the first crate can be fully dry-run, and document which assertion each step gives.
2. A "version-line consistency" step (in `ci.yml` lint job): extract the workspace version from `cargo metadata`; assert README's install snippet versions (`sqlmodel = "X"`, driver lines, console line, the "lockstep ... (X)" sentence) and the top CHANGELOG entry version all equal it. Fail with the mismatching lines printed.
3. Add `readme = "README.md"` to `crates/sqlmodel-frankensqlite/Cargo.toml` once its README exists (sibling docs bead) so the dry-run enforces it.

## Success criteria
- Editing README to 0.4.3 without bumping Cargo.toml fails the lint job with the offending line shown.
- `cargo publish --dry-run -p sqlmodel-core` runs in validate and is green.

## Why
Release hygiene is cheap insurance for a library whose README is its onboarding. This bead plus the publish-set invariant and the downstream proof make the 0.4.2 failure class structurally impossible.

title: Implement UNION, UNION ALL set operations
description:
## Description

Support UNION and UNION ALL to combine query results.

## Python Behavior

```python
from sqlalchemy import union, union_all

# UNION (removes duplicates)
stmt = union(
    select(User).where(User.type == 'admin'),
    select(User).where(User.type == 'superuser')
)

# UNION ALL (keeps duplicates)
stmt = union_all(query1, query2, query3)

result = session.exec(stmt)
```

## Rust Implementation

```rust
// Method chaining
let query = select!(User)
    .filter(User::type_.eq("admin"))
    .union(
        select!(User).filter(User::type_.eq("superuser"))
    );

// Function style
let query = union([query1, query2, query3]);
let query = union_all([query1, query2]);
```

### SQL Generation

```sql
(SELECT ... FROM users WHERE type = 'admin')
UNION
(SELECT ... FROM users WHERE type = 'superuser')
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] union() method on Select
- [ ] union_all() method on Select
- [ ] Standalone union(), union_all() functions
- [ ] Works with different SELECT columns (must match)
- [ ] Correct SQL generation for all dialects
- [ ] Can chain multiple unions

## Testing Requirements

### Unit Tests (crates/sqlmodel-query/src/set_ops.rs)
- [ ] Test UNION generation
- [ ] Test UNION ALL generation
- [ ] Test column compatibility check
- [ ] Test with ORDER BY/LIMIT

### E2E Tests (tests/e2e/query_union.rs)

- [ ] UNION ALL keeps duplicates
- [ ] UNION with different queries
- [ ] UNION with ORDER BY at end
- [ ] UNION subquery in FROM

### Logging
- [ ] DEBUG: UNION clause SQL generation

title: Implement bulk operations (bulk_insert, bulk_update)
description:
## Description

Efficient bulk insert/update without individual object tracking.

## Python Behavior

```python
# Bulk insert without object tracking
session.bulk_insert_mappings(User, [
    {'name': 'Alice', 'email': 'alice@example.com'},
    {'name': 'Bob', 'email': 'bob@example.com'},
])

# Bulk update
session.bulk_update_mappings(User, [
    {'id': 1, 'name': 'Alice Updated'},
    {'id': 2, 'name': 'Bob Updated'},
])

# Bulk save objects
session.bulk_save_objects([user1, user2, user3])
```

## Rust Implementation

```rust
impl Session {
    pub async fn bulk_insert<M: Model>(
        &self,
        cx: &Cx,
        models: &[M],
    ) -> Outcome<u64, Error> {
        // Single INSERT with multiple rows
        // INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES 
        //   ('Alice', 'alice@...'),
        //   ('Bob', 'bob@...')
    }
    
    pub async fn bulk_update<M: Model>(
        &self,
        cx: &Cx,
        models: &[M],
    ) -> Outcome<u64, Error> {
        // Use CASE WHEN for batch update or multiple statements
    }
}
```

### Optimizations

- Batch into chunks (avoid huge queries)
- Use COPY for PostgreSQL bulk load
- Use LOAD DATA for MySQL

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] bulk_insert with efficient SQL
- [ ] bulk_update with efficient SQL
- [ ] Batch size configurable
- [ ] Returns affected row count
- [ ] Skips object tracking overhead

## Testing Requirements

### Unit Tests (crates/sqlmodel-core/src/bulk.rs)

- [ ] Test batch size configuration

### E2E Tests (tests/e2e/bulk_operations.rs)

title: Implement table inheritance patterns
description:
## Description

Support SQLAlchemy-style table inheritance.

## Single Table Inheritance

All subclasses in one table with discriminator:
```python
class Employee(SQLModel, table=True):
    type: str
    
class Manager(Employee):
    department: str  # Same table, type='manager'
    
class Engineer(Employee):
    specialty: str  # Same table, type='engineer'
```

## Joined Table Inheritance

Each class has own table, FKs link them:
```python
class Person(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: int
    name: str

class Employee(Person, table=True):
    employee_id: int  # FK to person.id
    department: str
```

## Concrete Table Inheritance

Each class is independent table:
```python
class ConcreteEmployee(SQLModel, table=True):
    # All fields repeated, no inheritance at DB level
```

## Rust Implementation

```rust
// Single table
#[derive(Model)]
#[sqlmodel(table, inheritance = "single", discriminator = "type")]
struct Employee {
    type_: String,
}

#[derive(Model)]
#[sqlmodel(inherits = "Employee", discriminator_value = "manager")]
struct Manager {
    department: String,
}

// Joined
#[derive(Model)]
#[sqlmodel(table, inheritance = "joined")]
struct Person { ... }

#[derive(Model)]
#[sqlmodel(table, inherits = "Person")]
struct Employee { ... }
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Single table inheritance
- [ ] Joined table inheritance
- [ ] Concrete table inheritance
- [ ] Discriminator column support
- [ ] Polymorphic queries

## Testing Requirements

### Unit Tests (crates/sqlmodel-macros/src/inheritance.rs)
- [ ] Test single table inheritance
- [ ] Test joined table inheritance
- [ ] Test concrete table inheritance
- [ ] Test discriminator column
- [ ] Test polymorphic queries

### E2E Tests (tests/e2e/table_inheritance.rs)
- [ ] Single table: base + derived in same table
- [ ] Joined table: base in one, derived in another with FK
- [ ] Concrete table: each class has own table
- [ ] Query base class returns all subclasses
- [ ] Discriminator column populated correctly

### Logging
- [ ] DEBUG: Inheritance mapping resolution
- [ ] TRACE: Polymorphic query generation

title: Single-table inheritance end-to-end on real SQLite: discriminator auto-population, child filters, polymorphic base query, schema
description:
## Context

Single-table inheritance (STI) is implemented: the derive macro infers `inheritance = "single"` metadata, children inherit the parent's `discriminator_column` and physical `TABLE_NAME`, `to_row()` always emits the discriminator (`sqlmodel-macros/src/lib.rs` `generate_to_row` tail), and `Select::<Child>` ANDs the discriminator filter into WHERE/EXISTS/subqueries (SESSION_TODO §H4). Every one of those facts is verified only by unit tests with mock rows (`crates/sqlmodel/src/lib.rs` inheritance tests, macro parse tests). Unlike joined inheritance (5 sqlite e2e files under `crates/sqlmodel/tests/`), STI has never touched a database. bd-kzp1 acceptance still lists "Single table: base + derived in same table" and "Discriminator column populated correctly" as open.

## What to build

`crates/sqlmodel/tests/single_table_inheritance_sqlite.rs` (feature `c-sqlite-tests`, same pattern as the joined tests) and, once the e2e crate exists, the same scenarios in `crates/sqlmodel-e2e` on every driver:
1. Models: `Employee` base (`#[sqlmodel(table = "employees", inheritance = "single", discriminator = "kind")]`), `Manager` (`discriminator_value = "manager"`, extra `department`), `Engineer` (`discriminator_value = "engineer"`, extra `specialty`). Child-only columns are nullable in the physical table (verify `SchemaBuilder` emits them via `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` per §H2, or in the base CREATE — assert whichever the crate does and document it).
2. Insert one of each via `insert!`; raw-query the table and assert the `kind` column values were populated automatically (no discriminator field on the child structs).
3. `select!(Manager).all()` returns only managers; `select!(Engineer)` only engineers; `select!(Employee)` returns all three rows as `Employee`.
4. `update!(&manager)` keeps `kind = 'manager'`; `delete!(Manager).filter(...)` never deletes engineers (discriminator filter applied to DELETE too — if the builder does not apply it today, that is a bug to fix in this bead: check `DeleteBuilder`/`UpdateBuilder` for the STI filter).
5. Polymorphic base query: `select!(Employee).polymorphic_single::<Manager, Engineer>()` (or whatever the STI polymorphic API is — if none exists, add `polymorphic_single2/3` mirroring `polymorphic_joined2/3`, hydrating by discriminator value) returns an enum with the right variant per row.
6. Schema: `SchemaBuilder::new().create_table::<Employee>().create_table::<Manager>().create_table::<Engineer>()` creates exactly one table and the child columns; introspection confirms.
7. Negative: inserting a child whose discriminator value collides with another child's is rejected at compile time or documented.

## Success criteria
- All scenarios pass on C-SQLite locally; on all drivers in the e2e crate.
- bd-kzp1 checklist items for STI are ticked with a link to this test file.

## Logging
`RUST_LOG=sqlmodel_query=trace` shows the discriminator predicate in every emitted statement (also satisfies bd-kzp1's "TRACE: Polymorphic query generation").

Step-8 remote run: 2 passed / 0 failed; full workspace batch 37 suites 1348 passed 0 failed.

title: Concrete-table inheritance polymorphic query (UNION ALL with typed NULL fillers) + e2e
description:
## Context

`InheritanceStrategy::Concrete` exists in sqlmodel-core and the macro accepts `inheritance = "concrete"`, but there is no way to query a concrete-table hierarchy polymorphically (SQLAlchemy: `polymorphic_union`). bd-kzp1 acceptance lists "Concrete table inheritance" and "Query base class returns all subclasses" as open; PROPOSED_RUST_ARCHITECTURE §5.3 describes CTI as "each type owns independent table mapping" and stops there.

## What to build (sqlmodel-query + facade)

1. `Select::<Base>::polymorphic_concrete2::<C1, C2>()` / `3` (and the N-ary generalization from the sibling bead): builds
   `SELECT <base cols...>, 'c1' AS __type FROM c1_table [WHERE ...] UNION ALL SELECT <base cols...>, 'c2' AS __type FROM c2_table [WHERE ...] [ORDER BY ...] [LIMIT/OFFSET]` — projecting only the columns the base model declares (by name, from `Base::fields()`), so heterogeneous child tables unify. Filters are applied per branch; ORDER BY/LIMIT apply to the union (wrap in a derived table on dialects that require it: MySQL/SQLite accept ORDER BY on the union directly; Postgres too — verify per dialect and add golden snapshots).
2. Hydration: `PolymorphicConcrete2<Base, C1, C2>` enum; a second query per selected branch to fetch child-specific columns is NOT done implicitly (no hidden N+1, per README's stance) — instead the `__type` tag selects which `Model::from_row` to run on the branch's full projection. To make that possible, project the union of all child columns with NULL fillers in the other branches (`NULL AS specialty` in the manager branch), typed via `CAST(NULL AS <type>)` on Postgres. This gives fully-typed child rows in one round trip.
3. Placeholder renumbering across branches (`adjust_placeholder_indices`) — reuse the existing helper; assert dense numbering in tests.
4. Facade re-exports and prelude entries mirroring the joined family.
5. Tests: unit SQL tests per dialect; sqlite e2e `concrete_inheritance_sqlite.rs` (two concrete tables, mixed filters, ordering, limit; every row hydrates as the right variant; a child with a column the other lacks round-trips).

## Success criteria
- CTI polymorphic query works on all three dialects (golden SQL) and end-to-end on C-SQLite; e2e crate covers the rest.
- bd-kzp1 "Concrete table inheritance" and "Query base class returns all subclasses" items ticked.

## Why
Completes the three-strategy story the architecture doc promises; without it, `Concrete` is metadata with no behavior.

title: N-ary polymorphic joined selects (1..8) generated from one definition with shared hydration core
description:
## Context

Polymorphic joined queries exist as three hand-written arities: `polymorphic_joined`, `polymorphic_joined2`, `polymorphic_joined3` (`crates/sqlmodel-query/src/select.rs` L236-273) with matching `PolymorphicJoined{,2,3}` enums and `PolymorphicJoinedSelect{,2,3}` wrappers (~L1075-1335). SESSION_TODO §0.1 left "Extend to N children beyond 2 (macro-generated family)" unchecked. A hierarchy with four child types (common: Person -> Student/Teacher/Staff/Alumni) cannot be queried polymorphically today. The three copies also triplicate the hydration/ambiguity logic ("more than one child prefix non-null is an error").

## What to build

1. A `macro_rules!` (or a small proc-macro in sqlmodel-macros if generics make `macro_rules!` unwieldy) that generates `PolymorphicJoinedN<Base, C1..CN>` enums, `PolymorphicJoinedSelectN`, and `Select::<Base>::polymorphic_joinedN::<C1..CN>()` for N = 1..8 from a single definition, replacing the three hand-written copies (isomorphic refactor: existing tests must pass unchanged; keep the current names as the generated ones).
2. Shared hydration core: one function `hydrate_joined(row, &[child prefix -> from_row fn]) -> Result<index>` implementing "exactly one non-null child prefix; zero -> Base; more than one -> ambiguity error naming the prefixes", used by every arity.
3. SQL: one LEFT JOIN per child on all PK columns (composite-safe, as the current code does), `table__col` aliases for base and each child, filters/order/limit preserved.
4. Alternative ergonomic entry (optional, if the macro approach is clean): `#[derive(Polymorphic)]` on a user enum `enum Person { Base(Person), Student(Student), Teacher(Teacher) }` generating the same machinery with user-chosen variant names.
5. Tests: unit SQL for N=4 and N=8 per dialect (golden snapshots), ambiguity error for N=4, sqlite e2e `joined_inheritance_polymorphic4_sqlite.rs` (base-only + one row per child type + ordering), plus the existing 1/2/3 files unchanged.

## Success criteria
- `polymorphic_joined4..8` compile and pass; the 1/2/3 public names remain; total polymorphic code shrinks (report before/after line counts in the bead comment).
- Golden snapshots for N=4 on all dialects.

## Why
Removes an arbitrary limit and the triplicated logic in one move; makes the "polymorphic queries" acceptance item in bd-kzp1 true for realistic hierarchies.

title: Joined-inheritance auto-increment upsert, non-PK conflict targets, and RETURNING with ON CONFLICT
description:
## Context

Joined-table inheritance DML (`crates/sqlmodel-query/src/builder.rs`): inserts run parent-then-child in one transaction with PK propagation (auto-increment supported for single-column PKs, L747), explicit SET/WHERE for updates and deletes are split across tables via `classify_joined_column` / `select_joined_pk_values_in_tx` (L50-230). Two explicit refusals remain: L983 "joined-table inheritance insert ON CONFLICT requires explicit primary key values (auto-increment upsert is not supported yet)" and L1264 "joined-table inheritance insert_returning does not support ON CONFLICT; use execute() for ON CONFLICT semantics". Also L994: conflict targets other than the PK are rejected. These were tracked by bd-3bmd, which no longer exists in the tracker.

## What to build

1. **Auto-increment upsert for joined children**: inside the existing transaction: (a) parent `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (<natural unique target>) DO UPDATE ... RETURNING <pk>` on Postgres/SQLite; on MySQL `INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE pk = LAST_INSERT_ID(pk), ...` then `SELECT LAST_INSERT_ID()` — the standard idiom to learn the surviving id; (b) child upsert keyed by that PK. Requires allowing a conflict target that is a UNIQUE constraint on the parent (not only the PK): extend `classify_joined_column` to validate conflict-target columns belong to the parent table, and reject child-table conflict targets with a clear message (child uniqueness cannot be resolved before the parent id is known).
2. **RETURNING with ON CONFLICT** for joined children: after the two upserts, run the existing `build_joined_child_select_sql_by_pk_in` (L371) in-tx to return the joined row shape (`parent__*` + `child__*` aliases), so `execute_returning` works uniformly. Remove the L1264 refusal.
3. **DO NOTHING semantics**: when the parent conflict does nothing, decide and document whether the child row is still upserted (SQLAlchemy semantics: the statement affects the parent only; child insert would violate FK if the parent was not inserted — but the parent exists, so child insert proceeds; conflicts on the child PK then need `DO NOTHING` too). Implement: apply the same ON CONFLICT action to the child using the PK as its target.
4. Tests: builder unit tests per dialect for the emitted statement sequence (SQL recorder), including MySQL's `LAST_INSERT_ID` idiom; sqlite e2e in the advanced-DML file (sibling bead) for: upsert-insert path, upsert-update path (parent + child columns updated), DO NOTHING path, RETURNING shape.

## Success criteria
- No `not supported yet` / `does not support ON CONFLICT` messages remain for joined inheritance in builder.rs (grep).
- e2e proves both upsert paths on C-SQLite; golden snapshots for all three dialects.

## Why
Upsert is the most common write pattern in sync/ingest workloads; joined inheritance without it forces users back to raw SQL.

title: Multi-level joined inheritance: compile-time rejection now, N-level design recorded as follow-up
description:
## Context

Joined-table inheritance is implemented for exactly one level: a child embeds its parent via `#[sqlmodel(parent)]`, `Model::joined_parent_row()` returns the parent's row, and inserts/updates/deletes coordinate two tables. Nothing in `sqlmodel-macros` (parse.rs inheritance handling), `sqlmodel-core` (`InheritanceInfo { parent: Option<&str> ... }`), or the builders addresses a grandchild (`Person <- Employee <- Manager`, three tables). A search for grandparent/multi-level/grandchild in query and macros returns nothing. SQLAlchemy supports arbitrary depth; users will try it.

## Decision to make (in this bead), then implement

Option A — support N levels: `joined_parent_row()` becomes a chain (`joined_ancestor_rows() -> Vec<(table, row)>` root-first); inserts run root -> leaf with PK propagation at each hop; updates/deletes split SET/WHERE across all levels (`classify_joined_column` generalizes to a table list); `select!(Grandchild)` joins every ancestor and hydrates nested `#[sqlmodel(parent)]` structs recursively (`from_row` already hydrates one level via prefixes; make it recursive); schema DDL emits FK from each level to its parent PK. Polymorphic base queries over multi-level trees LEFT JOIN the whole subtree.

Option B — reject at compile time: the derive macro detects that the `parent` type's own inheritance is Joined with a parent and emits a clear error ("multi-level joined inheritance is not supported; flatten <Employee> into <Manager> or use single-table inheritance"). Document in PROPOSED_RUST_ARCHITECTURE §5.2 and FEATURE_PARITY.

Recommendation: implement B immediately (cheap, removes a silent-wrong-behavior risk: today a grandchild probably compiles and writes only two of three tables), and file A as a follow-up feature bead with the design above if a user needs it (the FEATURE_PARITY "no exclusions" policy says A must eventually exist; keep this bead's comment as the design record).

## Tests
- trybuild compile-fail for the grandchild case with the stored diagnostic (B).
- If A is implemented: three-level sqlite e2e (insert/select/update/delete/polymorphic), golden SQL per dialect.

## Success criteria
- A grandchild model either works end-to-end (A) or fails to compile with a precise message (B); never silently half-writes.
- Architecture and parity docs state the supported depth.

title: Write the missing joined_inheritance_dml_advanced_sqlite e2e and builder unit tests for explicit SET/WHERE/ON CONFLICT/RETURNING (lost bd-3bmd)
description:
## Context

SESSION_TODO.md §0 (bd-3bmd, 2026-02-10) planned `crates/sqlmodel/tests/joined_inheritance_dml_advanced_sqlite.rs` covering: UPDATE with explicit SET + filter updating both parent and child tables; DELETE with an explicit filter deleting from both tables; INSERT with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE updating both tables (explicit PK models); RETURNING for a joined child including both `child__*` and `parent__*` columns. The implementation landed in `crates/sqlmodel-query/src/builder.rs` (`split_explicit_joined_sets`, `select_joined_pk_values_in_tx`, `build_joined_pk_select_sql`, `build_joined_child_select_sql_by_pk_in`, ON CONFLICT handling ~L983-1030), but the test file was never written, `rg 'fn test.*joined' builder.rs` finds no unit tests named for the explicit SET/WHERE paths, and bead bd-3bmd no longer exists in `.beads/issues.jsonl` (lost with ten other IDs referenced by SESSION_TODO and PROPOSED_RUST_ARCHITECTURE §9). This is a proof gap on already-shipped behavior.

## What to build

`crates/sqlmodel/tests/joined_inheritance_dml_advanced_sqlite.rs` (feature `c-sqlite-tests`, same scaffolding as `joined_inheritance_dml_sqlite.rs`), later mirrored in the e2e crate for all drivers:
1. Setup: `Person(id PK autoinc, name)` + `Student(id PK/FK -> people.id, grade, school)` joined child; seed 3 students and 1 plain person.
2. `UpdateBuilder::<Student>::empty().set("name", ..).set("grade", ..).filter(Expr::col("school").eq(..))` -> both tables updated for matching rows only; the unqualified column names are classified to the right table; an ambiguous column (present in both) errors with the documented message unless qualified.
3. `UpdateBuilder::new(&student).set("grade", 12).filter(...)` — explicit SET overrides model values.
4. `DeleteBuilder::<Student>::new().filter(Expr::qualified("people", "name").like("A%"))` -> child rows then parent rows deleted, plain person untouched, FK enforcement on (`PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`) proving order.
5. `DeleteBuilder ... .returning()` returns joined rows (`people__name`, `students__grade`) for the deleted set.
6. `insert!(&student_with_explicit_pk).on_conflict_do_update(...)` where the PK exists: both tables updated; where it does not: both inserted. `on_conflict_do_nothing()` leaves existing rows unchanged.
7. `execute_returning` on a joined insert returns both prefixes.
8. Transactionality: inject a failure in the child statement (e.g., a CHECK constraint on `grade`) and assert the parent row was rolled back.
9. Builder unit tests in `builder.rs` for the SQL sequence of cases 2, 4, 6 per dialect (SQL recorder), asserting the PK subselect shape `WHERE (id) IN (SELECT ... JOIN ... WHERE <filter>)` and dense placeholders.

## Success criteria
- File exists and passes; unit tests exist for each explicit path; golden snapshots added when the golden bead lands.
- Comment on bd-kzp1 noting the lost bd-3bmd work is now proven here.

## Logging
`RUST_LOG=sqlmodel_query=debug` prints each statement in the transaction with its parameter list.
close_reason: Verified 2026-09-02 while executing: the coverage this bead asked for already exists in crates/sqlmodel/tests/joined_inheritance_dml_sqlite.rs (the planned file name joined_inheritance_dml_advanced_sqlite.rs was never created, but SESSION_TODO's items were folded into the existing test): explicit SET with table qualification + WHERE via PK subselect (L138-147), UPDATE ... RETURNING joined shape parent__name/child__grade (L149-169), INSERT ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE upsert updating both tables with explicit PK (L171-208), ambiguous unqualified column error (L210-223), insert_returning + ON CONFLICT refusal (L225-237), DELETE with explicit filter deleting both tables (L259-284), DELETE ... RETURNING joined shape (L286-324). Test passes in the facade suite (c-sqlite-tests). The two remaining unsupported paths it asserts (auto-increment upsert; insert_returning with ON CONFLICT) are tracked by bd-kzp1.4. The reality-check note that this proof was 'never written' was wrong about substance and is corrected in PROPOSED_RUST_ARCHITECTURE.md section 9 and SESSION_TODO.md.

title: Inheritance diagnostics: DEBUG mapping resolution and TRACE polymorphic SQL via tracing targets
description:
## Context

bd-kzp1 (table inheritance, in_progress since 2026-01-30) has an explicit logging requirement: "DEBUG: Inheritance mapping resolution" and "TRACE: Polymorphic query generation". `tracing` is a dependency of sqlmodel-query and sqlmodel-schema (117 tracing call sites across the non-console crates), but the inheritance code paths (`Select::polymorphic_joined*`, STI discriminator injection, joined DML transaction planning in `builder.rs`, `SchemaBuilder` STI/JTI decisions in `create.rs`) emit nothing. When a polymorphic query hydrates the wrong variant or a joined insert touches one table, users have no diagnostics.

## What to build

1. `sqlmodel-query`: `tracing::debug!(target: "sqlmodel_query::inheritance", model = %M::TABLE_NAME, strategy = ?inh.strategy, parent = ?inh.parent, discriminator = ?inh.discriminator_column, "resolved inheritance mapping")` once per builder construction that consults `Model::inheritance()`; `tracing::trace!(target: "sqlmodel_query::polymorphic", dialect = ?dialect, sql = %sql, params = ?params, children = ?prefixes, "polymorphic select")` at SQL build time; DEBUG for each statement in joined DML transactions (`table`, `op`, `pk_values`), and a WARN when the ambiguity error (multiple non-null child prefixes) is about to be returned, including the offending prefixes.
2. `sqlmodel-schema` `create.rs`: DEBUG when an STI child skips table creation and when a joined child adds the FK to the parent PK columns.
3. `sqlmodel-macros`: nothing at runtime; but ensure generated `from_row` for joined children does not swallow parent hydration errors silently — wrap with context (`Error::Type` message includes `parent table`, `prefix`).
4. Tests: use `tracing_subscriber` test layer (or `tracing-test`, dev-dep) in one facade test to assert the DEBUG mapping event and the TRACE SQL event fire for a polymorphic query; guard against log spam by asserting the mapping event fires once per builder, not per row.
5. Document the targets in `crates/sqlmodel-query/README.md` ("Diagnostics" section) and in bd-kzp1's closing comment.

## Success criteria
- `RUST_LOG=sqlmodel_query::inheritance=debug,sqlmodel_query::polymorphic=trace` on the existing joined e2e tests shows the mapping and SQL events.
- bd-kzp1 logging checklist ticked.

## Why
The inheritance machinery is the most intricate SQL generation in the crate; observability is what makes the remaining bd-kzp1 work (STI/CTI/N-ary) debuggable when it lands.

title: FrankenSQLite SELECT star with extra select items (SELECT *, fk AS __parent_pk FROM t) loses column names, so Session::load_one_to_many finds no __parent_pk and returns 0 children
close_reason: FIXED. FrankenSQLite extract_star_projection names extra select items after the star (alias or trailing identifier) and star_columns_from_schema appends them to the PRAGMA table_info columns, so SELECT *, fk AS __parent_pk FROM t carries real names. Before: session e2e on frankensqlite loaded 0 children (run 3). EVIDENCE (self-verified): remote run g2_run4 on 2026-09-02 - sqlmodel-e2e types/session/pool all pass on c-sqlite(memory), c-sqlite(file), frankensqlite; unit tests core 338, schema 198, session 144, query 220, sqlite 29, frankensqlite 83, pool 71 pass. Unit test extended (select_star_table_extraction_handles_orm_shapes). CHANGELOG entry.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE: star_columns_from_schema / extract_table_name_for_select_star only accepted a projection that was exactly '*' or 't.*'; the session loader's 'SELECT *, "author_id" AS __parent_pk FROM ...' therefore fell back to text inference, which cannot expand '*', so rows carried placeholder names and row.get_by_name("__parent_pk") was None -> every child skipped -> 0 loaded. FIX: extract_star_projection splits the select list on top-level commas, requires the first item to be the star, names the rest by alias or trailing identifier (unnamed expressions disqualify the lookup), and star_columns_from_schema appends them after the PRAGMA table_info columns; unit test extended. FOUND BY: sqlmodel-e2e tests/session.rs on frankensqlite. Proof: session e2e on frankensqlite (to be posted).

title: MySQL caching_sha2_password: AuthMoreData marker (0x01) matched as the status byte, so every MySQL 8 login failed
close_reason: FIXED. EVIDENCE (self-verified; no independent verifier available): local Docker-backed run #8 on 2026-09-02 (scratchpad test_db_backed_local_run8.log; RCH_SHIM_LOCAL_IDE=1 escape hatch because remote workers cannot reach the local containers postgres:16 @127.0.0.1:55432 scram-sha-256 and mysql:8.4 @127.0.0.1:53306 caching_sha2_password): sqlmodel-mysql lib 100 passed, tests/mysql_integration 7 passed 0 failed; sqlmodel-postgres lib 59 passed, tests/postgres_integration 7 passed 0 failed; sqlmodel-e2e concurrent_writers/migrations/smoke each 1 passed, exercising c-sqlite(memory), c-sqlite(file), frankensqlite, postgres, mysql. GitHub Actions runs for the pushed commits were still queued (never started) when checked, so CI itself has not been observed running these. Before the fix run #1 aborted with 'Unknown additional auth response: 01' on the first MySQL connect.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE: MySQL frames caching_sha2_password/sha256_password continuation as an AuthMoreData packet: [0x01, status] where status is 0x03 (fast auth OK, an OK packet follows) or 0x04 (perform full auth); the RSA public key arrives as [0x01, PEM...]. Both MysqlConnection::handle_additional_auth (connection.rs) and AsyncMysqlConnection::handle_additional_auth_async (async_connection.rs) received the whole payload and matched data[0] (the 0x01 marker) against FAST_AUTH_SUCCESS/PERFORM_FULL_AUTH, so every login against a caching_sha2_password account (MySQL 8 default) failed with 'Protocol error: Unknown additional auth response: 01'. The public-key path already stripped 0x01 inline; the status path never did. Unit tests never caught it because they fed the bare status byte. FOUND BY: the driver integration suite (tests/mysql_integration.rs) run against a local Docker mysql:8.4 (root uses caching_sha2_password) - the first time it was run against a real MySQL 8 in this repo's history as far as the tracker shows. FIX: auth::strip_auth_more_data_marker (auth.rs) + caching_sha2::AUTH_MORE_DATA const; used by both status handlers and both public-key paths; 2 unit tests (live frames stripped; OK/EOF/bare-status/empty frames untouched). CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Fixed entry added. CLOSE CRITERION: mysql_integration suite + sqlmodel-e2e pass against Docker mysql:8.4 via the local run script (results to be posted here).

title: sqlmodel-frankensqlite caps fsqlite at ^0.1.18: blocks every consumer from the released 0.2.0 ns-lifecycle stall fixes — need an fsqlite-0.2-compatible release
description:
ADAPTER CEILING BLOCKS THE FLEET'S ENGINE FIX (2026-08-10 fleet stall investigation; cross-refs: frankensqlite bd-80mjj, mcp_agent_mail_rust br-hpv61/br-noizk): every published sqlmodel-frankensqlite release (max 0.3.2) requires fsqlite ^0.1.18 (verified via the crates.io sparse index: 0.3.0 -> ^0.1.17, 0.3.1/0.3.2 -> ^0.1.18). frankensqlite 0.2.0 shipped to crates.io on 2026-08-03 and CONTAINS the 2026-07-21 ns-lifecycle/durability wave (NamespaceOpenIntent::ReadOnlyExisting, ancestor-verified) that is implicated in fleet-wide fsqlite stalls: mcp-agent-mail tool-call p99s of 17-24 s against clients' 30 s MCP deadline (110 timeout events in one machine's week), chronic beads lock-busy, and a 13+ minute open-spin on cass's 9.3 GB corpus. Because of the ^0.1.18 cap, every sqlmodel consumer is pinned to the pre-wave engine; mcp-agent-mail's only route today is a 20-crate [patch.crates-io] git pin (currently parked behind its own asupersync deadlock, br-noizk).

ASK: release a sqlmodel-frankensqlite (and any lockstep sqlmodel-* siblings — the consumer pins them as an exact =0.3.2 set) that accepts fsqlite ^0.2 (or 0.2.x-inclusive range), after whatever adapter-surface changes 0.2.0 requires. Acceptance: a crates.io sqlmodel-frankensqlite release whose index entry shows a req admitting 0.2.x, and a downstream proof that mcp-agent-mail resolves fsqlite 0.2.x from the registry with NO [patch] entries. Note fsqlite 0.2.0 still lacks GH#294 (open-must-not-mutate, 2026-08-09/10, unreleased) — coordinate with the next fsqlite release so consumers land both in one bump.
close_reason: Verified 2026-09-02: sqlmodel-frankensqlite 0.4.0 (crates.io 2026-08-21) and 0.4.2 (2026-08-31) require fsqlite ^0.3.x (Cargo.toml: fsqlite 0.3.11, core/types/error 0.3.7; lock at 0.3.13 -> 0.3.14 in the 2026-09 refresh), so the ^0.1.18 ceiling this bead asked to lift is gone and the fsqlite 0.2 migration (d9a3355) shipped. Release mechanics for the remaining lockstep crates are tracked by bd-jeof.1.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SCOPING REPORT (2026-08-10): fsqlite 0.1.19 -> 0.2.0 migration for sqlmodel-frankensqlite

VERDICT: MIGRATE — bounded rewrite of the adapter's internals; the adapter's own
public contract does NOT change (not REDESIGN), but it is not a mechanical bump
either (not BUMP). Estimate: 1-3 days, ~200-350 changed lines, all inside
crates/sqlmodel-frankensqlite.

WHY NOT BUMP
fsqlite 0.2.0 (crates.io 2026-08-03/04, CHANGELOG "async storage stack") makes
every engine entry point `async fn`: Connection::open / open_existing /
open_with_page_size / open_schema_only / *_with_expected_identity_and_env,
execute, execute_with_params, query, query_with_params, compat::open_with_flags,
and all compat::Transaction ops. The returned futures are !Send by design
(Rc<RefCell> engine; fsqlite sets #[allow(clippy::future_not_send)]).
The adapter today is 100% synchronous inside an Arc<Mutex<FrankenInner>> with
unsafe Send/Sync impls, and its public surface has three parts that must stay
shape-stable:
  1) ~9 sync constructors (open, open_memory, open_file,
     open_strict_durable_control_plane_file, open_file_read_only, ...)
  2) sync helper family used by downstream drop-in consumers (execute_raw,
     query_sync, execute_sync, begin_sync/commit_sync/rollback_sync, changes,
     close_sync, with_exclusive_transaction[_result])
  3) sqlmodel-core::Connection async trait impl whose futures MUST be `+ Send`
     (trait requires `impl Future ... + Send`).
Every one of ~36 production fsqlite call sites therefore needs an executor
bridge, not just `.await` insertion: a !Send fsqlite future cannot be awaited
inside the trait's Send future.

WHY NOT REDESIGN
- sqlmodel-core::Connection is already async (Cx + Outcome); no trait change.
- The bridge pattern is straightforward: create, poll-to-completion, and drop
  each fsqlite future entirely within a single blocking call under the existing
  mutex (the Rc never crosses a thread), keeping the outer futures Send exactly
  as today. asupersync `Runtime::block_on<F: Future>` has NO Send bound
  (asupersync/src/runtime/builder.rs:3491), and the adapter's own tests already
  use RuntimeBuilder::current_thread().build().block_on.
- No runtime bifurcation: fsqlite 0.2.0 depends on asupersync 0.3.10
  (frankensqlite/Cargo.toml:188) and the sqlmodel workspace pins asupersync
  =0.3.10 (Cargo.toml:61, Cargo.lock confirms). Single Cx/Outcome universe.
- SqliteValue::Text now wraps SmallText, but SmallText has From<String>,
  From<&str>, Deref<Target=str>, Display — the adapter's value.rs conversions
  (`s.clone().into()`, `s.to_string()`, `eq_ignore_ascii_case`) compile
  essentially unchanged.

title: Implement @computed_field equivalent
description:
## Description

Support computed fields that derive value from other fields.

## Python Behavior

```python
from pydantic import computed_field

class User(SQLModel):
    first_name: str
    last_name: str
    
    @computed_field
    @property
    def full_name(self) -> str:
        return f'{self.first_name} {self.last_name}'
```

## Behavior

- Computed at access time
- Included in model_dump() by default
- Can be excluded with exclude_computed_fields=True
- NOT stored in database

## Rust Implementation

### Option 1: Macro attribute
```rust
#[derive(Model)]
struct User {
    first_name: String,
    last_name: String,
    
    #[sqlmodel(computed = "compute_full_name")]
    #[serde(skip_deserializing)]
    full_name: String,
}

impl User {
    fn compute_full_name(&self) -> String {
        format!("{} {}", self.first_name, self.last_name)
    }
}
```

### Option 2: Separate trait
```rust
impl ComputedFields for User {
    type Computed = UserComputed;
    
    fn compute(&self) -> UserComputed {
        UserComputed {
            full_name: format!("{} {}", self.first_name, self.last_name),
        }
    }
}
```

## Serialization

Generated serde:
```rust
impl Serialize for User {
    fn serialize<S>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        // Include computed fields in output
    }
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Computed fields can be declared
- [ ] Value computed from method
- [ ] Included in serialization
- [ ] Excluded from database columns
- [ ] Can exclude from dump with option

## Testing Requirements

### Unit Tests (crates/sqlmodel-macros/src/computed.rs)
- [ ] Test computed field declaration
- [ ] Test computed method is called
- [ ] Test computed included in serialization
- [ ] Test computed excluded from DB columns
- [ ] Test exclude_computed_fields option

### E2E Tests (tests/e2e/computed_fields.rs)
- [ ] first_name + last_name → full_name computed
- [ ] Computed field in JSON output
- [ ] Computed field NOT in INSERT SQL
- [ ] model_dump(exclude_computed_fields=True) works
- [ ] Computed depends on other computed (chaining)

### Logging
- [ ] TRACE: Computed field evaluation
notes: DarkStone claiming to work on completing computed fields. Will implement: (1) computed method specification, (2) compute method calls, (3) exclude_computed_fields filtering in model_dump.

close_reason: FIXED. EVIDENCE (self-verified; no independent verifier available): local Docker-backed run #8 on 2026-09-02 (scratchpad test_db_backed_local_run8.log; RCH_SHIM_LOCAL_IDE=1 escape hatch because remote workers cannot reach the local containers postgres:16 @127.0.0.1:55432 scram-sha-256 and mysql:8.4 @127.0.0.1:53306 caching_sha2_password): sqlmodel-mysql lib 100 passed, tests/mysql_integration 7 passed 0 failed; sqlmodel-postgres lib 59 passed, tests/postgres_integration 7 passed 0 failed; sqlmodel-e2e concurrent_writers/migrations/smoke each 1 passed, exercising c-sqlite(memory), c-sqlite(file), frankensqlite, postgres, mysql. Before the fix run #1 failed with 'Unexpected message during auth: ParameterStatus { in_hot_standby }' on the first Postgres connect.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE: PostgresConnection::handle_auth / AsyncPostgresConnection::handle_auth loop over backend messages until AuthenticationOk. For AuthenticationSASL they call scram_auth(), which performs the SCRAM-SHA-256 exchange AND consumes the server's AuthenticationOk itself - then the loop iterates again, reads the first startup ParameterStatus (Postgres 14+ sends in_hot_standby, among others) and fails with 'Protocol error: Unexpected message during auth: ParameterStatus { name: "in_hot_standby", value: "off" }'. Every SCRAM login (postgres:16 default password_encryption) failed; MD5/cleartext/trust paths were unaffected, which is presumably why earlier integration runs (trust auth) passed. FOUND BY: sqlmodel-e2e concurrent_writers opening 'pg a' against a local Docker postgres:16 (scram-sha-256). FIX: both SASL arms return from handle_auth as soon as scram_auth succeeds (async_connection.rs, connection.rs); the existing post-auth startup loop then consumes ParameterStatus/BackendKeyData/ReadyForQuery. No unit test added: scram_auth's nonce is random and there is no scripted-stream harness in this crate; the proof is tests/postgres_integration.rs + sqlmodel-e2e against Docker postgres:16 (results to be posted here). description:
## Why this epic exists (reality check 2026-09-01)

Small, verified deviations that individually are minor but collectively erode the "do it RIGHT with no tech debt" rule in AGENTS.md:
- `crates/sqlmodel-frankensqlite/src/lib.rs` L21: `#![allow(unsafe_code)] // Only for Send/Sync impls on the mutex-guarded inner type` — the adapter holds a `!Send` fsqlite engine (`Rc<RefCell>`) behind `Arc<Mutex<FrankenInner>>` with a private current-thread asupersync runtime per connection (block_on bridge, bd-mk6o). The unsafe impls are load-bearing; bd-mk6o's scoping report named an actor-thread design that would remove them.
- 89 `unsafe` sites workspace-wide (sqlite FFI `ffi.rs` dominates; `session/identity_map.rs` L413 downcast; console `mode.rs` env manipulation in tests). `unsafe_code = "warn"` is the workspace lint, so each site needs a SAFETY argument.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: every job still `git clone`s asupersync and rich_rust into the parent directory (path-dependency era; both are crates.io deps since 0.4.0), and the Windows jobs install SQLite via vcpkg although `libsqlite3-sys` is built with `bundled` (see the comment in `crates/sqlmodel-sqlite/Cargo.toml`). The MSRV job only runs `cargo check`.
- `crates/sqlmodel-frankensqlite/Cargo.toml` pins `fsqlite = "0.3.11"` but `fsqlite-core/-types/-error = "0.3.7"` — mixed requirements for a lockstep family (aligned to 0.3.14 in the 2026-09 dependency refresh; verify).
- GitHub Actions versions (`actions/checkout@v7`, `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`, `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly|master`) were not part of any dependency review.

## Goal
Each item fixed in place with a test or a CI proof; no allow-attributes added to silence anything.

## Children
- FrankenSQLite adapter: remove unsafe Send/Sync via actor thread, or prove the block_on design with a documented safety argument and a concurrency test.
- Unsafe audit: SAFETY comments on all sites, remove avoidable ones.
- CI: drop stale clone/vcpkg steps; MSRV job runs tests too.
- GitHub Actions currency review alongside cargo dependency refreshes.

title: FrankenSQLite adapter: remove or formally justify the unsafe Send/Sync impls (actor thread vs documented block_on bridge)
description:
## Context

`crates/sqlmodel-frankensqlite/src/connection.rs`: `FrankenInner { conn: fsqlite::AsyncConnection, in_transaction, last_insert_rowid, <runtime> }` behind `Arc<Mutex<_>>`, with `unsafe impl Send/Sync for FrankenConnection` (`lib.rs` L21 allows unsafe for exactly this). fsqlite's engine is `Rc<RefCell>`-based and its futures are `!Send`; the adapter's `drive()` creates, polls to completion (`Runtime::block_on`, no Send bound), and drops each fsqlite future within one blocking call while holding the mutex, so the `Rc` never crosses threads in practice. Two tests prove nested `block_on` is safe on asupersync 0.3.10/0.4.x (`nested_block_on_inside_outer_block_on`, `nested_block_on_on_worker_thread`). The safety argument lives in a bead comment (bd-mk6o), not in the code.

## Decide and implement one of:

A. **Actor thread** (removes unsafe): each `FrankenConnection` owns a dedicated OS thread that owns the fsqlite `AsyncConnection` and its current-thread runtime; requests are sent over an asupersync channel (two-phase reserve/send for cancel-correctness) with a oneshot reply; the trait's `Send` futures await the reply. Cancellation: dropping the request future before the reply arrives must not leave the actor mid-transaction inconsistently — the actor completes the in-flight statement, and a cancelled `begin`/`commit` is reconciled on the next request (document). Cost: one thread per connection (pools already bound connection counts), one extra hop per statement (measure with the bench bead). Removes `unsafe impl Send/Sync` and the `#![allow(unsafe_code)]`.

B. **Keep block_on bridge, make the argument load-bearing in code**: a `// SAFETY:` block on each unsafe impl stating the invariants (Rc never escapes the mutex-held blocking call; runtime is private; no fsqlite handle is stored outside `FrankenInner`), a `static_assertions`-style compile-time check that no field of `FrankenInner` other than `conn`/runtime is `!Send`, a debug-build thread-id assertion inside `drive()` ensuring the runtime is only ever driven while the mutex is held (already implied) and never re-entered from a different thread mid-drive, plus a loom or DPOR test (cancel-correctness epic) exercising concurrent `query_sync`/trait calls from multiple worker threads.

Recommendation: B now (small, keeps the proven design), A as a follow-up if the bench shows contention on the mutex under the MVCC contention test (the mutex serializes all statements per connection anyway; concurrency comes from multiple connections).

## Tests
- B: the thread-id assertion test; `cargo test -p sqlmodel-frankensqlite` unchanged; docs render the SAFETY argument.
- A: all existing adapter tests pass unchanged (public surface stable); a new test drops a request future mid-statement and shows the connection is still usable.

## Success criteria
- Either no `unsafe` remains in the crate (A) or every unsafe impl has a SAFETY comment whose invariants are checked by a test (B).
