## Context

`rg -c 'unsafe ' crates --type rust` = 89 sites. Distribution: `crates/sqlmodel-sqlite/src/{ffi.rs,connection.rs,types.rs}` (C SQLite FFI; crate-level `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` at lib.rs L14), `crates/sqlmodel-session/src/identity_map.rs` L413 (`#[allow(unsafe_code)]` around a type-erased downcast), `crates/sqlmodel-frankensqlite/src/lib.rs` (Send/Sync, separate bead), `crates/sqlmodel-console/src/mode.rs` L337/L345 and console tests (env var set/remove in tests — `std::env::set_var` is unsafe since edition 2024). Workspace lint is `unsafe_code = "warn"`; bd-24ix reviewed one `SQLITE_TRANSIENT` transmute. There is no systematic SAFETY documentation.

## What to do

1. Inventory: list every `unsafe` block/impl/fn with file:line and a one-line purpose (put the table in the bead comment).
2. For each: add a `// SAFETY:` comment stating the invariant relied on (pointer validity/lifetime from the sqlite3 API contract, `SQLITE_TRANSIENT` copy semantics, `CStr` NUL guarantees, single-threaded env mutation in tests under a test lock, downcast type equality guaranteed by `TypeId` check preceding it).
3. Remove avoidable unsafe: `identity_map.rs` L413 — replace the unsafe downcast with `Box<dyn Any>::downcast` / `Arc<dyn Any + Send + Sync>::downcast` (safe APIs exist; the comment at L137-140 suggests a stored type-erased Arc — `Arc::downcast` is safe); console env manipulation in tests — use a process-wide test mutex and `std::env::set_var` inside `unsafe` with the SAFETY note, or refactor `OutputMode::detect` to take an `impl Fn(&str) -> Option<String>` env reader so tests inject values without touching the process environment (preferred; removes the unsafe entirely and makes the tests parallel-safe).
4. sqlite FFI: check each `sqlite3_*` call's error-code handling and lifetime of `*const c_char` returned by `sqlite3_column_text` (must be copied before the next `step`/`reset`), `sqlite3_bind_blob` with `SQLITE_TRANSIENT`, `sqlite3_finalize` on all paths (Drop). Add a Miri-compatible subset run if feasible (`cargo +nightly miri test -p sqlmodel-sqlite` will not run the C library; instead run `cargo test` under Valgrind or ASan in a CI job — `RUSTFLAGS=-Zsanitizer=address` on nightly, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu — for the sqlite crate only).
5. Keep `unsafe_code = "warn"` workspace-wide; consider `#![deny(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]` in the sqlite crate to force block-level SAFETY comments.

## Success criteria
- Every `unsafe` has an adjacent `SAFETY:` comment (grep test: count of `unsafe` sites == count of `SAFETY:` comments within 3 lines above).
- identity_map and console test unsafe removed.
- ASan job green for sqlmodel-sqlite.

## Why
AGENTS.md warns on unsafe rather than forbidding it; the trade is that every site carries its justification. Today none do.

title: CI cleanup: drop path-era asupersync/rich_rust clones and Windows vcpkg SQLite; MSRV job runs tests
description:
## Context

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `release.yml` carry steps from the path-dependency era:
- Every job runs "Clone dependencies": `git clone https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/asupersync.git` and `rich_rust.git` into the parent directory. Since 0.4.0 both are crates.io dependencies with no `[patch]`; the clones are dead weight (slow, and a stale clone could mask a registry problem if a `[patch]` ever reappears).
- Windows Test/Build jobs install SQLite via vcpkg and export `SQLITE3_LIB_DIR`/`SQLITE3_INCLUDE_DIR`; `libsqlite3-sys` is built with `features = ["bundled"]` (see the long comment in `crates/sqlmodel-sqlite/Cargo.toml`), so these are unused — and worse, `SQLITE3_LIB_DIR` may make libsqlite3-sys prefer the vcpkg library over the bundled one on Windows, silently changing what CI tests.
- MSRV job: `cargo check --workspace --exclude sqlmodel-frankensqlite` only; the declared 1.95 floor is never test-verified.
- Lint job uses `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly` (floating) while `rust-toolchain.toml` pins `nightly-2026-08-25`; rustup honors the file, so this works, but the action's own install is wasted and the intent is unclear to readers.
- Security job cannot fail (`|| true`) — handled by the security epic; coordinate.

## What to do

1. Remove the "Clone dependencies" steps from all jobs in both workflows.
2. Remove the Windows vcpkg SQLite steps and the `SQLITE3_*`/`LIB`/`PATH` env exports; confirm the Windows test job passes with the bundled build (it must — that was the point of bundling).
3. MSRV job: add `cargo test --workspace --exclude sqlmodel-frankensqlite --exclude sqlmodel-e2e` (RUSTFLAGS="" as now); keep the check step.
4. Toolchain steps: use `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master` with `toolchain: nightly-2026-08-25` read from the file? Simpler: keep the action for components (rustfmt, clippy) but add a comment that `rust-toolchain.toml` is authoritative; or drop the action and rely on rustup's auto-install (needs `rustup show` step to trigger it). Pick one and apply consistently.
5. Add `timeout-minutes` where missing and `concurrency` already exists; keep.
6. Run the full workflow on a branch (workflow_dispatch) before merging; record run URLs in the bead comment.

## Success criteria
- CI green on all OSes with the clone and vcpkg steps gone; total CI time reduced (record before/after).
- MSRV job runs tests.

## Why
CI should test what users get (registry deps, bundled SQLite), not a historical local layout.
close_reason: DONE (self-verified YAML; GitHub Actions cannot be executed from this machine): .github/workflows/ci.yml no longer clones asupersync/rich_rust or installs Windows vcpkg SQLite (bundled libsqlite3-sys builds everywhere); MSRV job now runs cargo test (excluding frankensqlite and e2e); release.yml clone step removed. Evidence that the YAML parses: runs for auto-pushed commit 3d79be0 were queued with every job listed. Completion of those runs was not observed in this session.

title: GitHub Actions currency and pinning policy (dependabot github-actions or SHA pins) as part of dependency refreshes
description:
## Context

Dependency refreshes (UPGRADE_LOG.md 2026-02-19 and 2026-09-02) cover Cargo dependencies only. The workflows pin `actions/checkout@v7`, `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`, `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly` / `@master`, and (release.yml) upload/release actions by major tag. Major-tag pins float to the latest minor, which is the GitHub-recommended default but means a broken action release can break CI with no local change; SHA pinning is the hardening alternative.

## What to do

1. Enumerate every `uses:` in `.github/workflows/*.yml`; check each action's latest major and release notes (GitHub releases API) for deprecations (Node runtime versions, input renames).
2. Decide the pinning policy and document it in a comment at the top of `ci.yml`: either major tags (current) with Dependabot `github-actions` ecosystem enabled in `.github/dependabot.yml` (create it; only `github-actions` and `cargo` with grouped updates, so PRs stay few), or SHA pins with a comment carrying the version (Dependabot updates SHA pins too).
3. Apply the policy; run the workflows on a branch; record run URLs.
4. Add a line to UPGRADE_LOG.md's procedure section: "GitHub Actions are part of every dependency refresh".

## Success criteria
- `.github/dependabot.yml` exists (or SHA pins applied) and the policy comment exists.
- All actions at current majors with no deprecation warnings in the run logs.

title: API polish after the 2026-09 rounds: MigrationRunner lock_timeout, unused MigrationStatus::Failed, Row::contains consistent with get_named, MySQL first-packet audit
description:
## Background
Small API inconsistencies left by the 2026-09 rounds, each a footgun for users:
1. `MigrationRunner::acquire_lock` waits up to a hard-coded 120 s on MySQL (`GET_LOCK(?, 120)`) and without limit on PostgreSQL (`pg_advisory_lock`); there is no way to configure the wait or to fail fast.
2. `MigrationStatus::Failed { error }` (crates/sqlmodel-schema/src/migrate.rs) is never produced by any code path; a user matching on it waits for something that cannot happen.
3. `Row::get_named` falls back to an unambiguous case-insensitive match (bug 33 follow-up), but `Row::contains_column` / `ColumnInfo::contains` are still exact, so `contains_column("constraint_name")` can be false while `get_named("constraint_name")` succeeds.
4. `PacketType::from_first_byte` (MySQL) is still used for the first packet of a response, where 0x00 really is OK; its doc now points to `RowPacket` for the row phase. Re-audit the remaining call sites (connection.rs around lines 446 and 596, async_connection.rs) for any other place a data packet can start with 0x00 or 0xFE.

## What to build
1. `MigrationRunner::lock_timeout(Duration)` builder, default 120 s on both servers (`pg_try_advisory_lock` polling with a deadline, or `SET LOCAL lock_timeout` inside a transaction); documented; unit test for the SQL emitted.
2. Remove `MigrationStatus::Failed` (no users, no backwards-compatibility policy per AGENTS.md) or produce it from `migrate` for the migration that failed; pick one, document, test.
3. Make `contains` / `contains_column` use the same resolution as `index_of`; unit test.
4. Write the audit result of item 4 as a comment; fix anything found with a unit test.
CHANGELOG entries for each user-visible change.
acceptance_criteria: lock_timeout builder with default 120s on both servers and a unit test; Failed variant removed or produced (documented, tested); contains/contains_column resolve like index_of with a unit test; audit comment written; CHANGELOG entries
close_reason: 1. MigrationRunner::lock_timeout(Duration) with DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT = 120 s (exported from sqlmodel-schema): PostgreSQL now polls pg_try_advisory_lock until the deadline (pg_advisory_lock used to block without limit), MySQL passes the seconds to GET_LOCK(?, ?) (was hard-coded 120); lock_statement() factored and unit-tested (lock_statement_carries_the_configured_timeout: default 120, custom 5, PG try-lock SQL, SQLite none, same/different tracking tables key equality); the e2e migrations two-runner race is green on PG and MySQL with the new code (Docker, 2026-09-03). 2. MigrationStatus::Failed removed (no producer; no back-compat policy) with its test adjusted. 3. Row::contains / contains_column now resolve via index_of (exact, then unambiguous case-insensitive) — asserted in named_lookup_falls_back_to_case_insensitive_match. 4. Audit of PacketType::from_first_byte call sites: connection.rs handle_auth_result and the COM_QUERY first response, async_connection.rs auth result, COM_QUERY first response, COM_STMT_EXECUTE first response — all five classify the FIRST packet of a response where 0x00 is an OK packet and a short 0xFE is EOF/auth-switch; a column-count packet can only start with a lenenc int prefix (<0xFB or 0xFC), never 0x00/0xFE; every row phase uses RowPacket::classify since bug 34. Nothing further to fix. CHANGELOG entry. Gates: core 342, schema 210 unit tests; clippy -D warnings; fmt.

title: Expose exact SQLite native error codes for fail-closed callers
description: Agent Mail dashboard exporter discovered that sqlmodel-sqlite collapses SQLITE_READONLY and unrelated SQLite failures into QueryErrorKind::Database without retaining the numeric primary/extended result code. Add a typed, driver-specific error-code surface without message parsing; cover execute_raw failures (including read-only writes) and all SQLite error constructors consistently; bump/publish the minimal patch release required by the downstream standalone exporter; update Agent Mail to verify SQLITE_READONLY exactly; run focused and workspace release gates.
notes: Published sqlmodel-sqlite 0.3.3 with exact asupersync =0.3.10 and MSRV 1.95. Downstream mcp-agent-mail hostile exporter regression passed via RCH, including exact extended()==SQLITE_READONLY verification.

title: C SQLite driver stores Timestamp/TimestampTz/Time as ISO text with millisecond precision, silently dropping microseconds
close_reason: FIXED. Shared microsecond-exact ISO formatters in sqlmodel_core::value (civil_from_days/iso_date/iso_time/iso_timestamp, floor division for pre-1970 instants); the C SQLite driver delegates to them. Before: 2024-03-15T10:20:30.123456 read back as .123 (types e2e run 2). EVIDENCE (self-verified): remote run g2_run4 on 2026-09-02 - sqlmodel-e2e types/session/pool all pass on c-sqlite(memory), c-sqlite(file), frankensqlite; unit tests core 338, schema 198, session 144, query 220, sqlite 29, frankensqlite 83, pool 71 pass. (types e2e asserts exact equality of NaiveTime 23:59:59.999999 and DateTime<Utc> ...123456 on both SQLite drivers). CHANGELOG entry.

title: Drivers never check cancellation: C SQLite, FrankenSQLite, and MySQL have zero Cx checkpoints, Postgres two; a pre-cancelled Cx still executes statements (Session::flush inserted rows)
close_reason: FIXED. sqlmodel_core::cancel_requested(cx); every Connection method in the C SQLite, FrankenSQLite, PostgreSQL, and MySQL drivers (including begin_transaction_impl) returns Outcome::Cancelled before touching the database when the context is already cancelled; Session::flush and Session::begin check too. AGENTS.md design bullet rewritten to what is true. EVIDENCE (self-verified): local Docker-backed run #11 on 2026-09-02 (scratchpad test_e2e_local_run11.log): sqlmodel-e2e concurrent_writers, migrations, pool, session, smoke pass on c-sqlite(memory), c-sqlite(file), frankensqlite, postgres (16, scram), mysql (8.4, caching_sha2); driver suites postgres 7/7 and mysql 7/7 (run #10). Remote run g2_run4: the same e2e scenarios plus types on the three SQLite drivers. The session scenario's cancellation step (flush with a pre-cancelled Cx returns Cancelled and inserts nothing) passes on all five drivers. CHANGELOG entry.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE: none of the drivers consulted the Cx: sqlmodel-sqlite and sqlmodel-frankensqlite Connection impls took  and ran the statement synchronously before returning the future; sqlmodel-mysql/postgres only touched cx via OwnedMutexGuard::lock (and mapped its failure to a generic connection error). Session::flush/begin had no check either, so the e2e Session scenario's flush(&cancelled_cx) inserted the row and returned Ok. FIX: sqlmodel_core::cancel_requested(cx) -> Option<CancelReason>; every Connection method in all four drivers returns Outcome::Cancelled before doing work when the context is already cancelled (sqlite/franken: 9 methods each; postgres/mysql: the shared lock prologue in every method); Session::flush and Session::begin check too. AGENTS.md design-decision bullet rewritten to what is actually true (entry checks; SQLite statements cannot be interrupted mid-flight). CHANGELOG entry. Proof: e2e session scenario cancellation step on every driver (to be posted).

title: Add cancel-correct pool close-and-drain lifecycle
description: Add Pool::close_and_drain(&Cx) for recovery quiescence: atomically close admission, close idle connections, wake blocked acquirers, await active lease retirement without lost wakeups, preserve closed state on cancellation/timeout, notify on every final active-count path, and prevent post-close resurrection. Add deterministic lifecycle/race tests. No release or version bump in this task.
close_reason: Verified 2026-09-02: Pool::close_and_drain(&self, cx: &Cx) -> Outcome<(), Error> exists at crates/sqlmodel-pool/src/lib.rs L1099, landed in 38b2c0b (fix(pool): make close-and-drain cancel-correct (bd-rofu)); pool suite 71 tests pass. Remaining proof on real connections and under DPOR is tracked by bd-slot.6 and bd-x6jl.3.

title: Integrate console into sqlmodel-sqlite driver
description:
## Purpose
Add rich console output to the SQLite driver for database operations, PRAGMA visualization, and transaction state feedback.

## Background
SQLite operations that benefit from console output:
- Database file open/create
- Attaching additional databases
- PRAGMA queries and results
- WAL mode operations
- Transaction state (begin/commit/rollback)
- Busy timeout waiting

## Implementation Details

### File Modifications
crates/sqlmodel-sqlite/src/connection.rs
crates/sqlmodel-sqlite/src/lib.rs (re-exports)

### ConsoleAware Implementation
Add optional SqlModelConsole to SqliteConnection:
struct SqliteConnection {
    // existing fields...
    console: Option<Arc<SqlModelConsole>>,
}

### Database Open Feedback
SQLite database: ./data.db
  Mode: read-write
  Journal: WAL
  Page size: 4096
  Cache size: 2000 pages

### PRAGMA Visualization
Format PRAGMA query results in a nice table:
PRAGMA table_info(users):
+---------+---------+---------+---------+
| cid     | name    | type    | notnull |
+---------+---------+---------+---------+
| 0       | id      | INTEGER | 1       |
| 1       | name    | TEXT    | 0       |
+---------+---------+---------+---------+

### Transaction State
Show transaction boundaries:
[BEGIN] Transaction started
  ... operations ...
[COMMIT] Transaction committed (23ms, 5 operations)

### WAL Checkpoint Progress
For checkpoint operations:
WAL checkpoint: [========>      ] 60% (1200/2000 pages)

### Busy Timeout Feedback
When waiting for locks:
[..] Waiting for database lock... (2.1s)

## Plain Text Mode
Opened SQLite database: ./data.db (WAL mode)
Transaction committed: 23ms
PRAGMA table_info: 5 columns

## Conditional Compilation
Use cfg feature flag same as postgres driver.

## Verification Steps
1. Test database open with console enabled
2. Test PRAGMA formatting
3. Test transaction state feedback
4. Verify WAL checkpoint progress
5. Test busy timeout messaging
6. Verify plain text output
7. Test with console disabled

## Dependencies
- sqlmodel-console crate
- SqlModelConsole, Theme components
acceptance_criteria:
SQLite driver implements ConsoleAware trait
Connection events emit console output
Query execution outputs to console when enabled
Error states display through ErrorPanel
All unit tests verify console integration
Integration tests verify end-to-end output
close_reason: done

title: Documentation truth and tracker integrity: make every planning doc match the code and the tracker match the work
description:
## Why this epic exists (reality check 2026-09-01)

Code is the ground truth for where the project is; the docs are the measuring stick for where it promised to be. On 2026-09-01 the two disagree in every planning document, and the issue tracker has lost work items that the docs still cite. Verified items (file:line against the tree at cc8e564):

README.md
- L141 `sqlmodel = "0.4.2"` and L153 "released in lockstep at the same version (0.4.2)": false at the registry (see the release-integrity epic).
- Architecture diagram (~L317-352) and "Crate Responsibilities" table omit `sqlmodel-frankensqlite`; the drivers line reads "sqlmodel-postgres sqlmodel-mysql sqlmodel-sqlite (drivers)".
- L408-410 type table lists chrono/uuid types that cannot compile as model fields (see the unreachable-features epic).
- L502 troubleshooting "error[E0658]: edition 2024 is unstable" -> "rustup default nightly": edition 2024 has been stable since Rust 1.85; the entry is obsolete and misdirects users.
- FAQ L535 "Is this production-ready? Nearly." vs "When SQLModel Rust might not fit: you require immediate production readiness (we're in active development)". Pick one framing.

FEATURE_PARITY.md
- L5 "Last Updated: 2026-02-10", L392 "Last verified: 2026-01-27" — seven months stale; no row for sqlmodel-frankensqlite, sqlmodel-session, or sqlmodel-console in the Test Coverage table; "Fully Production-Ready" section unqualified; `raw_query!()`/`raw_execute!()` are described as macros but are functions (`crates/sqlmodel-query/src/lib.rs` L143, L153).

PLAN_TO_PORT_SQLMODEL_TO_RUST.md
- L157 asupersync "TCP/IO 🔜 Phase 2 — Database drivers blocked" (drivers shipped long ago); phases 1-6 never marked complete; L203-206 success criteria never measured.

PROPOSED_RUST_ARCHITECTURE.md
- §9 cites `bd-3bmd` as an open follow-up; that bead does not exist in `.beads/issues.jsonl`.

EXISTING_SQLMODEL_STRUCTURE.md
- §12 "Explicit Exclusions" says lazy loading, unit of work, identity map, generics, computed fields are intentionally NOT ported — all are implemented and bd-162's policy is "no exclusions"; L659 "Migrations ⚠️ Basic support — No auto-generation" contradicts FEATURE_PARITY ("schema_diff + MigrationWriter ✅ Implemented").

AGENTS.md
- L167 / L275: a workspace `tests/` directory for cross-component tests — it does not exist. L87 lists `thiserror` as a key dependency — it is not a direct dependency of any crate. Nothing mentions that the RCH hook can refuse local fallback (use `rch exec -- cargo ...`).

crates/sqlmodel-frankensqlite
- The only crate without a README.md and without `readme = "README.md"` in Cargo.toml (published to crates.io with no page body).

SESSION_TODO.md
- A Codex scratchpad from 2026-02-10 with unchecked items (bd-3bmd block; B2; E3; H5; F3; C "Landing the plane") that were either done elsewhere or never tracked. Files are never deleted in this repo (AGENTS.md rule 1), so it must be retired in place.

Tracker (.beads)
- Eleven bead IDs referenced by SESSION_TODO.md / PROPOSED_RUST_ARCHITECTURE.md do not exist: bd-ukkg, bd-2bht, bd-4bhg, bd-3bmd, bd-3j44, bd-3g6y, bd-ywnj, bd-2lpn, bd-22u8, bd-1ytr, bd-3obp.
- Open/in-progress beads whose work is already in the tree: bd-26g5 (`Expr::Subquery(String)`, no recursive type), bd-gbcp (workspace `assert_is_empty = "allow"` since 0.4.0; clippy -D warnings clean on 2026-09-01), bd-n8aa (clippy clean), bd-rofu (`Pool::close_and_drain` at pool/lib.rs L1099, commit 38b2c0b), bd-mk6o (0.4.0 shipped fsqlite 0.3.x; now 0.3.14). bd-o59n remains valid (reader.rs L94/L96 links still break `cargo doc -D warnings`).

## Goal

Every planning document states only what the code does; README snippets are compiled; a guard test fails when a crate is missing from the README or lacks a README; the tracker's open set equals the actual remaining work; the lost IDs are mapped to commits.

## Children
- Doc-truth pass across README, FEATURE_PARITY, PLAN, PROPOSED_ARCH, EXISTING_STRUCTURE, AGENTS (itemized).
- README snippets compiled as doctests via include_str.
- Tracker reconciliation: close done beads with evidence, map lost IDs, comment on bd-kzp1/bd-162.
- Retire SESSION_TODO.md in place.
- sqlmodel-frankensqlite README + readme field.
- Doc-drift guard test.

title: Compile README code blocks as doctests via include_str (hidden assertions prove the documented SQL)
description:
## Context

README.md contains ~15 Rust code blocks (Quick Example, Quick Start 1-3, Console setup, Model Attributes Reference, Expression Builder Reference). None is compiled. The 2026-09-01 check found the type table promising uncompilable field types and the Quick Start `SchemaBuilder` snippet's DDL comment (`"id" BIGINT AUTOINCREMENT`) plausibly out of date relative to `create.rs`. Rust supports compiling a markdown file's code blocks as doctests via `#[doc = include_str!("../README.md")]`; this is the standard way to keep a README honest.

## What to build

1. In `crates/sqlmodel/src/lib.rs`: `#[cfg(doctest)] #[doc = include_str!("../../README.md")] pub struct ReadmeDoctests;` (path relative to the crate; the README lives at the workspace root — the facade crate's `Cargo.toml` should also gain `readme = "../../README.md"` if not already using its own README; verify what crates.io shows for `sqlmodel`).
2. Make every README Rust block compile under the facade's doctest environment: add hidden setup lines (`# use sqlmodel::prelude::*;`, `# async fn demo(cx: &Cx, conn: &impl Connection) -> Outcome<(), Error> {` ... `# Outcome::Ok(()) }`) using the `#` doctest-hiding syntax so rendered README text is unchanged (GitHub renders `# ` lines as-is inside ```rust blocks — so instead use ```rust,ignore for blocks that need heavy scaffolding? No: prefer real compilation. Where scaffolding would clutter the README, restructure the snippet so it is a complete `fn` and mark blocks that need a live DB as ```rust,no_run so they compile but do not execute).
3. Blocks that show generated SQL/DDL as comments (`// Generates: SELECT ...`): turn them into assertions inside the doctest (`assert_eq!(query.to_sql(Dialect::Postgres), "SELECT ...")`) hidden with `#` so the README shows the comment while the test proves it.
4. The Expression Builder Reference block is a list of expressions, not statements; wrap as `let _ = Expr::col("age").gt(18);` lines via hidden prefix or convert the block to a table if that reads better.
5. Console block needs `sqlmodel-console` with `rich`: gate with `# #[cfg(feature = "console")]` or mark ```rust,ignore with an explicit reason comment in the README source (HTML comment) — allowed only for that block.
6. CI: `cargo test -p sqlmodel --doc` already runs in the Test job; confirm the README doctests execute there (`--features c-sqlite-tests` if a block needs SQLite).

## Success criteria
- `cargo test -p sqlmodel --doc` shows the README doctests (count them in the bead comment) passing.
- Deliberately changing `Expr::col("age").gt(18)`'s documented SQL in the README fails the doctest.
- Rendered README on GitHub is unchanged in appearance except where snippets were made complete.

## Why
Cheapest possible doc-drift prevention for the document users read first; also caught real drift on 2026-09-01.
close_reason: DONE. crates/sqlmodel/src/lib.rs includes README.md as a doctest (#[cfg(all(doctest, feature = "nightly-try"))]); README Rust blocks rewritten as complete programs (overview with the real SQL asserted at top level, quick start = model + schema_for + crud, transactions = transfer with retry_transaction and Session::with_retry); console/attribute-cheatsheet/Expr-catalogue blocks marked rust,ignore with a stated reason; the console diagram block tagged text. Found two long-standing README falsehoods: Select::to_sql (does not exist; real API build_with_dialect) and ? on Outcome (needs asupersync's nightly-outcome-try -> new nightly-try feature). EVIDENCE: cargo test -p sqlmodel --doc --features nightly-try: 3 passed, 7 ignored (remote runs g2_run2..4); CI doctest step and the gates script pass the feature.

title: sqlmodel-frankensqlite README.md and readme field (only crate published without one)
description:
## Context

Every workspace crate has a `README.md` and `readme = "README.md"` in its Cargo.toml except `crates/sqlmodel-frankensqlite` (directory contains only `Cargo.toml` and `src/`). It is published to crates.io (0.4.2 on 2026-08-31) with an empty page body, and it is the crate with the most to explain: nightly-only (`core_intrinsics` via fsqlite-pager on x86_64), `BEGIN CONCURRENT`/MVCC semantics, the sync helper family (`execute_raw`, `query_sync`, `execute_sync`, `begin_sync`, ...), strict-durable control-plane profile (`open_strict_durable_control_plane_file`), the block_on bridge design (private current-thread asupersync runtime per connection; nested block_on proven safe in tests), `open_existing` for query-only callers, exact error mapping (`WriteConflict`/`SerializationFailure` -> retryable), and behavioral differences from C SQLite (triggers, `sqlite_master`).

## What to write

`crates/sqlmodel-frankensqlite/README.md` following the sibling crates' structure (`crates/sqlmodel-sqlite/README.md` as the template: title, one-paragraph role, "Role in the SQLModel Rust System", "Usage", "Links"), plus sections specific to this crate:
1. Requirements: nightly toolchain and why; fsqlite version line (0.3.14 as of 2026-09-01) and the workspace policy of tracking fsqlite releases.
2. Opening connections: the constructor family with one-line semantics each; the strict-durable profile and what it enforces.
3. Transactions: isolation-level mapping (EXCLUSIVE/IMMEDIATE/DEFERRED today; `BEGIN CONCURRENT` via `TransactionMode::Concurrent` once the sibling bead lands) and retry guidance (`Error::is_retryable`, `retry_transaction`).
4. Differences from C SQLite: the known list (link to the differential-oracle bead's allow-list once it exists).
5. Concurrency model: the bridge design in three sentences, the `Send`/`Sync` safety argument, the pool retirement hook (`close_without_checkpoint`, from 0.3.0 notes).

title: Doc-drift guard test: crates listed in README/AGENTS, READMEs present, referenced paths and bead IDs exist, banned stale phrases
description:
## Context

Doc drift accumulated silently for seven months (FEATURE_PARITY last verified 2026-01-27; frankensqlite absent from README's architecture; a nonexistent `tests/` directory in AGENTS.md; a lost bead cited in the architecture doc). Humans will not re-audit monthly; a test will.

## What to build

A workspace-level guard test (location: `crates/sqlmodel-e2e/tests/doc_truth.rs` once that crate exists; until then `crates/sqlmodel/tests/doc_truth.rs`, no features needed) that reads the repo's markdown files at test time (path via `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")/../..`) and asserts:
1. Every directory under `crates/` (from `cargo metadata` or `std::fs::read_dir`) appears by name in README.md's "Crate Responsibilities" table and in AGENTS.md's Workspace Structure tree.
2. Every crate directory contains `README.md` and its `Cargo.toml` has `readme = "README.md"` (parse with a minimal `toml` dev-dep or a line scan).
3. Every path mentioned in AGENTS.md's "Workspace Structure" and "Key Files by Crate" tables exists (`crates/<crate>/src/<file>.rs`).
4. Every bead ID pattern `bd-[a-z0-9]+(\.\d+)?` mentioned in README/AGENTS/PLAN/PROPOSED_ARCH/FEATURE_PARITY/EXISTING_STRUCTURE exists in `.beads/issues.jsonl` (parse the JSONL ids).
5. README install snippet versions equal the workspace version from `cargo metadata` (the release-validation bead does the same in CI shell; keeping it in a Rust test makes it run locally too).
6. FEATURE_PARITY "Last verified" date is not older than 120 days relative to the newest commit date in the tree? (Time-based asserts flake; instead assert the date is >= the date of the most recent `## [x.y.z]` CHANGELOG entry — a release should re-verify parity.)
7. No markdown file contains the retired phrases list (`edition 2024 is unstable`, `TCP/IO | 🔜`, `raw_query!`) — maintained as a small const array with a comment per entry saying why it is banned.

Failures print the file, line, and the offending text.

## Success criteria
- Test fails on the tree as of 2026-09-01 for items 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 (proving it detects the known drift), then passes after the doc-truth and README beads.
- Runs in < 1s; no network.

## Why
Turns the reality check's most tedious findings into a permanent, free gate.
close_reason: Doc-truth guard landed as crates/sqlmodel-e2e/tests/doc_truth.rs — six checks, pure filesystem reads, ~0.03s, no network. (1) every crate directory appears in README's Crate Responsibilities table and in AGENTS.md; (2) every crate ships README.md and sets readme = "README.md" in its manifest; (3) every src/<file> cited by AGENTS.md's Key Files by Crate table exists; (4) every bd-* id cited in README/AGENTS/PLAN/PROPOSED_RUST_ARCHITECTURE/FEATURE_PARITY/EXISTING_SQLMODEL_STRUCTURE exists in .beads/issues.jsonl, with historical 'no longer exists' footprints exempt; (5) every sqlmodel version cited in README equals the workspace version or is a dotted prefix of it (0.4 admits 0.4.2); (6) FEATURE_PARITY's Last Updated date is not older than CHANGELOG's newest dated release; (7) no markdown contains a retired phrase, each with a documented reason (edition 2024 is unstable / TCP-IO emoji cell / raw_query!). The guard caught and I fixed real drift on landing: README's Crate Responsibilities table listed sqlmodel-console twice and sqlmodel-pool not at all, and lacked any sqlmodel-e2e row; crates/sqlmodel-e2e had no README.md and no readme key (both added, with a scenario table). Failure messages print file, line, and offending text. Gates: 6/6 green in 0.03s; clippy -p sqlmodel-e2e --all-targets -D warnings clean; fmt clean; workspace check clean.

title: ORM user guide (docs/guide): models, queries, sessions, relationships, inheritance, migrations, drivers, pooling, errors, cancellation — all snippets doctest-compiled
description:
## Context

README "Known Limitations" L484: "**Limited documentation**: We're working on it". The README's own Documentation section (L306) links only the console user guide, the console agent-compatibility guide, and three design documents. `docs/` contains only `console/`. There is no user-facing guide for the things the library is for: defining models (every `#[sqlmodel(...)]` attribute with DDL consequences), the query builder (every `Expr` family with per-dialect SQL), Session/unit-of-work semantics (identity map reference identity, flush ordering, cascade rules), relationships (`Lazy<T>`, `Related<T>`, `RelatedMany<T>`, batch loaders, back_populates), inheritance (STI/JTI/CTI), schema and migrations (SchemaBuilder, diff, MigrationWriter/Runner, introspection), drivers (choosing C-SQLite vs FrankenSQLite, Postgres/MySQL connection config, TLS/auth modes), pooling, error handling (`Outcome`, `Error` kinds, `is_retryable`), cancellation and budgets, and testing patterns. Python SQLModel's docs are a large part of its appeal; parity includes the onboarding experience.

## What to build

`docs/guide/` with one markdown file per topic above (10-12 files, each 150-400 lines), plus `docs/guide/README.md` as the index, linked from the root README's Documentation section. Rules:
1. Every Rust snippet compiles: the guide files are included as doctests from the facade (`#[cfg(doctest)] #[doc = include_str!("../../docs/guide/<topic>.md")]` per file, same mechanism as the README doctest bead) with `no_run` for DB-touching examples and `c-sqlite-tests` feature for those that can execute in-memory.
2. Every "generates this SQL" statement is an assertion in a hidden doctest line, so the guide cannot drift from the emitted SQL.
3. Cross-link to rustdoc (`docs.rs/sqlmodel`) for API detail; the guide explains concepts and shows canonical patterns, not every method.
4. Each page ends with "Differences from Python SQLModel" (2-6 bullets) — this is where the design-differences content from EXISTING_SQLMODEL_STRUCTURE §12 belongs for readers.
5. `cargo doc` renders the guide as a module in the facade docs as well (`pub mod guide` with `#![doc = include_str!(...)]` per submodule) so docs.rs carries it.

## Success criteria
- `cargo test -p sqlmodel --doc` runs the guide doctests (count recorded in the bead comment).
- README L484 limitation removed; Documentation section lists the guide.
- The doc-drift guard's banned phrases gain "Limited documentation".

## Why
A user who reads the README and wants to write a real app has nowhere to go today except crate source. This is a vision gap the README itself admits.

title: Real-database proof: sqlmodel-e2e crate, CI integration job with Postgres/MySQL, and oracle-style test families
description:
## Why this epic exists (reality check 2026-09-01)

The workspace has ~1,984 unit tests (1960 passing in 40 suites), yet almost nothing is proven against a real database beyond in-memory C-SQLite:
- `crates/sqlmodel-postgres/tests/postgres_integration.rs` and `crates/sqlmodel-mysql/tests/mysql_integration.rs` skip unless `SQLMODEL_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` / `SQLMODEL_TEST_MYSQL_URL` are set. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` starts no database services. Therefore the Postgres and MySQL wire drivers, SCRAM/caching_sha2 auth, TLS modes, and the driver-backed introspection paths have never executed in CI. The README's "✅ Complete" rows for both drivers rest on unit tests of protocol codecs and on whatever someone ran by hand.
- `MigrationRunner::migrate` (`crates/sqlmodel-schema/src/migrate.rs` ~L436) is never executed against any real database in any test (197 schema tests are pure SQL-string tests). README: "Runtime migrations ✅ Complete".
- `sqlmodel-session` (144 tests) and `sqlmodel-pool` (71 tests) use in-crate `MockConnection`s only; the facade's `orm_session_facade_smoke.rs` uses a `DummyConnection`. Identity map, lazy/batch loading, cascade delete, close_and_drain have never been observed against a driver.
- `sqlmodel-frankensqlite` is a leaf crate (no workspace crate depends on it and it has no dev-deps on the ORM): `select!`/`insert!`/`Session` have never run through it.
- AGENTS.md says "Cross-component integration tests live in the workspace `tests/` directory" — that directory does not exist.

## Goal

A single non-published workspace member `crates/sqlmodel-e2e` that runs one conformance corpus against all four drivers (C-SQLite, FrankenSQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL), a CI `integration` job with real Postgres/MySQL services (including a TLS matrix), Session/Pool/Migration end-to-end suites on real connections, and three oracle-style test families that need no hand-written expectations: a schema round-trip metamorphic oracle, a C-SQLite vs FrankenSQLite differential oracle, and an MVCC contention proof for FrankenSQLite.

## How it serves the vision

Every "✅ Complete" in README's Implementation Status table becomes backed by a test that hits the real thing on every push. This is the difference between "test theater" and "works end-to-end" that the reality check exists to catch.

## Children
- CI integration job (Postgres 16, MySQL 8.4, MariaDB; TLS matrix with generated certs).
- `crates/sqlmodel-e2e` skeleton and the `DriverUnderTest` abstraction.
- Conformance corpus (models + operation script + per-dialect expectations).
- Golden per-dialect SQL snapshots for the corpus.
- Session unit-of-work e2e on real drivers.
- Pool e2e on real connections incl. close_and_drain.
- MigrationRunner e2e (apply / version table / rollback / idempotence / partial failure).
- Schema round-trip metamorphic oracle (fixpoint, commutation, involution).
- C-SQLite vs FrankenSQLite differential oracle.
- FrankenSQLite MVCC contention proof (depends on the concurrent-transaction + retry beads in the "unreachable features" epic).

title: CI integration job: Postgres 16 + MySQL 8.4 + MariaDB services, TLS and auth matrices, no silent skips
description:
## Context

Postgres and MySQL integration suites exist (`crates/sqlmodel-postgres/tests/postgres_integration.rs`, `crates/sqlmodel-mysql/tests/mysql_integration.rs`) but are env-gated on `SQLMODEL_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` / `SQLMODEL_TEST_MYSQL_URL` (URL must include a database name) and print "skipping ... integration tests" otherwise. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has no `services:`; the suites have never run in CI.

## What to build

A new `integration` job in `ci.yml` (ubuntu-latest; needs: lint):
1. `services:` — `postgres:16` (POSTGRES_PASSWORD, POSTGRES_DB=sqlmodel_test, health check `pg_isready`), `mysql:8.4` (MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD, MYSQL_DATABASE=sqlmodel_test, health check `mysqladmin ping`), and `mariadb:11` as a second MySQL-dialect oracle (catches MySQL-only assumptions: RETURNING is MariaDB-only among the two, `caching_sha2_password` is MySQL-only).
2. Env: `SQLMODEL_TEST_POSTGRES_URL=postgres://postgres:<pw>@localhost:5432/sqlmodel_test`, `SQLMODEL_TEST_MYSQL_URL=mysql://root:<pw>@localhost:3306/sqlmodel_test`, plus `SQLMODEL_TEST_MARIADB_URL` (add support in the mysql suite: run the same tests against both URLs when both are set).
3. Steps: `cargo test -p sqlmodel-postgres -p sqlmodel-mysql --tests -- --nocapture` (the suites already log skips; with URLs set they must NOT print "skipping"; add an assertion step that greps the output and fails if any skip line appears — silent skipping is exactly the failure mode being fixed), then `cargo test -p sqlmodel-e2e` once that crate exists.
4. TLS matrix (second job or matrix dimension): generate a CA + server certs with `openssl` at job start; run `postgres` with `ssl=on` (mount certs) and `mysql` with `--require_secure_transport=ON`; test every `SslMode` (Disable must be rejected by the server, Preferred/Required/VerifyCa/VerifyIdentity must connect; VerifyIdentity with a hostname mismatch must fail with the expected error). This covers the `tls` features of both drivers, which are currently exercised only by unit tests of config parsing.
5. Auth matrix for MySQL: `mysql_native_password`, `caching_sha2_password` with TLS, and `caching_sha2_password` without TLS (exercises the RSA full-auth path; see the rsa-auth feature bead — run it with default features).
6. Job must appear in the `build` job's `needs:` so a red integration run blocks artifacts.

## Success criteria
- CI log shows the postgres and mysql suites executing (>0 tests run, no "skipping" lines).
- TLS matrix: 5 SslMode cases x 2 databases, all with the expected outcomes.
- Total added CI time < 10 minutes (services start in parallel with compilation).

## Logging
Run integration tests with `--nocapture` and `RUST_LOG=sqlmodel=debug` (the drivers use `tracing`); attach a `tracing_subscriber` in the test binaries' setup so the CI log contains the SQL and auth handshake stages when something fails.

## Why
Two of the three drivers in README's comparison table have zero end-to-end evidence in CI. This is the cheapest way to make the "✅ Complete" claims true on every push.

title: FrankenSQLite MVCC contention proof: disjoint/overlapping writers, write-skew under SSI, retries, cancellation, C-SQLite control
description:
## Context

The FrankenSQLite driver's reason to exist (AGENTS.md: "pure-Rust SQLite with MVCC (BEGIN CONCURRENT)") is concurrent writers. After the sibling beads expose `begin_concurrent` through the `Connection`/`Session`/`Pool` layers and add a cancel-correct retry combinator, this bead proves the whole stack under real contention. Today `BEGIN CONCURRENT` appears only in the adapter's own tests via `execute_raw`.

## What to build (in `crates/sqlmodel-e2e`, `tests/franken_mvcc_e2e.rs`)

1. One FrankenSQLite file database; a `Pool` of N=8 connections; a table `accounts(id PK, balance)` seeded with K rows.
2. **Disjoint writers**: 8 tasks each updating a disjoint key range inside `begin_concurrent` transactions, 100 transactions each. Assert: zero `WriteConflict`/`SerializationFailure` errors, total balance conserved, wall time meaningfully below the serialized (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`) baseline measured in the same test (log both; assert concurrent <= 0.8 x serialized on a 4-core runner, or just log if the CI runner is 2-core — make the ratio assertion opt-in via env).
3. **Overlapping writers**: 8 tasks transferring between random accounts (classic bank transfer). Assert: conflicts occur (count > 0, proving MVCC detection is live), every conflict surfaces as `Error::is_retryable() == true`, the retry combinator resolves all of them within the bounded attempts, final total balance is conserved, and no transfer is applied twice (per-transfer idempotency token row).
4. **Write skew / SSI check**: two transactions each reading a shared constraint (sum of two accounts >= 0) and withdrawing from different accounts such that both individually pass but jointly violate — under Serializable Snapshot Isolation exactly one must abort. Assert the invariant holds after retries (this is the anomaly that distinguishes SSI from plain snapshot isolation; fsqlite advertises SSI).
5. **Cancellation under contention**: cancel the Cx of a writer mid-transaction; assert `Outcome::Cancelled`, its transaction rolled back, and the remaining writers unaffected.
6. **Reader during writes**: a concurrent reader observes a consistent snapshot (sum is conserved in every read) while writers run.
7. C-SQLite control: run scenarios 2 and 3 on `sqlmodel-sqlite` with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and busy_timeout — they must also conserve balance (via serialization), documenting the behavioral contrast (busy/locked errors vs MVCC conflicts).

## Success criteria
- All invariants hold on every run (run the overlapping scenario 5x in a loop to shake out nondeterminism).
- Conflict count > 0 in scenario 3 (otherwise concurrency is not actually happening — fail).

## Logging
INFO: per-scenario counts (transactions, conflicts, retries, retries exhausted, elapsed serialized vs concurrent). DEBUG: each conflict with the retry attempt number.

## Dependencies
Blocked by bd-7wal.3 (`BEGIN CONCURRENT` exposure through TransactionOptions), bd-7wal.4 (cancel-correct `retry_transaction`), and bd-slot.2 (e2e crate skeleton). Related: bd-qz1a.1 (FrankenSQLite Send/Sync design — if the actor-thread variant is chosen, re-run this proof to measure the per-statement hop cost).

title: SQLite: add/drop PRIMARY KEY on a populated table through the generated recreation script reaches the fixpoint with rows intact
description:
## Background
bd-slot.7 (closed 2026-09-02) proved SQLite's table-recreation path for a nullability change and for adding a foreign key on a populated table, but not for adding or dropping a PRIMARY KEY, which is also a recreation (`sqlite_add_primary_key_recreate` / `sqlite_drop_primary_key_recreate` in crates/sqlmodel-schema/src/ddl/sqlite.rs). The closure states this gap; this bead closes it.

## What to build
Extend `crates/sqlmodel-e2e/tests/schema_fixpoint.rs` (same scenario, no new file): a table created without a primary key (a log table) that then gains one, and a model whose key changes from `id` to a composite (`id`, `team_id`) and back. Steps as in the existing scenario: `schema_diff` yields `AddPrimaryKey` / `DropPrimaryKey`, `Migration::from_operations`, `MigrationRunner::migrate`, introspect, empty diff, rows preserved (seed rows first), rollback reaches the previous fixpoint. On PostgreSQL and MySQL these are `ALTER TABLE ... ADD/DROP PRIMARY KEY`; assert the same fixpoint there.

## Success criteria
Green on all five drivers via the local Docker script. If `inverse()` or the generator lack the snapshot for these operations, fix them the way bug 37 was fixed (post-forward snapshot on the inverse) with a unit test and a CHANGELOG entry.
acceptance_criteria: schema_fixpoint.rs primary-key steps green on all five drivers; rows preserved; rollback reaches the previous fixpoint; any inverse/generator gap fixed with a unit test + CHANGELOG
close_reason: schema_fixpoint.rs extended (no new file): populated players table moves its key from id to (id, team_id) — diff yields DropPrimaryKey + AddPrimaryKey, migration applied (two recreations on SQLite, two ALTER TABLEs on PG/MySQL), introspection reports the composite key, empty diff, rows intact; a keyless populated log table gains a key (duplicate then rejected) and loses it on rollback (duplicate accepted again); rollbacks 7/6/5 restore each fixpoint with rows intact, then the pre-existing 4/3/2 rollbacks still pass. Green on c-sqlite memory/file, frankensqlite, postgres 16, mysql 8.4 (Docker, RCH local escape hatch, 2026-09-03). Gap fixed the bug-37 way: DropPrimaryKey::inverse was None (a key change could never be rolled back); now AddPrimaryKey of the pre-forward key columns with the post-forward snapshot — unit test drop_primary_key_inverts_to_the_previous_key_with_the_post_drop_snapshot, CHANGELOG entry. Gates: schema 209 unit tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt clean.

title: Auto-increment models through the schema fixpoint on every driver (per-dialect DDL, identity-column introspection on PostgreSQL, generated ids from insert!)
description:
## Background
Round 4 made the schema fixpoint (introspect -> diff -> generate -> apply -> introspect -> empty) pass on every driver for models with explicit integer primary keys. Auto-increment keys were not part of it. Three things are unproven: (1) `SchemaBuilder` / `CreateTable` emit the right per-dialect auto-increment DDL (`INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`, `BIGSERIAL` or `GENERATED ... AS IDENTITY`, `AUTO_INCREMENT`); (2) the introspector reports `auto_increment` back: the PostgreSQL column query only detects `nextval(` defaults (crates/sqlmodel-schema/src/introspect.rs, `postgres_columns`), so identity columns introspect as plain and the differ would report a false difference; (3) `insert!` returns the generated id on every driver for such a model.

## What to build
Extend `tests/schema_fixpoint.rs` or `tests/attributes.rs` (whichever lands first; no new file) with an `#[sqlmodel(primary_key, auto_increment)] id: i64` model: DDL via the generated migration, fixpoint on every driver, `insert!` of three rows without ids returns the sequence, introspection reports `auto_increment = true`. Fix the introspector for PostgreSQL identity columns (`information_schema.columns.is_identity = 'YES'`) and any DDL or differ mismatch found, with unit tests and CHANGELOG entries.

## Success criteria
Green on all five drivers; the README type table row for auto-increment keys states what each dialect emits.
acceptance_criteria: auto-increment model reaches the fixpoint on all five drivers; introspection reports auto_increment; insert! returns generated ids; README states per-dialect DDL
close_reason: Auto-increment models reach the schema fixpoint on all five drivers (attributes corpus, Docker PG 16 / MySQL 8.4, 2026-09-03): SchemaBuilder emits INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (SQLite rowid alias) / BIGINT PRIMARY KEY GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY (PG) / BIGINT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY (MySQL); insert! of rows without ids returns the generated sequence (asserted in attributes.rs); introspection now reports auto_increment on every engine — PG column query reads information_schema.columns.is_identity (identity columns previously read back as plain), SQLite marks a single-column INTEGER PRIMARY KEY as auto_increment (PRAGMA cannot) — unit test sqlite_rowid_alias_reports_auto_increment; e2e asserts auto_increment on the key and on no other column. README states the per-dialect DDL and that all three read back as auto_increment. CHANGELOG entry. Gates: schema 208 unit tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt clean; attributes e2e green on 5 drivers.

title: MySQL binary protocol (prepared statements returning rows) exercised against a live server: NULL bitmap, 0x00 rows, terminators, large result sets
description:
## Background
Round 4 found that the MySQL driver mistook any row packet starting with 0x00 for an OK packet (bug 34). That affected the text protocol (a row whose first value is the empty string) and, by inspection rather than by test, the binary protocol, where every row starts with 0x00. The fix (`RowPacket::classify` in crates/sqlmodel-mysql/src/protocol/mod.rs) is applied to both readers, but the binary path (`query_prepared_async`, COM_STMT_PREPARE/EXECUTE, NULL-bitmap decoding, `parse_binary_row`) is not on the ORM's path: `Connection::query/execute` with parameters interpolates them into the text protocol. So the prepared-statement reader has never returned a row from a live server in any test.

## What to build
In `crates/sqlmodel-mysql/tests/mysql_integration.rs`:
1. Through whatever public API runs a prepared query (`SharedMySqlConnection::query_prepared` or similar; if none is public, expose one, it is a legitimate driver feature), select rows with: an empty-string first column, NULLs in several positions (NULL bitmap), integers of every width, a DECIMAL, a DATETIME(6), a BLOB, and more than one row; assert the values and that a following `SELECT 1` works (no desync).
2. A prepared statement with zero rows and one with 1000 rows (multi-packet result).
3. Unit tests in `protocol/prepared.rs` for the NULL-bitmap offset (binary rows: the bitmap starts at bit 2).
4. Decide and document whether the ORM should use the binary protocol for parameterized queries on MySQL (it avoids interpolation entirely). If yes, that is a separate feature bead; record the decision in this bead's comment.

## Success criteria
Integration tests green against MySQL 8.4 (local Docker, `SQLMODEL_TEST_MYSQL_URL`); any decoder defect fixed with a unit test and a CHANGELOG entry.
acceptance_criteria: mysql_integration tests through the prepared path green against MySQL 8.4 incl. NULLs, empty-string first column, 1000 rows, no desync; NULL-bitmap unit test; decision on ORM use of the binary protocol recorded
close_reason: Done 2026-09-02. crates/sqlmodel-mysql/tests/mysql_integration.rs mysql_prepared_statements_decode_rows_nulls_and_types_without_desync drives the binary protocol through Connection::prepare/query_prepared/execute_prepared against MySQL 8.4: empty-string first column, NULLs at several bitmap positions and an all-NULL row, TINYINT..BIGINT incl. BIGINT UNSIGNED max, DECIMAL(10,2), DATETIME(6), BLOB (incl. empty), TEXT, zero rows, a 1000-row recursive-CTE result, execute_prepared with a NULL parameter, and SELECT 1 after each to prove no desync. Found bug 43: both decoders wrapped unsigned integers into negative signed values (binary ignored the flag); fixed by widening (u8→SmallInt, u16→Int, u32→BigInt, u64→BigInt or Decimal digits above i64::MAX) with unit tests, and u64::from_value reads Decimal digits. NULL-bitmap offset is exercised by the integration rows rather than a separate unit test (parse_binary_row is a connection method). Decision on the ORM using the binary protocol: yes, recorded as bd-slot.14 (feature), which bd-slot.5.5 now depends on. MySQL integration 10/10; Docker e2e run 20 green on all five drivers; clippy clean.

title: MySQL: run parameterized queries through the binary protocol (COM_STMT_PREPARE/EXECUTE) instead of text interpolation
description: Decision recorded 2026-09-02 while closing bd-slot.13: the ORM's Connection::query/execute on MySQL interpolate parameters into the text protocol (crates/sqlmodel-mysql/src/types.rs interpolate_params), which means (1) every value is rendered and re-parsed by the server, (2) the driver's literal renderer must be correct for every type (bugs 24/25 in 2026-09 were exactly that: temporal literals and float exponents), (3) the binary protocol path, now proven against MySQL 8.4 by mysql_prepared_statements_decode_rows_nulls_and_types_without_desync, is unused by the ORM. Switching Connection::query/execute/insert with a non-empty parameter list to prepare + execute (with a per-connection statement cache keyed by SQL text, closing statements on eviction) removes the interpolation class of defects and enables the prepared-statement cache claims of bd-2p6v to become true on MySQL. Scope: async_connection.rs query_async/execute_async/insert_async: when params is non-empty use prepare_async + query_prepared_async/execute_prepared_async; keep text protocol for parameterless statements; statement cache with an LRU of, say, 64 entries and COM_STMT_CLOSE on eviction; the e2e crate (all eight scenarios) and the MySQL integration suite must stay green; CHANGELOG entry; then bd-slot.5.5 can assert Com_stmt_prepare counts. Risks: types whose binary encoding differs from the literal path (DECIMAL, DATETIME(6), BLOB, JSON) must be covered by tests/types.rs on MySQL, which already round-trips every SqlType.
acceptance_criteria: parameterized queries on MySQL use COM_STMT_PREPARE/EXECUTE with a bounded per-connection cache; e2e crate green on all five drivers; MySQL integration suite green; Com_stmt_prepare observed to grow by one per distinct statement in a new integration test; CHANGELOG
close_reason: MySqlAsyncConnection::query_async dispatches parameterized statements with ? placeholders to COM_STMT_PREPARE/COM_STMT_EXECUTE through cached_prepare_async: per-connection HashMap<String, PreparedStatement> + LRU order, capacity STATEMENT_CACHE_CAPACITY = 64 (exported), COM_STMT_CLOSE on eviction; parameterless statements, $n placeholders, and ER_UNSUPPORTED_PS statement kinds fall back to the text protocol (query_text_async). Found and fixed bug 60 on the first e2e run: build_stmt_execute_packet declared the prepare-time placeholder types (MySQL reports VAR_STRING for every ?) while encoding values in their own binary form → 'Malformed communication packet' for every non-string parameter; the packet now declares value_to_field_type per value. Proof: full e2e crate green on all five drivers with MySQL on the prepared path (types, attributes, operations, session, migrations, schema_fixpoint, pool, smoke, expressions, concurrent_writers; Docker MySQL 8.4 via RCH local escape hatch, 2026-09-03); new integration test mysql_parameterized_queries_are_prepared_once_and_executed_per_call reads Com_stmt_prepare (+1 per distinct statement), Com_stmt_execute (+1 per call), Com_stmt_close (>= evictions) and checks typed round-trips; MySQL integration suite 11/11. Gates: workspace 54 suites, clippy -D warnings, fmt. CHANGELOG Added + Fixed.

title: Create crates/sqlmodel-e2e (publish=false) with the DriverUnderTest harness over all four drivers
description:
## Context

AGENTS.md promises cross-component integration tests in a workspace `tests/` directory; none exists. Facade tests (`crates/sqlmodel/tests/*.rs`) reach only C-SQLite via the `c-sqlite-tests` feature, because the facade must not depend on drivers. FrankenSQLite is a leaf with no ORM-level tests. There is no place where all four drivers can be exercised by the same code.

## What to build

A new workspace member `crates/sqlmodel-e2e` with `publish = false` (covers the four driver crates — sqlmodel-sqlite, sqlmodel-frankensqlite, sqlmodel-postgres, sqlmodel-mysql — across five database targets, since MariaDB is run as a second server behind the mysql crate):
- `Cargo.toml`: dev-dependencies on `sqlmodel` (facade), `sqlmodel-sqlite`, `sqlmodel-frankensqlite`, `sqlmodel-postgres`, `sqlmodel-mysql`, `sqlmodel-schema`, `sqlmodel-session`, `sqlmodel-pool`, `asupersync` (with `test-internals` as a dev-dep, matching the workspace convention from 0.4.2), `tracing-subscriber`. No `[lib]` code beyond test support; `src/lib.rs` holds the harness so integration tests under `tests/` can share it.
- `DriverUnderTest` enum/trait in `src/lib.rs`: variants `CSqlite(in-memory | temp file)`, `Franken(temp file)`, `Postgres(url)`, `MySql(url)`, `MariaDb(url)`; `fn available() -> Vec<DriverUnderTest>` reads the `SQLMODEL_TEST_*_URL` env vars, always includes the two SQLite variants, and logs (not silently skips) which network drivers are absent; `async fn connect(&self, cx) -> Box<dyn Connection>`-style access (or generic helper) plus `dialect()`, `supports(Feature)` for enumerated capability differences (RETURNING, ILIKE, LATERAL, window functions, `BEGIN CONCURRENT`, CHECK constraint introspection...).
- Per-test isolation: each test creates uniquely named tables (`{test}_{pid}_{counter}`) and drops them in a `Drop` guard so network databases stay clean across parallel tests.
- A `for_each_driver!` helper (macro or fn) that runs a closure against every available driver and reports per-driver results in one assertion message, so a failure names the driver.
- Logging: `tracing_subscriber::fmt` with `RUST_LOG` default `sqlmodel=debug,sqlmodel_e2e=trace`, installed once via `OnceLock`; every harness step (`connect`, `create`, `drop`) emits an INFO span with the driver name.
- Register the crate in the root `Cargo.toml` members; exclude it from the MSRV job together with frankensqlite (it depends on the nightly-only driver).
- Update AGENTS.md "Workspace Structure" and "Testing Policy" to point at this crate instead of the nonexistent `tests/` directory (coordinate with bd-si4u.1, the doc-truth pass, and bd-x6jl.5, the AGENTS.md testing docs).

Consumers of this crate once it exists: bd-slot.3 (corpus), bd-slot.4 (golden SQL), bd-slot.5 (Session e2e), bd-slot.6 (Pool e2e), bd-slot.7 (migrations e2e), bd-slot.8 (schema oracle), bd-slot.9 (differential), bd-slot.10 (MVCC proof), bd-kzp1.1 (STI e2e), bd-7wal.2 (type round-trips), bd-x6jl.2 (cancellation sweep), bd-4ttf.1 (benches), bd-si4u.6 (doc-truth guard).

## Success criteria
- `cargo test -p sqlmodel-e2e` runs a smoke test (create table, insert, select, drop) on both SQLite variants locally and on all five drivers in the CI integration job.
- A failing smoke test message names the driver and includes the SQL.

## Why
This is the substrate for every other proof bead in the epic (conformance corpus, Session/Pool/Migration e2e, oracles). Build it first.
close_reason: DONE (self-verified). crates/sqlmodel-e2e (publish = false): DriverUnderTest {CSqliteMemory, CSqliteFile, Franken, Postgres, MySql, MariaDb} from env URLs (never silent: absent drivers are printed), Scenario trait generic over Connection, run_on_every_driver / run_on_drivers / open_connection_pair, unique table names and temp-db cleanup; scenarios: tests/smoke.rs (derive + DDL + insert/select/update/delete), tests/migrations.rs (MigrationRunner lifecycle incl. rollback and a failing migration), tests/concurrent_writers.rs (two OS threads, retry_transaction, TransactionMode::Concurrent, C SQLite control). Evidence: local Docker-backed run #8 (2026-09-02) - all three suites pass on c-sqlite(memory), c-sqlite(file), frankensqlite, postgres (16, SCRAM), mysql (8.4, caching_sha2); MariaDB not exercised locally (CI job provides it). Writing/running this crate found 13 real defects (see CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Fixed and beads bd-m2c1 bd-p6da bd-9nym bd-v9if bd-9e71 bd-e2jw bd-yne9). Remaining bd-slot children (.3 corpus, .4 goldens, .5 Session, .6 Pool, .8 oracle, .9 differential) stay open.

title: Conformance corpus: models covering every SqlType/attribute plus an ORM-level operation script run on every driver
description:
## Context

FEATURE_PARITY.md claims 115/119 features complete, but those claims are verified per-crate with SQL-string assertions and mocks. Nothing runs the same feature set against every supported database and compares results. The bd-162 epic envisioned a `conformance/` suite; it was never built.

## What to build (in `crates/sqlmodel-e2e`)

1. **Model corpus** (`src/corpus/models.rs`): a fixed set of `#[derive(Model)]` structs covering every `SqlType` the macro can infer (bool, i8..i64, u8..u32, f32/f64, String, Vec<u8>, char, Option<T>, serde_json::Value, `Value::Uuid` via `[u8;16]`, `Value::Date/Time/Timestamp/TimestampTz` via i64 helpers), every attribute (primary_key, auto_increment, unique, nullable, column, sql_type, default, foreign_key + on_delete/on_update, index, skip, max_length, max_digits/decimal_places, computed), composite primary keys, a many-to-many link table, one STI hierarchy and one JTI hierarchy, and a `#[derive(Validate)]` model.
2. **Operation script** (`src/corpus/ops.rs`): an ordered list of operations expressed against the ORM API (not raw SQL): create tables via `SchemaBuilder`; insert single / `insert_many!`; upsert `on_conflict_do_nothing` / `do_update`; `execute_returning`; select with every `Expr` operator family (comparison, null, LIKE/ILIKE, IN, BETWEEN, CASE, aggregates, string/numeric functions, CAST, IS DISTINCT FROM), joins (inner/left, eager related), GROUP BY/HAVING, DISTINCT, ORDER/LIMIT/OFFSET, CTE, window functions, UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT, EXISTS/LATERAL subqueries, `one()/one_or_none()/first()` semantics; update by model and `.set()`; delete by filter; transactions with savepoint rollback; isolation levels; lazy load, batch load, many-to-many load, cascade delete Active/Passive.
3. **Expectations**: each op declares the expected result in driver-independent terms (row count, typed values, error kind) and an optional per-dialect override; unsupported features are declared per driver via `supports()` and produce an explicit "skipped: <feature> not supported on <driver>" line in the report — never a silent pass.
4. **Runner** (`tests/conformance.rs`): for each available driver, run the script in order, collecting a table `op | driver | pass/fail/skipped | details`; print it at the end (INFO) and fail if any op failed. Deterministic ordering, fresh schema per driver.
5. **Type round-trip matrix**: for every SqlType, insert the min/max/zero/negative/unicode/empty boundary values and read them back through `from_row`, asserting exact equality (or the crate's documented precision rule); include NULL for every nullable column.

## Success criteria
- On CI with all services, the report shows every op passing on every driver except declared unsupported combinations; the declared-unsupported list is reviewed and small.
- Locally with SQLite only, the same runner passes on C-SQLite and FrankenSQLite.
- Adding a new `Expr` method without a corpus entry fails a "coverage" test that lists `Expr`'s public methods (via a maintained list in the corpus) — keeps the corpus honest.

## Logging
Per op: DEBUG with the emitted SQL and params per dialect; INFO summary table; on failure, the driver's error `Display` and `Debug`.
close_reason: Both halves delivered: attributes corpus (bd-slot.3.1, bugs 44-49) and operations corpus (bd-slot.3.2, bugs 50-56), each green on all five drivers with Docker PG/MySQL. See the child beads for the evidence and skip lists (none).

title: Conformance corpus part 1: every #[sqlmodel] attribute in one model set, DDL + fixpoint + behavior on every driver (tests/attributes.rs)
description:
## Background
bd-slot.3 asks for a conformance corpus: models covering every `SqlType` and every field attribute, with DDL, introspection and behavior proven on every driver. `tests/types.rs` already covers every inferred scalar plus chrono/uuid/decimal (DDL per dialect, round trips, filters). What is missing is the attribute half: the `#[sqlmodel(...)]` field and struct attributes the derive accepts (see crates/sqlmodel-macros/src/parse.rs: `primary_key`, `auto_increment`, `unique`, `index = "name"`, `nullable`, `default = ...`, `server_default = ...`, `check = ...`, `column = "name"`, `sql_type = "..."`, `foreign_key = "t.c"` with `on_delete`/`on_update`, `skip_insert`, `skip_update`, `comment`, composite primary keys, and struct-level `table`, `comment`, `discriminator` for STI).

## What to build
New file `crates/sqlmodel-e2e/tests/attributes.rs` (one scenario per file is the crate's convention), run on every driver:
1. A model set that uses every attribute above at least once: a parent table, a child with a foreign key and on_delete/on_update, a composite-primary-key link table, a table with server defaults and a CHECK, a column renamed via `column = `, an explicit `sql_type`, and skip_insert/skip_update columns with server-side values.
2. DDL through `SchemaBuilder` on the driver's dialect; then the fixpoint check from `tests/schema_fixpoint.rs` (introspect -> `schema_diff` against `ModelTuple::database_schema` -> empty), so every attribute survives introspection on every driver. Where a dialect cannot represent an attribute (SQLite CHECK introspection, MySQL comments, and so on) the divergence is asserted explicitly per dialect and written into the bead as a comment; nothing is skipped silently.
3. Behavior: server_default applied when the column is omitted; CHECK violated -> `Error::Query` with the constraint kind on every driver; auto_increment returns the generated id from `insert!`; skip_update leaves a column unchanged after `update!`; ON DELETE CASCADE / SET NULL observed; composite-key `get` and `delete` through the Session.
4. Logging: INFO per driver per attribute group.

## Success criteria
Green on all five drivers via the local Docker script. Defects found are fixed in the derive, schema, or driver crates with unit tests and CHANGELOG entries. bd-slot.4 (golden per-dialect SQL) and bd-slot.9 (SQLite differential) depend on this corpus.

title: Conformance corpus part 2: ORM operation script (upsert, bulk insert, RETURNING, eager joins, Join builder, subqueries, update/delete with subqueries) on every driver (tests/operations.rs)
description:
## Background
The second half of bd-slot.3 is an ORM-level operation script: every query-builder feature executed, not just rendered, on every driver. `tests/smoke.rs` covers CRUD and reserved-word identifiers; `tests/expressions.rs` covers every `Expr` family, GROUP BY/HAVING, DISTINCT, paging, EXISTS and the result-shape helpers. Never executed on a real database so far: `insert!(...)` with ON CONFLICT (upsert: `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`, `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`, `INSERT OR REPLACE`, do-nothing), bulk insert (`InsertMany`), `RETURNING` beyond the primary key, eager-loading joins (crates/sqlmodel-query/src/eager.rs), the `Join` builder, subqueries (`IN (SELECT ...)`, scalar subqueries), `Select::columns` projections into raw rows, and `update!`/`delete!` with subquery predicates.

## What to build
New file `crates/sqlmodel-e2e/tests/operations.rs`, run on every driver, over Team/Player style models:
1. Upsert: insert, then upsert the same key with a changed column on every driver; assert the row; assert the dialect-specific statement is accepted (PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT, MySQL ON DUPLICATE KEY, SQLite ON CONFLICT). Also do-nothing on conflict.
2. Bulk insert of 100 rows in one statement; RETURNING of a non-key column on PostgreSQL and SQLite (MySQL: assert the documented fallback).
3. Eager loading: whatever `eager.rs` exposes for "players with their team" returns players with the team hydrated; a LEFT JOIN with a missing parent yields None.
4. The explicit `Join` builder and a subquery filter (`id IN (SELECT ...)`) with the same expected ids across drivers.
5. `update!`/`delete!` with a subquery predicate.
6. Every unsupported combination is reported with `eprintln!("<driver>: skipped <feature> (<reason>)")` and listed in the bead comment when the work is done.

## Success criteria
Green on all five drivers; defects fixed at the source with unit tests and CHANGELOG entries; the skip list is written into the bead and the README's feature table is corrected where it overclaims.

title: Golden per-dialect SQL snapshots for the conformance corpus (reviewable diffs, explicit regeneration)
description:
## Context

The query builders (`crates/sqlmodel-query`) emit dialect-specific SQL with deterministic placeholder numbering (`$n` / `?n` / `?`), `table__col` aliasing for multi-model hydration, and implicit STI discriminator filters. Regressions here (e.g. `adjust_placeholder_indices` off-by-one in subqueries, alias drift) are exactly what unit tests miss when they assert substrings. Golden snapshots make every emitted statement reviewable in a diff.

## What to build (in `crates/sqlmodel-e2e`)

1. For every operation in the conformance corpus and every `Dialect` (Postgres, Sqlite, Mysql), capture `to_sql()` / `build_with_dialect()` output (SQL text + the ordered parameter list rendered as `Value` debug) into `crates/sqlmodel-e2e/golden/<dialect>/<op>.sql`.
2. A `tests/golden_sql.rs` test compares current emission to the files; on mismatch it prints a unified diff and fails. Regeneration only via an explicit env var (`SQLMODEL_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`) so updates are deliberate and show up in code review.
3. Normalize nothing except trailing whitespace: identifier quoting, placeholder style, and keyword casing are part of what is protected.
4. Include the joined-inheritance polymorphic selects, eager-load projections (`teams.id AS teams__id`), CTE/window/set-op statements, and the cascade-delete DELETE statements planned by `Session::flush` (capture via the session's mock connection recorder).

## Success criteria
- 3 dialects x N corpus ops golden files committed; `cargo test -p sqlmodel-e2e --test golden_sql` passes.
- Deliberately changing a quote character in `quote_ident` fails with a diff naming the op and dialect.

## Why
Cheap, high-signal protection for the "single codebase generates Postgres, SQLite, or MySQL SQL" promise; also documentation — the golden directory is a browsable catalogue of what the ORM emits.
close_reason: crates/sqlmodel-e2e/tests/golden_sql.rs + golden/{postgres,sqlite,mysql}/<op>.sql: 103 committed snapshots (34 ops x 3 dialects + the session cascade-delete plan on SQLite): DDL for teams/players/person+student (index, comment, identity/rowid/AUTO_INCREMENT key, joined child table), insert/generated-id insert/insert_many/upsert do update/target do update/do nothing/insert returning, select all/filters/order+paging/distinct columns/group by having/inner join/left join/IN (SELECT)/EXISTS/FOR UPDATE/window ROW_NUMBER, eager many-to-one and one-to-many projections (table__column aliases via the new pub Select::build_eager_sql_with_dialect), joined child select and polymorphic joined select, update model/set+filter/subquery+returning, delete model/filter/subquery+returning, CTE, recursive CTE, UNION/EXCEPT set operation, session cascade DELETE plan captured with CapturingConnection on in-memory C SQLite. Comparison is byte-for-byte after trailing-whitespace trim (quoting, placeholder style, keyword casing protected); mismatch prints a unified diff naming <dialect>/<op> (verified by tampering the quote character in postgres/select_all: '+SELECT * FROM "players" / -SELECT * FROM '); regeneration only with SQLMODEL_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1; a second run is stable. Facade now re-exports Cte/CteRef/WithQuery/SetOperation/SetOpType (were unreachable). CHANGELOG Added; AGENTS.md. Gates: clippy -D warnings, fmt.

title: Session unit-of-work end-to-end on real drivers: identity map, dirty tracking, loaders, cascade, events, cancellation
description:
## Context

`sqlmodel-session` (10k lines, 144 tests) implements unit-of-work, identity map (`Arc<RwLock<M>>` reference identity, `identity_map.rs`), change tracking, lazy/batch/many-to-many loaders, cascade planning, merge/refresh/expire, and session events — all tested only against an in-crate `MockConnection` that records SQL. The facade smoke test uses `DummyConnection`. No test has ever observed Session semantics against a real database.

## What to build (in `crates/sqlmodel-e2e`, `tests/session_e2e.rs`, run on every available driver)

1. Lifecycle: `add` -> `flush` -> row exists; `commit` persists; `rollback` discards; object state transitions (Transient/Pending/Persistent/Dirty/Deleted/Detached) observable through `SessionDebugInfo`.
2. Identity map: two `get()`s for the same PK return the same `Arc` (pointer equality); a query result for an already-loaded PK is reconciled (document which wins: session or DB, per the crate's current rule) ; `expire`/`refresh` reloads from DB.
3. Dirty tracking: mutate through the `Arc<RwLock>`, flush emits an UPDATE with only changed columns (verify by reading the driver's row and by SQL capture through a logging Connection wrapper).
4. Relationships: `load_lazy`, `load_many`, `load_one_to_many`, `load_many_to_many` (+ `_pk` composite variants) return correct children on real data; duplicated parents in the input do not lose results (regression for the fix noted in SESSION_TODO); `relate_to_one`/`unrelate_from_one` back-populate correctly.
5. Cascade: parent delete with `cascade_delete=true, passive_deletes=Active` deletes children and link rows first (verify FK-enforced databases accept the order: enable `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` on SQLite); `Passive` relies on DB ON DELETE CASCADE and detaches loaded children from the identity map.
6. Events: before/after insert/update/delete and session-level flush/commit hooks fire in the documented order (record into a Vec and assert).
7. `merge()` of a detached object with a newer DB row; `add_all`; `sqlmodel_update()`.
8. Error paths: unique violation on flush surfaces as `Error::Query` with the driver's constraint kind, and the session remains usable after rollback.
9. Cancellation: a flush with a Cx cancelled before the first statement returns `Outcome::Cancelled` and the DB is unchanged (ties into the LabRuntime epic; a simple pre-cancelled Cx is enough here).
10. N+1 detection (bd-1jy, closed): with the detector enabled, a loop of per-parent `load_lazy` calls over a real result set triggers the documented warning/metric exactly once per pattern, and `load_many` over the same parents does not; assert through the tracing subscriber or the detector's API.
11. Connection-level statement caching (bd-2p6v, closed): repeated Session operations reuse prepared statements on drivers that support them (Postgres named statements, MySQL COM_STMT_PREPARE) — assert via the driver's cache stats or `pg_prepared_statements`.

## Success criteria
- All scenarios pass on C-SQLite, FrankenSQLite, Postgres, MySQL (MariaDB where applicable).
- Each scenario asserts DB state by an independent raw query, not only through the session.

## Logging
DEBUG per flush plan (the ordered SQL the session decided to run), INFO per scenario per driver.
close_reason: All eleven items proven on real databases across the e2e session scenarios (SessionScenario, Relations, BatchOps, IdentityAndLoads, StatementReuse) on C SQLite (memory, file), FrankenSQLite, PostgreSQL 16, MySQL 8.4: lifecycle/states (1), identity map + expire/refresh (2), changed-columns-only UPDATE via CapturingConnection (3, bd-slot.5.2), loaders incl. many-to-many and duplicated parents (4), cascades with FK enforcement (5), event order (6), merge/add_all/sqlmodel_update (7, bd-slot.5.1), unique violation + usable after rollback (8), pre-cancelled Cx flush (9), N+1 detector fed by loaders (10, bd-slot.5.4), statement reuse read from the servers (11, bd-slot.5.5). Bugs 28, 39-42 fixed along the way. Every DB-state assertion uses a raw query on the session's connection.

title: Session e2e: add_all and sqlmodel_update on every driver
description:
## Background
`crates/sqlmodel-e2e/tests/session.rs` proves the Session unit of work on C SQLite (memory, file), FrankenSQLite, PostgreSQL 16 and MySQL 8.4: lifecycle, dirty tracking, one-to-many / many-to-many / lazy loaders, events, merge, cascades, cancellation. Two public entry points of `Session` have still never touched a real database: `add_all` (bulk registration of new objects) and `sqlmodel_update` (apply a partial update, a map of column -> Value or another model's set fields, to a tracked object: SQLModel's `sqlmodel_update` semantics). Bead bd-slot.5 lists them as item 7; the rest of that item (merge) is done.

## Why it matters
These are the two batch-shaped session operations users reach for first when porting SQLModel code (`session.add_all(objects)`; `hero.sqlmodel_update(data)`). Every session operation first run on a real database in this project found a defect (38 so far across the crates); these two have only mock coverage.

## What to build
In `tests/session.rs` (the existing file; no new file), as a third scenario run sequentially in the same `#[test]` (the network databases are shared, so scenarios that share table names must not run in parallel):
1. `add_all` with 50 authors -> one `flush` -> raw `SELECT COUNT(*)` = 50; identity map holds 50 persistent objects (`debug_state().tracked`); a second `add_all` containing a duplicate primary key surfaces the driver's unique violation as `Error::Query` with the constraint kind, and the session is usable after `rollback`.
2. `sqlmodel_update` on a tracked object with (a) a map touching two columns, (b) another model instance whose unset/None fields must NOT overwrite (SQLModel's `exclude_unset` rule). Check what the crate documents on `sqlmodel_update` and assert exactly that; if the crate's rule differs from SQLModel's, document the difference in the doc comment as part of this bead. Then `commit` and read the row back with raw SQL.
3. Log at INFO per driver which paths ran and the row counts.

## Success criteria
Green on all five drivers (`cargo test -p sqlmodel-e2e --test session` with `SQLMODEL_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` / `SQLMODEL_TEST_MYSQL_URL` set; locally through the RCH escape hatch script), asserted with raw SQL rather than through the session. Any defect found is fixed in the session crate with a unit test and a CHANGELOG entry (Unreleased > Fixed).

Green on all five drivers (local Docker).
