title: Session::flush updates only changed columns; CapturingConnection wrapper in sqlmodel-e2e proves the statement on every driver
description:
## Background
`Session::flush` (crates/sqlmodel-session/src/lib.rs, the `pending_dirty` loop) decides an object is dirty by comparing `serde_json::to_vec(&tracked.values)` with `original_state`, and then emits an UPDATE that SETs every non-primary-key column. Bead bd-slot.5 item 3 asks for "UPDATE with only changed columns, verified by reading the driver's row and by SQL capture through a logging Connection wrapper". Neither the column-level diff nor the capturing wrapper exists.

## Why it matters
Setting every column on every save (a) sends every value over the wire each time, (b) turns concurrent updates of different columns into lost updates (two sessions each write back the other's stale column), and (c) makes MySQL/PostgreSQL rewrite unchanged TEXT/BLOB values. SQLAlchemy's unit of work only SETs changed attributes, which is the behavior this project claims to port.

## What to build
1. Session: keep the per-column snapshot (`original_state` already serializes `values`; store the deserialized `Vec<Value>` or compare per index) and build the SET list from the columns whose value differs. If no column differs, emit nothing. Objects merged onto an unknown snapshot keep the all-columns behavior. Unit tests in the session crate with the in-crate `MockConnection` asserting the exact SQL (`UPDATE "t" SET "name" = $1 WHERE "id" = $2`, not every column).
2. e2e crate: add a `CapturingConnection<C>` wrapper in `crates/sqlmodel-e2e/src/lib.rs` that implements `Connection` by delegating to `C` and records every SQL string and parameter list executed (an `Arc<Mutex<Vec<(String, Vec<Value>)>>>`). It must be generic over the driver and delegate `begin`/`begin_with_options` (the transaction type of `C` is used as-is; statements run through the transaction are captured too if the transaction type can be wrapped, otherwise document that only connection-level statements are captured and use `flush` outside an explicit transaction in the tests).
3. `tests/session.rs`: through the wrapper, mutate one column of a persistent object, `flush`, assert the captured UPDATE names exactly that column (dialect-quoted) on every driver, and assert the row with raw SQL.
4. CHANGELOG: Fixed ("Session::flush updated every column") and Added (`CapturingConnection`, test-only, in the e2e crate).

## Success criteria
Session unit tests green; e2e session scenario green on all five drivers with the captured statement asserted; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. The wrapper is reused by the identity-map, N+1 and statement-cache beads, which depend on this one.
acceptance_criteria: session unit tests assert column-level UPDATE SQL; e2e captured UPDATE names exactly the changed column on all five drivers; clippy clean; CHANGELOG Fixed + Added
close_reason: Done 2026-09-02. Session::flush builds the SET list from the columns that differ from the snapshot (original_state deserialized per column); an unchanged object emits no statement; objects without a readable snapshot keep the all-columns behavior. Unit test flush_updates_only_the_changed_columns asserts the exact SQL and params against the mock (session 146 tests green). New CapturingConnection<C> in crates/sqlmodel-e2e/src/lib.rs records every statement (connection-level; transaction objects delegate to the driver's own type, documented); the session scenario wraps the driver connection and asserts that the dirty-tracking commit issued exactly one UPDATE naming only the changed column, green on c-sqlite(memory/file), frankensqlite, postgres 16, mysql 8.4 (local Docker). clippy -D warnings clean for session and e2e. CHANGELOG Fixed + Added.

title: Session identity-map guarantees on real drivers: no second query, expire/refresh reload, documented reconciliation rule (clone semantics, not pointer identity)
description:
## Background
bd-slot.5 item 2 asked for "two get()s for the same PK return the same Arc (pointer equality)". The Session API does not hand out `Arc`s: `get` returns `Option<M>` clones out of the identity map (see `Session::get_with_options` and `TrackedObject` in crates/sqlmodel-session/src/lib.rs). The observable identity-map guarantees are therefore: a second `get` for a tracked, non-expired object does not query the database; `expire`/`expire_all`/`refresh` force the next `get` to re-query; a query result for an already-tracked primary key is reconciled by the crate's documented rule (session wins or database wins; find the rule in `lib.rs`, it lives in the identity-map merge path).

## What to build
Using the `CapturingConnection` from the flush bead (this bead depends on it), in `tests/session.rs` on every driver:
1. `get(1)` twice -> exactly one SELECT captured; equal objects.
2. `expire(&obj)` then `get(1)` -> a second SELECT captured; the value reflects a raw `UPDATE` done in between on the same connection.
3. `refresh(&mut obj)` reloads; `expire_all` after `commit` is asserted through `object_state`.
4. Load the same primary key through `select!(Author).filter(id = 1).all()` while the session holds a modified, unflushed copy: assert the crate's documented reconciliation rule, and put that rule in one sentence into the `Session` type docs if it is not there.
5. Record in a comment on bd-slot.5 that the "pointer identity" wording was wrong and what the actual guarantee is.

## Success criteria
All assertions by captured SQL count and raw rows on all five drivers; docs updated; CHANGELOG Docs entry if the reconciliation rule was undocumented.
acceptance_criteria: captured SELECT counts and raw rows on all five drivers; Session docs state the reconciliation rule; comment on bd-slot.5 corrects the pointer-identity wording
close_reason: Done 2026-09-02. tests/session.rs IdentityAndLoads scenario through CapturingConnection: a second get() for a tracked object issues no SELECT (count asserted), a raw UPDATE behind the session stays invisible until expire(), expire forces exactly one reload with the new value, refresh reloads immediately; green on c-sqlite(memory/file), frankensqlite, postgres 16, mysql 8.4 (local Docker). Session type docs now state the identity-map semantics: clones not pointers, no second query, expire/expire_all/rollback/refresh, and that query-builder results never touch the map (there is no reconciliation path to document). The pointer-identity wording in bd-slot.5 item 2 was wrong for this API.

title: N+1 detector proven on a real result set: per-parent lazy loads report once, load_one_to_many does not
description:
## Background
Bead bd-1jy (closed) added an N+1 query detector to the session (search `n_plus_one` / `NPlusOne` / `detector` in crates/sqlmodel-session/src). It has only been exercised against the in-crate mock. bd-slot.5 item 10 asks to prove it on a real result set: a loop of per-parent lazy loads must trigger the documented warning or metric exactly once per pattern, and `load_one_to_many` over the same parents must not.

## What to build
In `tests/session.rs`, on every driver, with the `CapturingConnection` (dependency) so the number of SELECTs is also asserted:
1. Seed 5 authors with 2 books each (the existing Author/Book models).
2. Enable the detector as the crate documents (config flag or builder). Loop over the authors calling the lazy one-to-many load per author; assert (a) 5 SELECTs were captured, (b) the detector reported the pattern exactly once, through its public API if it has one (counter or last report), otherwise through a `tracing` subscriber installed for the test that counts the documented event target or field names (never free-text log lines).
3. Reset, then `load_one_to_many` for all 5 parents at once -> 1 SELECT and no detector report.
4. If the detector has no public way to observe its verdict, add one (a counter on the session or a `tracing` event with a stable target) and document it; that is in scope.

## Success criteria
Green on all five drivers; the detector's observable API is documented in its doc comment and in the README's session section if the README mentions N+1 detection (if the README claims it without a way to observe it, fix the claim).
acceptance_criteria: green on all five drivers; detector verdict observable through a documented API or tracing target; README claim matches
close_reason: Done 2026-09-02. Found bug 42: no loader ever called record_lazy_load, so enable_n1_detection could never report anything. load_lazy records one load per call (keyed by the child table, 'lazy'); load_many, load_one_to_many and load_many_to_many_pk record one load per call. e2e IdentityAndLoads: five per-parent load_one_to_many calls → 5 SELECTs and potential_n1 = 1 at threshold 3; one batch call for the same parents → 1 SELECT and potential_n1 = 0; five load_lazy calls → potential_n1 = 1. Green on all five drivers. Observable API is n1_stats() (N1Stats: total_loads, relationships_loaded, potential_n1) plus the tracker's tracing warning; README lazy-loading row documents enable_n1_detection/n1_stats. CHANGELOG Fixed.

title: Prepared-statement cache claims verified against live PostgreSQL/MySQL (pg_prepared_statements, Com_stmt_prepare) or corrected
description:
## Background
Bead bd-2p6v (closed) added connection-level prepared-statement caching. bd-slot.5 item 11 asks to prove that repeated Session operations actually reuse prepared statements on drivers that support them. Round 4 established a relevant fact: the MySQL driver runs `Connection::query/execute` with parameters through the text protocol (`interpolate_params`), so its prepared-statement path (COM_STMT_PREPARE) is not on the Session's path at all; PostgreSQL uses the extended protocol (check `run_extended` in crates/sqlmodel-postgres/src/async_connection.rs for whether statements are named and cached).

## What to build
1. Establish the facts first and write them into this bead as a comment: for each driver, which path a `Session::get` takes and whether any cache is on it. If the cache from bd-2p6v is not on the Session's path for a driver, say so plainly in the CHANGELOG (Docs) and the driver README.
2. PostgreSQL: run 20 `Session::get` calls for different ids on one connection; assert via `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_prepared_statements` on the same connection that the statement was prepared once (or that the driver uses unnamed statements; then assert that and document it). Use the driver's cache statistics API if bd-2p6v added one.
3. MySQL: if the driver exposes a way to run a prepared query, run the same 20 gets through it and assert `SHOW SESSION STATUS LIKE 'Com_stmt_prepare'` increased by exactly 1; otherwise record that the Session does not use prepared statements on MySQL and add no fake assertion.
4. SQLite: assert the C driver's statement cache statistics if it has any (search `statement_cache`); FrankenSQLite: document.

## Success criteria
Every claim about statement caching in README, CHANGELOG and crate docs matches what the tests observe on live servers. No assertion may pass by a mock.
acceptance_criteria: per-driver facts recorded as a comment; live assertions where a cache is on the Session path; README/CHANGELOG/crate docs match observations; no mock-only assertion

title: Pool end-to-end on real connections: contention, timeouts, retirement, health check, close_and_drain, poisoning
description:
## Context

`sqlmodel-pool` (4k lines, 71 tests) promises timeouts, health checks (`test_on_checkout`), idle/lifetime retirement, metrics, sharding/read-replica routing, lock-poisoning recovery, and (bd-rofu, commit 38b2c0b) cancel-correct `close_and_drain`. All tests use a `MockConnection`. README: "Connection pooling ✅ Complete". The pool has never held a real driver connection in a test.

## What to build (in `crates/sqlmodel-e2e`, `tests/pool_e2e.rs`)

1. Pool over each real driver (SQLite file DB for the two SQLite variants; Postgres/MySQL URLs in CI): `PoolConfig { min, max, acquire_timeout, idle_timeout, max_lifetime, test_on_checkout }`.
2. Contention: spawn 4x`max` tasks (asupersync scope) each acquiring, running a query, releasing; assert no more than `max` connections exist concurrently (observe via `pool.stats()` and, for Postgres/MySQL, via `pg_stat_activity` / `SHOW PROCESSLIST` counts), no acquire error, all queries succeed.
3. Acquire timeout: hold `max` leases; an extra acquire returns `Error::Pool(Exhausted/Timeout)` after the configured time (use LabRuntime virtual time if available; otherwise short real timeouts).
4. Retirement: set `max_lifetime` small; after it elapses, connections are replaced (track distinct backend PIDs for Postgres via `pg_backend_pid()`; for SQLite compare connection identity via a per-connection `PRAGMA`-based token).
5. Health check: kill a Postgres backend with `pg_terminate_backend` while it is idle in the pool; next `acquire` with `test_on_checkout` transparently replaces it.
6. `close_and_drain`: with 3 active leases and 5 waiting acquirers, call `close_and_drain(cx)`: waiters get a closed error promptly, active leases finish and are retired, the call returns after the last retirement, `acquire` after close fails, and a cancelled `close_and_drain` leaves the pool closed (state preserved) — these are the exact guarantees bd-rofu listed.
7. Lock poisoning: panic inside a lease-holding task (asupersync panic boundary) and assert the pool recovers (`lock_or_recover`) and `Error::Pool(Poisoned)` is surfaced where documented.

## Success criteria
- Scenarios pass on all available drivers; counts asserted from the database side where possible.
- Runtime under 20s locally on SQLite.

## Logging
`tracing` from the pool at DEBUG (it already instruments acquire/release); the test prints `pool.stats()` snapshots before/after each scenario.
close_reason: All seven items proven on real connections in crates/sqlmodel-e2e/tests/pool.rs (SQLite file x2, PostgreSQL 16, MySQL 8.4): real-driver pool (item 1), 4 x max task fan-out under one asupersync runtime with pg_stat_activity/processlist counts (2, bd-slot.6.1), acquire timeout (3), lifetime retirement through backend ids (4, bd-slot.6.2), server-side kill + transparent replacement with test_on_checkout and the detach rule without it (5, bd-slot.6.2), close_and_drain with 3 active leases and queued waiters plus a cancelled drain leaving the pool closed (6), and a panicking lease holder (7, bd-slot.6.3). Pool defects found and fixed along the way: acquire failed instead of replacing a dead idle connection; std Condvar wait deadlocked single-threaded runtimes (bug 59); test_on_return was accepted but never implemented (removed); the crate example showed a non-existent API. Runtime on SQLite well under 20 s.

title: Pool e2e: 4x max task fan-out under one asupersync runtime with server-side connection counts (pg_stat_activity / processlist)
description:
## Background
`crates/sqlmodel-e2e/tests/pool.rs` proves the pool on real connections: fill to max, timeout, reuse, churn, close_and_drain, lifetime retirement, and two OS-thread waiters served in turn. bd-slot.6 item 2 asks for a real fan-out, 4 x max acquirers as tasks under one asupersync runtime (the pool's intended use), not OS threads, and for the "no more than max connections" claim to be checked on the server, not only through `pool.stats()`.

## What to build
In `tests/pool.rs` (extend `exercise_contention`):
1. Under one `RuntimeBuilder::current_thread()` runtime, spawn 4 x MAX tasks with asupersync's structured concurrency (the same scope/spawn API the retry or session code uses; never tokio), each acquiring, running `SELECT 1`, sleeping a few milliseconds, releasing. Assert every task succeeded, `stats().connections_created <= MAX`, `timeouts == 0`.
2. Server-side count: while MAX leases are held, PostgreSQL `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE application_name = '<tag>'` (set `application_name` through the connection config if the driver supports it; otherwise count by user and database and subtract the control connection) and MySQL `SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.processlist WHERE user = 'root'` from a separate control connection must equal MAX plus the control connection. For the SQLite file drivers the pool count is the only observable; state that.
3. Logging: INFO with the server-side count per driver.

## Success criteria
Green on the multi-connection drivers via the local Docker script; if the drivers cannot set `application_name` or connection attributes, add that config option (small feature) rather than weakening the assertion.
acceptance_criteria: all tasks succeed, connections_created <= max, timeouts 0; server-side count equals max on postgres and mysql; green via the local Docker script
close_reason: tests/pool.rs exercise_fan_out: 4 x MAX (12) acquirers spawned as tasks under one RuntimeBuilder::current_thread() runtime (rt.handle().spawn, joined in block_on), each acquire + two statements + release: all succeed, acquires 15, timeouts 0, connections_created 3 = MAX, active 0 afterwards, on c-sqlite(file), frankensqlite, postgres 16, mysql 8.4 (Docker, RCH local escape hatch, 2026-09-03). Server-side count while MAX leases are held: PostgreSQL pg_stat_activity WHERE application_name = <tag> (the pool's factory sets PgConfig::application_name) reports exactly 3; MySQL information_schema.processlist by user+db reports 4 = 3 + the control connection; SQLite drivers state the pool stats are the only observable. Found and fixed bug 59: Pool::acquire waited with std Condvar::wait_timeout, blocking the runtime thread, so under a single-threaded runtime the lease holders never ran and every waiter timed out (PG run took 93 s and failed); the wait is now asupersync Notify raced with a timer slice (cx.now() + time::sleep, as core retry does). Unit test waiters_yield_instead_of_blocking_a_single_threaded_runtime (4 tasks, pool of 1, current-thread runtime). Gates: pool 72 unit tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt; CHANGELOG.

title: Pool e2e: health check after pg_terminate_backend / KILL CONNECTION and lifetime retirement observed through backend ids
description:
## Background
bd-slot.6 items 4 and 5: prove `test_on_checkout` health checks and lifetime retirement against the server, not only the pool's own counters. The pool already replaces a connection older than `max_lifetime` on the next acquire (proven in the pool scenario through `connections_created`); nothing proves the replacement is a different server session, and nothing proves that a connection killed on the server is replaced transparently.

## What to build
In `tests/pool.rs`, PostgreSQL and MySQL only (SQLite has no server sessions):
1. Retirement: with `max_lifetime(1)`, take `SELECT pg_backend_pid()` / `SELECT CONNECTION_ID()` through a lease, release, wait, acquire again and assert a different id.
2. Health check: hold a lease, note its backend id, release it (it is now idle in the pool), then from a control connection run `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(<id>)` / `KILL CONNECTION <id>`. The next `acquire` with `test_on_checkout(true)` must succeed and hand out a working connection (`SELECT 1`); `stats().connections_closed` grew by one. Then the same with `test_on_checkout(false)`: the first statement on the dead lease fails with the driver's connection error, and the pool does not hand the same dead connection out again after it is returned. Find the exact rule the pool implements (search `test_on_return` / `is_healthy` in crates/sqlmodel-pool/src/lib.rs), document it, and assert it.
3. Logging: INFO with the backend ids.

## Success criteria
Green on PostgreSQL 16 and MySQL 8.4 via the local Docker script; the pool docs state the health-check rule the test asserts.
acceptance_criteria: different backend id after lifetime expiry; killed idle connection replaced transparently with test_on_checkout; documented rule asserted without test_on_checkout; green on postgres 16 and mysql 8.4
close_reason: tests/pool.rs exercise_server_sessions (PostgreSQL 16 + MySQL 8.4 via Docker, RCH local escape hatch, 2026-09-03): (1) max_lifetime(1) retirement observed through pg_backend_pid()/CONNECTION_ID(): the replacement is a different server session; (2) idle connection killed from a control connection (pg_terminate_backend / KILL CONNECTION): with test_on_checkout the next acquire succeeds on a new session, connections_closed +1, connections_created 2, total <= max — this required a pool fix: validate_and_wrap returned a Disconnected error after closing the dead connection and acquire surfaced it (caller had to retry); acquire now loops to the next idle/new connection (unit test test_failed_validation_routes_through_close_for_pool updated); (3) without test_on_checkout the dead lease is handed out again and its first statement fails with Error::Connection (PG 'Connection closed by server', MySQL 'Connection closed while reading header'); the documented rule is to detach() it — asserted: after detach total 0, next acquire opens a fresh session. The never-implemented test_on_return option was removed (a return is a synchronous Drop); crate docs now state the health-check rule and the crate example shows the real Pool::new(config)/acquire(cx, factory) API (it showed a non-existent one). Gates: pool 71 unit tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt; pool e2e green on c-sqlite(file), frankensqlite, postgres, mysql.

title: Pool e2e: a panicking lease holder returns its connection; accounting and close_and_drain stay consistent
description:
## Background
bd-slot.6 item "poisoning": the pool crate has unit tests for lock poisoning (`test_waiters_count_after_poisoning`) with a mock. With real connections nothing proves that a thread panicking while holding a lease leaves the pool serving other users with consistent accounting.

## What to build
In `tests/pool.rs`, every multi-connection driver:
1. Spawn an OS thread that acquires a lease and then panics (the lease drops during unwinding); join it and expect the join error.
2. Afterwards: `stats().active_connections == 0`, the pool still serves `acquire` plus `SELECT 1`, `total_connections <= MAX`, and `close_and_drain` completes.
3. If any of these hang or mis-count, fix the pool (the `Drop` of `PooledConnection` and the poisoned-mutex paths) with a unit test.

## Success criteria
Green on all multi-connection drivers; the pool crate docs say that a panicking lease holder returns its connection.
acceptance_criteria: after a panicking holder thread: active 0, acquire works, total <= max, close_and_drain completes, on every multi-connection driver; pool docs updated
close_reason: tests/pool.rs exercise_panicking_holder on every multi-connection driver (c-sqlite(file), frankensqlite, postgres 16, mysql 8.4; Docker via RCH local escape hatch, 2026-09-03): an OS thread acquires a lease, runs SELECT 1, then panics; join() is Err; afterwards active_connections 0, total 1 (the lease returned during unwinding), acquire + SELECT 1 works and reuses the connection (connections_created stays 1), close_and_drain completes, total 0. Also added exercise_cancelled_drain for the parent bead's last unproven guarantee: close_and_drain with a cancelled Cx and an active lease returns Cancelled, the pool stays closed (acquire → PoolErrorKind::Closed), the active lease still works, and a later drain completes with total 0. No pool fix was needed for these two; pool crate docs now state that a panicking holder returns its connection. Gates: fmt, clippy -D warnings; pool e2e green on all four drivers.

title: MigrationRunner end-to-end: apply, version table, rollback, idempotence, partial failure, checksum drift, SQLite recreate paths
description:
## Context

`sqlmodel-schema` implements `SchemaBuilder`, `schema_diff`, `MigrationWriter`, `MigrationRunner` (`migrate.rs` ~L436 `pub async fn migrate<C: Connection>(&self, cx, conn)`), version tracking, and introspection for all dialects. FEATURE_PARITY marks migration tracking and auto-generation "✅ Implemented"; README says "Runtime migrations ✅ Complete". No test executes `MigrationRunner::migrate` against a real database; the 197 tests assert SQL strings.

## What to build (in `crates/sqlmodel-e2e`, `tests/migration_e2e.rs`, every available driver)

1. Fresh database -> `migrate()` with 3 migrations -> version table exists with 3 rows (name, checksum, applied_at), tables exist (introspect), data seeded by migration 2 is present.
2. Idempotence: `migrate()` again applies nothing and changes no version rows.
3. Down/rollback: roll back the last migration; its table is gone; version table has 2 rows; re-apply works.
4. Partial failure: migration 3 has a deliberately failing statement after a successful one; on dialects with transactional DDL (Postgres, SQLite) the database is unchanged and no version row is written; on MySQL (non-transactional DDL) the runner must record the failure state the crate documents (define and assert it; if undefined today, define it in `migrate.rs` docs as part of this bead).
5. Checksum drift: modify an already-applied migration's SQL; `migrate()` refuses with a clear error naming the migration.
6. Generated migrations: `schema_diff(current_introspected, target_models)` -> `MigrationWriter` -> apply -> introspect again -> diff is empty (this is the fixpoint relation the metamorphic-oracle bead generalizes; do the single happy-path here so the runner bead stands alone).
7. SQLite table-recreation paths (constraint ops implemented via copy/rename in `ddl/sqlite.rs`) run for real: add/drop PK, FK, UNIQUE on a populated table preserving rows and indexes, with `PRAGMA foreign_keys` toggled as the DDL generator emits.
8. Concurrency guard: two runners started concurrently against the same database (Postgres/MySQL) — exactly one applies each migration (advisory lock or version-row uniqueness); document the mechanism if absent and implement the minimal lock.

## Success criteria
- All scenarios pass on all available drivers; MySQL partial-failure semantics are documented and asserted.
- The version table schema is asserted column-by-column via introspection.

## Logging
Runner emits INFO per migration (name, statements count, duration) and DEBUG per statement; tests run with `RUST_LOG=sqlmodel_schema=debug`.
close_reason: Done 2026-09-02. Every item of the list is exercised by crates/sqlmodel-e2e on c-sqlite(memory/file), frankensqlite, postgres 16, mysql 8.4 (Docker run 19 green): (1-3) apply/version table/rollback/idempotence (tests/migrations.rs); (4) partial failure: statements split and run one at a time, one transaction per migration where Dialect::supports_transactional_ddl (pg, sqlite: database unchanged), MySQL semantics documented on migrate() and asserted (leftover table, no tracking row, error names migration + statement); (5) checksum drift: Migration::checksum recorded, MigrationStatus::Drifted, migrate refuses naming the migration; (6) schema_diff fixpoint: tests/schema_fixpoint.rs introspect→diff→from_operations→migrate→introspect→empty diff, then evolve (ADD COLUMN), relax NOT NULL (SQLite recreation), add a nullable FK column (SQLite recreation, enforcement checked) and roll each back with rows and the index intact; (7) SQLite recreate paths: nullability and foreign-key recreation on a populated table proven; adding/dropping a PRIMARY KEY on a populated table is NOT individually exercised (UNIQUE on SQLite is an index, no recreation); (8) concurrency guard: pg_advisory_lock / GET_LOCK held for migrate()+rollback(), BEGIN IMMEDIATE + in-transaction re-check on SQLite; two-runner race applies each migration exactly once on all multi-connection drivers. Defects found and fixed along the way: 30-38 (pg introspection PKs, table order, dialect-blind expected schema, MySQL FK names, MySQL 0x00 row packets, MySQL differ false positives, unrunnable SQLite rollback stubs, FrankenSQLite stale snapshot after failed COMMIT).

title: Schema round-trip metamorphic oracle: fixpoint, commutation, involution across dialects (corpus + generated schemas)
description:
## Context

The schema subsystem has three legs: introspection (`introspect.rs`, per dialect), diffing (`diff.rs` producing `SchemaOperation`s), and DDL generation (`ddl/{sqlite,postgres,mysql}.rs`, including `SchemaOperation::inverse()`). Bugs hide in the seams (a unique index reported by introspection that the differ then tries to `DROP INDEX`; SQLite autoindex naming; MySQL implicit FK indexes; naming conventions `uk_<table>_<cols>`). Hand-written expectations cannot cover the combinatorics. Metamorphic relations can: they state properties that must hold for ANY schema, so the corpus can be large and generated.

## What to build (in `crates/sqlmodel-e2e`, `tests/schema_oracle.rs`)

Three relations, each run for every available driver and every model in the conformance corpus (and, second phase, for randomly generated table definitions via a small generator over column types / nullability / defaults / PK shapes / unique sets / FK targets / indexes):

1. **Fixpoint**: `create(M)` on an empty DB; `S = introspect(DB)`; `diff(M, S) == []`. If the differ finds work right after creation, either DDL, introspection, or the differ is wrong — the failure message prints the offending operations.
2. **Commutation**: for two schemas A, B (two corpus versions or two generated tables): `create(A)`; `apply(diff(introspect, B))`; `introspect() ≅ B` (compare with the crate's `TableInfo` equality modulo declared-irrelevant fields like index names when auto-generated).
3. **Involution**: for each op in `diff(A, B)`: `apply(op); apply(op.inverse())`; `introspect() ≅ introspect-before` — proves `inverse()` (used for rollback) is a true inverse on every dialect, including the SQLite recreate paths.

Also: **Cross-dialect agreement** — the sequence of `SchemaOperation`s produced by `diff` for the same (A, B) must be identical across dialects (dialects differ in DDL text, not in the operations), asserted structurally.

Generated-schema phase: use a tiny deterministic generator (seeded, no new dependency needed; or `proptest` as a dev-dep of the e2e crate only) with shrinking so a failing case prints a minimal table definition.

## Success criteria
- All three relations hold for every corpus model on every driver in CI.
- 200 generated schemas per driver pass locally on SQLite (both variants) in < 60s.
- Every failure prints: dialect, schema (as `TableInfo` Debug), the operations, and the DDL executed.

## Why
This replaces hundreds of brittle expected-SQL tests with three laws. It is the strongest available evidence for "Runtime migrations ✅ Complete" and for the introspection row FEATURE_PARITY still marks "⚠️ Partial".
close_reason: Schema metamorphic oracle landed in sqlmodel-e2e/tests/schema_oracle.rs. Corpus relations on every driver (C-SQLite memory/file, FrankenSQLite, plus Postgres/MySQL/MariaDB when env-gated): 7 corpus models (basic, auto-increment, defaults+check, unique, FK+CASCADE, composite PK, named indexes) satisfy (1) fixpoint — create via the differ's own CreateTable DDL, introspect, schema_diff must be empty; (2) commutation — create CommV1 (itself verified a V1 fixpoint), apply diff(V1->CommV2), require the V2 fixpoint; (3) involution — every diff operation is applied then inverted with the state required to return to the pre-op snapshot; inverse-less ops are asserted to stay within the documented destructive set. Cross-dialect agreement: the SchemaOperation sequence for identical (current, expected) pairs is asserted structurally identical across SQLite/Postgres/MySQL over 12 generated pairs, no database needed. Generated phase: 200 seeded-LCG table definitions (engine-safe by construction — indexed columns VARCHAR/INTEGER, literal defaults, single integer PK) run through the fixpoint law on all three SQLite variants (3 x 200 cases) plus commutation on every fifth case; the batch completes in well under the 60s budget (43s total for the whole suite including corpus relations on 5 drivers). Every failure message prints dialect, both schemas, the operations, warnings, and the executed DDL statement. Proptest was deliberately not added: the seeded LCG generator keeps the lockfile untouched and cases reproducible. Gates: schema_oracle 3/3 green; clippy -p sqlmodel-e2e --all-targets -D warnings clean; fmt clean. Closes the P1 lane of bd-slot.

title: C-SQLite vs FrankenSQLite ORM-level differential oracle with a truthful known-divergence list
description:
## Context

Two SQLite drivers ship: `sqlmodel-sqlite` (C SQLite via bundled libsqlite3-sys) and `sqlmodel-frankensqlite` (pure Rust, MVCC). AGENTS.md: "C SQLite still needed for triggers and `sqlite_master`" and the frankensqlite crate's test focus lists "behavioral differences from C SQLite". Nothing at the ORM level checks that the two agree on the ORM's own operations, so a FrankenSQLite behavioral change (fsqlite ships weekly: 0.3.7 -> 0.3.14 in two weeks) can silently alter ORM results for one driver only.

## What to build (in `crates/sqlmodel-e2e`, `tests/sqlite_differential.rs`)

1. Run the entire conformance corpus (ops + type round-trip matrix) on C-SQLite and FrankenSQLite side by side, in lockstep, and compare every result row-for-row (`Vec<Row>` -> normalized `Vec<Vec<Value>>`), every affected-row count, every `last_insert_rowid`, and every error KIND (not message text).
2. An explicit allow-list of known divergences (`KNOWN_DIVERGENCES: &[(op_id, reason)]`) — e.g. trigger DDL, `sqlite_master` queries, error message wording — each with a link to a frankensqlite issue or a one-line justification. Any divergence not in the list fails the test; any list entry that no longer diverges also fails ("stale divergence: remove it"), so the list stays truthful.
3. Schema oracle results (from the metamorphic bead) compared across the two drivers as well: `introspect()` must produce equal `TableInfo` for the same DDL, or the difference is in the allow-list.
4. Run against a file database for both (FrankenSQLite is file-oriented; also confirm C-SQLite `:memory:` vs file gives identical results to catch memory-only assumptions).
5. Property phase (optional, same seed generator as the schema oracle): random INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/SELECT sequences over the corpus tables, compared across drivers — a lightweight ORM-level differential fuzzer, bounded to ~500 steps in CI.

## Success criteria
- Corpus differential passes with a reviewed KNOWN_DIVERGENCES list of < 10 entries.
- A fsqlite bump that changes any ORM-visible behavior fails this test in the dependency-update PR.

## Logging
On divergence: op id, both SQL strings (they should be identical), both results (pretty-printed), fsqlite version (from `cargo metadata` at build time via `env!`/build script or a const), and the C SQLite version (`sqlite3_libversion`).

## Why
This is the guard that lets the project keep tracking FrankenSQLite's rapid release cadence (the 2026-09 dependency refresh moved 0.3.13 -> 0.3.14 with a checkpoint-watermark change) without hand-auditing each bump.

LIKE/IN/BETWEEN/NULL, DISTINCT/LIMIT/OFFSET, GROUP BY aggregates, scalar functions, inner JOIN with the qualified projection, IN (SELECT), EXISTS, typeof() storage classes, UPDATE/DELETE by filter, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE RETURNING, last_insert_rowid probes, rollback/commit, Introspector table_info/table_names, sqlite_master DDL, syntax/missing-table error kinds) runs on C SQLite (file) and FrankenSQLite (file) in lockstep; observations compared after normalizing Int/SmallInt/TinyInt/Bool→BigInt and Float→Double; error KINDS compared. Unlisted divergences fail; stale listed ones fail. KNOWN_DIVERGENCES has 5 entries, all cross-checked against the sqlite3 CLI 3.46 (C SQLite 3.53.2 is the reference-correct side): fsqlite 0.3.14 bumps last_insert_rowid() on a failed INSERT (shows in upsert do update/do nothing), does not set it for INSERT ... RETURNING (rowid after insert/delete returning), and stores CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS verbatim in sqlite_master. Filed bd-8rti to report upstream. Report prints op count, divergences with reasons, C SQLite and fsqlite versions; SQLMODEL_DIFF_VERBOSE=1 prints every observation. title: Write sqlmodel-console Cargo.toml with feature flags
description:
# Write sqlmodel-console Cargo.toml with Feature Flags

## Task Description

Create the Cargo.toml for sqlmodel-console with proper feature flags that make
rich_rust an optional dependency. This is critical for the "zero cost when disabled"
design principle.

## Cargo.toml Content

```toml
[package]
name = "sqlmodel-console"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.85"
authors = ["Jeffrey Emanuel <jeff@pastel.network>"]
description = "Beautiful terminal output for sqlmodel_rust"
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
repository = "https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/sqlmodel_rust"
keywords = ["database", "console", "terminal", "rich", "styled"]
categories = ["command-line-interface", "visualization"]

[features]
default = []

# Basic rich output (tables, panels, colors)
rich = ["dep:rich_rust"]

# SQL syntax highlighting (adds syntect dependency via rich_rust)
syntax = ["rich", "rich_rust/syntax"]

# Full feature set
full = ["rich", "syntax"]

[dependencies]
# Core (always available)
serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }

# Optional: rich terminal output
rich_rust = { path = "../../../rich_rust", optional = true }

[dev-dependencies]
# For testing output capture
# (none needed initially)
```

## Key Design Decisions

### Why Path Dependency for rich_rust?
1. Both projects are developed together
2. Avoids version sync issues with crates.io
3. Local changes immediately available
4. No network dependency during development

### Why `dep:rich_rust` Syntax?
Rust 2021+ allows `dep:` prefix to reference optional dependencies in feature 
definitions without implicitly creating a feature with the same name.

### Feature Hierarchy
```
full ──► syntax ──► rich ──► [rich_rust crate]
```

Each feature level adds capabilities:
- `rich`: Basic Console, colors, tables, panels, trees
- `syntax`: SQL syntax highlighting via syntect
- `full`: All features enabled

## Verification

```bash
# Check Cargo.toml syntax
cargo check -p sqlmodel-console 2>&1 || echo "Expected: won't work until workspace updated"

# After workspace update:
cargo check -p sqlmodel-console
cargo check -p sqlmodel-console --features rich
cargo check -p sqlmodel-console --features syntax
cargo check -p sqlmodel-console --features full
```

## Notes

- Path to rich_rust is `../../../rich_rust` because:
  - From `crates/sqlmodel-console/` we go up to `crates/`
  - Then up to `sqlmodel_rust/`
  - Then up to parent containing both projects
  - Then into `rich_rust/`
  - Adjust if your directory structure differs

- No workspace inheritance for dependencies here since rich_rust is local
acceptance_criteria:
Cargo.toml has correct package metadata
Feature flags defined (rich, syntax, full)
rich_rust is optional path dependency
serde is optional for theme serialization
Dependencies version-locked appropriately
Package compiles with all feature combinations

title: Phase 4: Query Output System
description:
# Phase 4: Query Output System

## Overview

This phase implements beautiful query result display - tables for result sets,
SQL syntax highlighting for generated queries, and query structure visualization.

## Why Query Output Matters

Query results are the primary output of a database library. Beautiful result
tables transform the experience from "reading raw data" to "understanding data."

### Before (Plain)
```
id|name|email|created_at
1|Alice|alice@example.com|2024-01-15 10:30:00
2|Bob|bob@example.com|2024-01-16 14:22:00
```

### After (Rich)
```
┌──────────────────────────── Query Results ────────────────────────────┐
│ 2 rows in 12.34ms                                                     │
├───────┬─────────────┬──────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┤
│    id │ name        │ email                │ created_at              │
├───────┼─────────────┼──────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┤
│     1 │ Alice       │ alice@example.com    │ 2024-01-15 10:30:00    │
│     2 │ Bob         │ bob@example.com      │ 2024-01-16 14:22:00    │
└───────┴─────────────┴──────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┘
```

## Components to Implement

### 1. QueryResultTable Renderable
A table specifically for query results with:
- Auto-sized columns based on content
- Type-based cell coloring (nulls gray, numbers cyan, etc.)
- Row count and timing in header/footer
- Truncation for long values
- Optional row numbers

### 2. Value Type Styling
Color values based on their SQL type:
- `NULL` → Gray, italic
- `Boolean` → Yellow
- `Integer/Float` → Cyan
- `String` → Green
- `Date/Time` → Magenta
- `Binary/Blob` → Orange (show "[BLOB: 1234 bytes]")
- `JSON` → Purple

### 3. SQL Syntax Highlighting
Use rich_rust's syntax highlighting for SQL:
- Keywords (SELECT, FROM, WHERE) → Magenta
- Strings → Green
- Numbers → Purple
- Comments → Gray
- Operators → Red
- Identifiers → White

### 4. Query Builder Visualization
Tree view of query structure:
```
SELECT from heroes
├── Columns: id, name, secret_name
├── WHERE: age > 18
├── ORDER BY: name ASC
└── LIMIT: 10
```

### 5. Query Timing Display
Visual breakdown of query execution:
```
Query completed in 12.34ms (3 rows)
  Parse:  ██░░░░░░░░ 1.2ms
  Plan:   ████░░░░░░ 3.4ms  
  Exec:   ████████░░ 7.7ms
```

## Plain Mode Output Formats

For agent compatibility, plain mode supports:
1. **Pipe-delimited**: `id|name|email` (default)
2. **CSV**: Standard CSV with quoting
3. **JSON Lines**: One JSON object per row
4. **JSON Array**: Single array of objects

The format is selectable via `QueryResultTable::format()`.

## Tasks in This Phase

1. Create QueryResultTable renderable
2. Implement Value type styling system
3. Integrate SQL syntax highlighting
4. Create QueryTreeView for query structure
5. Implement QueryTiming display
6. Add methods to sqlmodel-query Select/Insert/Update/Delete
7. Create examples and tests

## Integration with sqlmodel-query

Add console display methods to query builders:

```rust
impl<M: Model> Select<M> {
    /// Print the generated SQL with syntax highlighting.
    #[cfg(feature = "console")]
    pub fn explain(&self, console: &SqlModelConsole, dialect: Dialect) {
        let sql = self.to_sql(dialect);
        console.print_sql(&sql);
    }
    
    /// Print query structure as tree.
    #[cfg(feature = "console")]
    pub fn print_structure(&self, console: &SqlModelConsole) {
        let tree = self.to_tree();
        console.print_tree(&tree);
    }
}
```

## Dependencies (Beads)

This phase depends on:
- Phase 2 (Core Infrastructure) - SqlModelConsole
- Phase 3 (Error Display) - for error handling in display

## Performance Considerations

- Column width calculation should be O(rows × cols)
- Cache column widths after first calculation
- Truncate long values rather than wrapping (configurable)
- Limit displayed rows (e.g., first 100) with "... and N more" indicator
acceptance_criteria:
QueryResultTable renderable displays query results in table format
SQL syntax highlighting works in Rich mode
Plain mode outputs parseable tabular data
Large result sets are handled efficiently with streaming
All unit tests pass for query output
Performance benchmarks show acceptable overhead
close_reason: Phase 4 complete: QueryResultTable, SqlHighlighter, QueryTree, QueryTiming all implemented with 92 passing tests

title: Query Caching and Performance
description:
## Overview

Implement query caching and performance optimizations from SQLAlchemy.

## Query Caching

### Statement Caching
- Cache compiled SQL statements
- Reuse for repeated queries with different parameters
- lambda_stmt for lazy compilation

### Result Caching
- Cache query results
- Configurable TTL
- Invalidation on writes

## Connection Pooling Enhancements

### Pool in Session
- Session-bound connection
- Automatic checkout/return
- Connection affinity

### Read Replicas
- Route reads to replicas
- Route writes to primary
- Configurable routing rules

### Sharding
- Horizontal partitioning
- Shard key routing
- Cross-shard queries

## Bulk Operations

### Bulk Insert
```rust
session.bulk_insert_mappings(User, [
    {"name": "Alice"},
    {"name": "Bob"},
])
```

### Bulk Update
```rust
session.bulk_update_mappings(User, [
    {"id": 1, "name": "Alice Updated"},
])
```

## Query Optimization

### Eager Loading Strategies
- joinedload - Single query with JOIN
- selectinload - Separate SELECT with IN clause
- subqueryload - Subquery for related objects

### Query Hints
- FOR UPDATE
- WITH (NOLOCK) - SQL Server
- USE INDEX - MySQL

title: SchemaBuilder on MySQL: String fields map to TEXT, so unique/indexed/primary-key string columns fail with 'BLOB/TEXT column used in key specification without a key length'
close_reason: FIXED. FieldInfo::effective_sql_type_for(Mysql): Text columns that are primary keys, unique, indexed, or foreign keys are declared VARCHAR(255); plain Text stays TEXT. README quick-start DDL corrected (it claimed VARCHAR(255) for the unique email on SQLite, where it is TEXT). EVIDENCE (self-verified): local Docker-backed run #11 on 2026-09-02 (scratchpad test_e2e_local_run11.log): sqlmodel-e2e concurrent_writers, migrations, pool, session, smoke pass on c-sqlite(memory), c-sqlite(file), frankensqlite, postgres (16, scram), mysql (8.4, caching_sha2); driver suites postgres 7/7 and mysql 7/7 (run #10). Remote run g2_run4: the same e2e scenarios plus types on the three SQLite drivers. (session scenario creates e2e_session_books with a unique isbn on mysql). CHANGELOG entry.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE: the derive maps String to SqlType::Text; MySQL cannot index TEXT without a prefix length, so the DDL for e2e Book (isbn String unique) failed with 'BLOB/TEXT column used in key specification without a key length'. FIX: FieldInfo::effective_sql_type_for(Mysql): Text + (primary_key | unique | index | foreign_key) -> VARCHAR(255); documented in README/CHANGELOG. FOUND BY: e2e session scenario on Docker mysql:8.4. Proof: local run (to be posted).

title: Postgres: insert!(model).execute() never worked (builder emitted no RETURNING; driver requires it)
close_reason: FIXED. EVIDENCE (self-verified; no independent verifier available): local Docker-backed run #8 on 2026-09-02 (scratchpad test_db_backed_local_run8.log; RCH_SHIM_LOCAL_IDE=1 escape hatch because remote workers cannot reach the local containers postgres:16 @127.0.0.1:55432 scram-sha-256 and mysql:8.4 @127.0.0.1:53306 caching_sha2_password): sqlmodel-mysql lib 100 passed, tests/mysql_integration 7 passed 0 failed; sqlmodel-postgres lib 59 passed, tests/postgres_integration 7 passed 0 failed; sqlmodel-e2e concurrent_writers/migrations/smoke each 1 passed, exercising c-sqlite(memory), c-sqlite(file), frankensqlite, postgres, mysql. GitHub Actions runs for the pushed commits were still queued (never started) when checked, so CI itself has not been observed running these. Before the fix (run #3) e2e smoke on postgres failed at the first insert with 'INSERT did not return an id; add RETURNING id'; run #8 passes insert/select/update/delete on postgres.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE: InsertBuilder::execute (sqlmodel-query builder.rs) built the INSERT and called Connection::insert; the PostgreSQL driver's insert_async reads the id from the first column of the result and errors with 'INSERT did not return an id; add RETURNING id' when no rows come back. No path added RETURNING, so insert!(model).execute() had never worked on PostgreSQL. FIX: for Dialect::Postgres, when .returning() was not requested and the model has exactly one primary-key column, the builder appends RETURNING <quoted pk>; insert_async now returns 0 for a non-integer key (uuid/text) instead of an error, matching MySQL/SQLite last-insert-id semantics. FOUND BY: sqlmodel-e2e tests/smoke.rs on Docker postgres:16. Proof: e2e smoke run (to be posted).

title: Query builders emit table names bare (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE): a table named order/user/group breaks on every dialect; quote via dialect and update ~40 pinned test strings
close_reason: Done 2026-09-02: every builder quotes table names for the dialect through the new Dialect::quote_table (per-segment for schema.table, pass-through when already quoted): Select FROM/EXISTS, subquery FROM, Join tables, eager-load joins and aliased projections, joined-inheritance helpers, Insert/InsertMany/Update/Delete and their helpers; polymorphic projections deferred to build time. 46 pinned SQL strings updated; query 221 + session 145 unit tests green. Proof: e2e smoke ReservedWords scenario (table `order`, columns `user`/`select`, insert/select/update/delete) green on c-sqlite(memory/file), frankensqlite, postgres 16, mysql 8.4 (local Docker run 16). The scenario also exposed FrankenSQLite's unquoted PRAGMA table_info(order) (nameless SELECT *), fixed in the driver. Gates: fmt, clippy -D warnings, doc, workspace tests 2008 passed, audit, deny clean.

title: PostgreSQL: named prepared-statement cache on the Connection::query path (Parse once per SQL + param OIDs, Close on eviction)
description: Established while closing bd-slot.5.5 (2026-09-03): the PostgreSQL driver runs every Connection::query/execute with parameters through the extended protocol with the UNNAMED statement and portal (run_extended in crates/sqlmodel-postgres/src/async_connection.rs: Parse name "" + Bind + Execute + Sync), so the server parses and plans the statement on every call and pg_prepared_statements stays empty on the Session path. Named statements exist only for explicit prepare()/query_prepared(). MySQL got the equivalent cache in bd-slot.14 (64-entry LRU keyed by SQL text, COM_STMT_CLOSE on eviction) and the whole e2e crate proved it. Scope here: in run_extended, when params are non-empty, look up a per-connection cache keyed by (sql, declared param OIDs); on a miss send Parse with a generated name (sqlmodel_sN) followed by Sync and record it; then Bind/Execute against the named statement; bounded (64) with Close(Statement) on eviction; cache invalidated on connection reset. Risk to design around: Parse fixes the parameter types — the same SQL executed later with a differently typed Value must either hit a different cache entry (key includes OIDs) or the driver must declare OID 0 (unknown) at Parse so the server infers types from context; decide with a test that alternates Int/BigInt for the same statement. Proof: e2e crate green on postgres; an integration test asserting pg_prepared_statements grows by one per distinct statement across 20 Session::get calls and that the count is bounded by the capacity; CHANGELOG. Until then the docs state plainly that PostgreSQL does not reuse prepared statements on the query path.

title: Integrate console into sqlmodel-postgres driver
description:
## Purpose
Add rich console output to the PostgreSQL driver for connection progress, authentication feedback, and query visualization.

## Background
PostgreSQL connections involve multiple steps:
1. DNS resolution
2. TCP connection
3. SSL/TLS negotiation (optional)
4. Authentication (password, SCRAM-SHA-256, etc)
5. Parameter negotiation

Each step can be visualized to show progress and help debug connection issues.

## Implementation Details

### File Modifications
crates/sqlmodel-postgres/src/connection.rs
crates/sqlmodel-postgres/src/lib.rs (re-exports)

### ConsoleAware Implementation
Add optional SqlModelConsole to PostgresConnection:
struct PostgresConnection {
    // existing fields...
    console: Option<Arc<SqlModelConsole>>,
}

impl ConsoleAware for PostgresConnection {
    fn set_console(&mut self, console: Option<Arc<SqlModelConsole>>) {
        self.console = console;
    }
}

### Connection Progress Output
When console is Some and mode is Rich:

Connecting to PostgreSQL...
  [OK] DNS resolved: 192.168.1.100
  [OK] TCP connected
  [..] Negotiating SSL...
  [OK] SSL established (TLS 1.3)
  [..] Authenticating (SCRAM-SHA-256)...
  [OK] Authenticated as user
  [OK] Connected (server: PostgreSQL 15.2)

### Query Timing Output
For queries, optionally show timing:
Query executed in 12.3ms (5 rows returned)

### EXPLAIN Visualization
When EXPLAIN or EXPLAIN ANALYZE is run:
- Parse the explain output
- Render as a tree showing:
  - Node types (Seq Scan, Index Scan, Hash Join)
  - Costs and actual times
  - Row estimates vs actual
  - Highlighting expensive nodes

### COPY Progress
For COPY operations:
- Show progress bar with row count
- Display throughput (rows/sec, MB/s)

## Plain Text Mode
In plain mode, emit minimal text:
Connected to PostgreSQL 15.2 at localhost:5432
Query: 12.3ms, 5 rows

## Conditional Compilation
Use cfg feature flag:
#[cfg(feature = "console")]
fn emit_connection_progress(&self, stage: &str, status: StageStatus) { ... }

#[cfg(not(feature = "console"))]
fn emit_connection_progress(&self, _: &str, _: StageStatus) {}

## Verification Steps
1. Test connection with console enabled
2. Test connection with console disabled
3. Verify agent mode produces plain text only
4. Test EXPLAIN tree rendering
5. Test COPY progress
6. Verify SSL and auth step feedback
7. Test connection failure messaging

## Dependencies
- sqlmodel-console crate
- SqlModelConsole, Theme, OperationProgress components

title: Cancel-correctness proof: LabRuntime virtual time, exhaustive cancellation sweep, DPOR oracles, budget tests
description:
## Why this epic exists (reality check 2026-09-01)

Two central promises are asserted but not demonstrated:
- README "Structured Concurrency": every operation is cancel-correct ("no leaked resources"), budget/timeout enforced, proper panic boundaries. The code threads `&Cx` through 284 parameters and calls `cx.checkpoint()` at 14 sites, but no test systematically proves what happens when cancellation lands at each checkpoint, and no test proves budgets are honored mid-operation.
- AGENTS.md "Key Design Decisions": "LabRuntime for deterministic tests — virtual time, DPOR schedule exploration, correctness oracles". `rg LabRuntime crates/` returns 0 results. Pool timing tests (idle_timeout, max_lifetime, acquire_timeout) run against wall-clock time.

## Goal

Cancel-correctness becomes a tested property: an exhaustive cancellation-injection sweep over every builder/session/pool operation, LabRuntime virtual-time tests for every timing feature, DPOR exploration of the pool and session interleavings with explicit oracles, budget exhaustion tests, and AGENTS.md documentation of the harness so future beads reuse it.

## How it serves the vision

"Cancel-correct async" is the differentiator in README's comparison table (the only ✅ in the "Structured concurrency" row). A differentiator without proof is a liability. asupersync ships the tools (LabRuntime, virtual time, DPOR); the project just never picked them up.

## Children
- Pool timing under LabRuntime virtual time.
- Cancellation-injection sweep harness (`CancelAt<C>` connection wrapper, exhaustive k = 0..K).
- DPOR exploration of pool acquire/release/close_and_drain and Session flush vs concurrent loads.
- Budget/timeout exhaustion tests across drivers.
- AGENTS.md testing-section documentation of the harness.

title: Pool timing tests under LabRuntime virtual time (idle/lifetime/acquire timeout/health/close_and_drain)
description:
## Context

`crates/sqlmodel-pool/src/lib.rs` implements `idle_timeout`, `max_lifetime`, acquire timeout, `test_on_checkout`, retirement (`AcquireAction::RetireAndRetry`), and `close_and_drain`. Its 71 tests use `asupersync::{Budget, Time}` (L1348) with a MockConnection and, where timing matters, real sleeps or generous margins. AGENTS.md names LabRuntime (virtual time) as the intended testing approach; it is unused anywhere in the workspace.

## What to build

1. Add asupersync's lab/test facilities as a dev-dependency feature for sqlmodel-pool (the `test-internals` dev-feature is already enabled; confirm which feature exposes `LabRuntime`/virtual clock in asupersync 0.4.10 — search its docs; do not guess).
2. Rewrite/extend the timing tests to run under a LabRuntime with a virtual clock:
   - `idle_timeout`: acquire+release 3 connections, advance virtual time past the timeout, next acquire retires exactly the idle ones (stats assert), zero wall-clock sleep.
   - `max_lifetime`: a connection acquired repeatedly is replaced exactly when its lifetime passes, not before.
   - acquire timeout: with max leases held, an acquirer waiting `acquire_timeout` gets `Error::Pool(...)` at exactly T+timeout (virtual), and is not woken early by unrelated releases.
   - `test_on_checkout`: a mock that reports unhealthy after N virtual seconds is replaced on the first checkout after that instant.
   - `close_and_drain`: waiters are woken immediately on close (no timer needed), active leases retire on release, the drain future completes at the last release — all with deterministic ordering under the lab scheduler.
3. Keep one or two wall-clock smoke tests to guard against a runtime-integration regression the lab cannot see (document why).
4. Report the before/after test runtime for the pool crate in the bead comment (target: timing tests complete in < 100ms total).

## Success criteria
- `cargo test -p sqlmodel-pool` has zero `std::thread::sleep`/real-time waits in timing tests (grep) and total runtime drops measurably.
- Each timing feature has a virtual-time test asserting the exact instant of the effect.

## Why
Makes the pool's timing promises exact and CI-stable, and establishes the LabRuntime pattern the rest of the epic builds on.

Production: ConnectionMeta stamps asupersync Time via a TimerDriverHandle shared through PoolShared (Pool::new = wall clock, Pool::with_timer_driver injects a virtual clock); acquire deadlines/idle/lifetime checks read the same clock. Tests: 5 new LabRuntime tests prove exact virtual instants - idle timeout retires exactly the 3 expired idle conns (created 4/closed 3), max lifetime replaced exactly once past 500ms (not before at 400ms), acquire Timeout at exactly T+200ms virtual, unhealthy conn replaced on first checkout after flip, close_and_drain wakes waiter at t=0 with no timer and completes at exactly the last release (10_000ms). Meta/age/touch/backdating tests rewritten on VirtualClock. Gates: cargo test -p sqlmodel-pool 77/77 in 0.10s; clippy -p sqlmodel-pool --all-targets -D warnings clean; workspace check + clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; fmt clean; zero thread::sleep in the crate's timing tests (before: 3 sites slept on wall clock). Before/after suite runtime: 72 tests 0.11s (with real sleeps, timing behavior unproven) -> 77 tests 0.10s (timing exact, zero wall waits; long-deadline scenarios like the 10s drain hold now cost 0ms). Unblocks bd-x6jl.3 (DPOR) and bd-x6jl.5 (AGENTS.md harness docs).

title: Cancellation-injection sweep harness: CancelAt<C> wrapper, exhaustive k=0..K over every builder/session/pool/migration op
description:
## Context

The codebase has 14 `cx.checkpoint()` sites and threads `&Cx` through every async operation (284 parameters), returning `Outcome<T, E>` with `Cancelled` as a first-class result. There is no test that asks: "if cancellation is observed at checkpoint k of operation X, is the database unchanged and is every resource released?" Random cancellation tests would answer this probabilistically; an exhaustive sweep answers it definitively for each operation because K is small (single digits per op).

## What to build (in sqlmodel-core test support, reused by the e2e crate)

1. `CancelAt<C: Connection>` wrapper (test-support module, `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]`): implements `Connection` by delegating to `C` while counting "checkpoints" = every delegated call (`query`, `execute`, `begin`, `commit`, `rollback`, `savepoint`...) and cancelling the provided Cx (via asupersync's cancellation API used in tests — the `test-internals` feature) immediately before the k-th delegated call. Also record the full call sequence for assertions.
2. Sweep driver: `for k in 0..=K_max { run op with CancelAt(k); assert outcome & state }` where `K_max` is discovered by running once with no cancellation and counting calls; the sweep asserts (a) `Outcome::Cancelled` for k <= K_max, (b) DB state equals the pre-op snapshot (real SQLite in-memory: dump all corpus tables and compare) for every k, (c) if the op opened a transaction, a `rollback` (or the transaction drop path) was observed after the cancellation point, (d) no `commit` after cancellation, (e) identity map / pending sets unchanged for Session ops, (f) pool counters balanced (leases returned) for pool ops.
3. Operations swept: every builder `execute`/`execute_returning`/`all`/`one`/`first` (plain and joined-inheritance variants), `Session::{flush, commit, rollback, get, load_lazy, load_many, load_one_to_many, load_many_to_many, merge, refresh}`, `Pool::{acquire, close_and_drain}`, `MigrationRunner::migrate`, `SchemaBuilder` execution helpers, `retry_transaction` (from the retry bead: cancellation must not trigger a retry).
4. Where an operation is NOT atomic by design (e.g., migrations on MySQL's non-transactional DDL), the sweep documents the exact partial state (`allowed_partial_states`) instead of asserting no change — making the non-atomicity explicit and tested rather than hidden.
5. Run on C-SQLite in-memory for speed; the e2e crate runs the same sweep on FrankenSQLite (MVCC rollback path) and, in CI, on Postgres/MySQL for a subset.

## Success criteria
- Every listed operation has a sweep test; the sweep table (op, K_max, all-k results) is printed at INFO.
- Any op that leaves state behind after cancellation is a real bug: file it with the k and the call sequence from the recorder.

## Why
This converts "cancel-correct" from a design intention into a property checked for every checkpoint of every operation — the strongest evidence available for README's central claim, and it is cheap because K is tiny.
close_reason: Cancellation-injection sweep harness landed. sqlmodel-core gains a test-support module (feature test-support) with CancelAt<C>: a Connection wrapper that flips cx.set_cancel_requested(true) immediately before the k-th delegated call and records every delegated call (including a CancelAtTx for begin/commit/rollback/savepoints) in an ordered call log; cancel_at_call=0 is the record-only baseline run that discovers K_max. sqlmodel-e2e/tests/cancellation_sweep.rs sweeps 25 operations on C SQLite in memory: 8 builder ops, create_all, MigrationRunner::migrate, retry_transaction, 4 polymorphic/joined-inheritance ops, 10 Session ops, and the pool cancelled-acquire contract. Per-checkpoint oracles: outcome==Cancelled, checkpoint marked cancelled_before, no commit after cancellation, and state equals snapshot (create_all/migrate document their exact allowed partial states). FINDING: the sweep caught C-SQLite and FrankenSQLite TransactionOps (query/query_one/execute/savepoint/rollback_to/release/commit/rollback) ignoring an already-cancelled Cx - retry_transaction at checkpoint 2 executed the INSERT and committed anyway. Fixed both drivers with the postgres-style pre-flight cancel_requested guard (cancelled commit leaves the tx uncommitted so drop still rolls back); MySQL commit/rollback got the same missing pre-flight guard. Gates: sweep 4/4 green; cargo test core+sqlite+franken+mysql 578 passed; full e2e suite green; workspace check + clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; fmt clean. Unblocks bd-x6jl.3/.4/.5 (the same harness runs on FrankenSQLite and, in CI, the network drivers).

title: DPOR schedule exploration with oracles for pool close_and_drain, session identity-map interleavings, retry combinator
description:
## Context

The pool's `close_and_drain` (bd-rofu, commit 38b2c0b) promises: atomically close admission, wake blocked acquirers, await active lease retirement "without lost wakeups", preserve closed state on cancellation, "notify on every final active-count path", prevent post-close resurrection. The session shares an identity map (`Arc<RwLock<M>>`) between flush and concurrent loaders. These are interleaving properties; unit tests exercise a handful of orderings. asupersync's LabRuntime offers DPOR (dynamic partial-order reduction) schedule exploration, which enumerates all inequivalent interleavings of a small concurrent program — the right tool, named in AGENTS.md, unused.

## What to build

1. Pool model program under LabRuntime DPOR (sqlmodel-pool tests): 2-3 acquirers, 1-2 releasers, 1 `close_and_drain` caller, optional 1 canceller of the drain; mock connections with deterministic behavior. Oracles checked after every explored schedule: (a) no acquirer blocks forever after close (every waiter gets Ok-before-close or a closed error), (b) active count reaches 0 exactly once and the drain future completes after it, (c) no connection is handed out after close (`acquire` post-close errors), (d) a cancelled drain leaves `is_closed() == true` and a re-invoked drain completes, (e) stats invariants (idle + active <= max; created - retired == idle + active).
2. Session model program: one `flush` of N dirty objects concurrent with `load_many` of overlapping PKs on the same Session (if the API allows concurrent use; if it is `&mut self`-only, document that DPOR is unnecessary here and instead explore Session vs identity-map `Arc<RwLock>` reader/writer interleavings through the public API that does allow it). Oracles: identity map never holds two entries for one PK; a loaded object never overwrites unflushed dirty state; pending sets are consistent after any interleaving.
3. Retry combinator model (from the retry bead): concurrent retry_transaction callers on a mock that injects SerializationFailure based on schedule; oracle: every caller ends in Ok or RetriesExhausted, never a hung future; cancellation observed at any point yields Cancelled promptly.
4. Bound exploration (schedules explored ≤ a few thousand) so it runs in `cargo test`; record the explored-schedule count in the test output; keep a fixed seed for reproducibility and a way to replay a failing schedule (LabRuntime supports schedule artifacts — use the strict canonical artifacts feature noted in asupersync 0.4.7 notes).

## Success criteria
- DPOR tests exist for pool and retry programs and pass; explored schedule counts logged.
- Any oracle violation found is filed as a bug with the replayable schedule attached (that is the point).

## Why
"No lost wakeups" and "no resurrection after close" are exactly the class of bugs DPOR finds and example-based tests miss. This is where the LabRuntime design decision pays for itself.
close_reason: Bounded schedule exploration landed in sqlmodel-pool tests (dpor module). Mechanism pinned by scouting asupersync 0.4.10: there is NO complete DPOR enumerator (README disclaims it; DporExplorer is a race-informed seed sweep whose DPOR footprint sees only runtime lifecycle TraceEvents, not user sync primitives). Programs: (1) Pool close_and_drain model — 2 holders releasing at virtual 3ms/5ms, 1 waiter, 1 drainer, explored with DporExplorer::explore (34 runs, 3 schedule classes, 0 violations; oracles per run: every waiter resolves Ok-pre-close or Closed, no lease after close, drain completes, pool drains empty with created==closed==2, idle+active<=max); (2) retry combinator — two concurrent retry_transaction callers over a FlakyBegin connection injecting Serialization failures from a shared counter: with 2 injected failures both callers eventually commit (11 runs), with 11 both end RetriesExhausted (32 runs, 6 classes); no caller ever hangs and cancellation semantics stay covered by retry.rs's existing tests. Violations are collected per run and asserted after the sweep with offending seeds printed; SQLMODEL_DPOR_SEED=<n> replays a single seed, and failing seeds can be frozen via asupersync's canonical forced-schedule artifacts (record -> to_canonical_bytes -> derive_candidate) for delta-debugging. Session identity-map interleavings documented as unrepresentable: every state-mutating Session op takes &mut self, so concurrent sharing requires an external futures-aware mutex that the crate's design forbids (one Session per task over pooled connections is the intended pattern). Gates: dpor tests 2/2 green (0.02s); full pool suite 79/79; clippy -p sqlmodel-pool --all-targets -D warnings clean; workspace check clean; fmt clean.

title: Budget/timeout exhaustion tests per driver and per multi-statement operation; documented semantics table
description:
## Context

README "Structured Concurrency" lists "Budget/timeout enforcement" as a delivered property; AGENTS.md: "all database operations support cancellation via cx.checkpoint() and budget/timeout via cx.budget()". The drivers' async paths (postgres `async_connection.rs`, mysql `async_connection.rs`, frankensqlite bridge, sqlite blocking bridge) take `&Cx`, but no test exhausts a budget mid-operation and asserts the outcome and the connection's state afterwards. asupersync's `connect_timeout` is used for connects; per-query budgets are unverified.

## What to build

1. Per driver (C-SQLite, FrankenSQLite; Postgres/MySQL in the CI integration job): a query that takes longer than the budget (`SELECT pg_sleep(2)`, `SELECT SLEEP(2)`, a SQLite recursive CTE counting to 10^8 / a busy loop via `sqlite3_progress_handler` equivalent in the wrapper if the driver exposes it) run with `cx` carrying a 100ms budget. Assert: returns `Outcome::Timeout`/`Cancelled`-family (whatever the crate's convention is — pin it down and document in `Cx`-usage docs) within budget + tolerance; the connection is either still usable (query cancelled server-side via `pg_cancel_backend`/`KILL QUERY`/`sqlite3_interrupt`) or marked broken and the pool replaces it — one of the two, asserted explicitly per driver.
2. Under LabRuntime virtual time (mock connection): budget accounting across a multi-statement operation (Session flush of N objects): the operation stops at the statement where the budget is exhausted, rolls back, and reports which statement (INFO log) — sweep the budget from 0 to total cost to hit every boundary (same exhaustive idea as the cancellation sweep).
3. Pool `acquire` with a budget smaller than `acquire_timeout`: the budget wins; with a larger budget the pool timeout wins; assert both.
4. Connect timeouts: a black-hole address (RFC 5737 TEST-NET, 192.0.2.1) with a 200ms budget returns within tolerance for both network drivers.
5. Document the budget semantics table (driver x operation -> outcome variant, server-side cancel yes/no) in `crates/sqlmodel-core/src/connection.rs` docs.

## Success criteria
- Tests exist for every driver and pass in their respective environments; the semantics table matches observed behavior.
- No operation can exceed its budget by more than the documented tolerance in tests.

## Why
Budgets are how a structured-concurrency ORM avoids the "one slow query stalls the request" failure. Without tests, the feature is a hope.
notes: Recon (AmberTapir, 2026-09-04): (1) Session::flush checks only cx.is_cancel_requested — it never consults the Cx budget, so budget exhaustion alone cannot stop a flush; implementing budget semantics in sqlmodel-session is a prerequisite, not a test-only change. (2) sqlmodel-sqlite does not expose sqlite3_interrupt, so the per-driver 'server-side cancel' assertion needs driver work first. (3) Postgres (localhost:55432) and MySQL (localhost:53306) containers ARE running locally for the env-gated parts (SQLMODEL_TEST_POSTGRES_URL / SQLMODEL_TEST_MYSQL_URL). (4) Part 3 (pool acquire: budget < acquire_timeout wins; larger budget loses to the pool timeout) is fully implementable on LabRuntime today — natural first slice. Suggest splitting: 4a pool acquire budget (LabRuntime), 4b session flush budget semantics + sweep, 4c network drivers + interrupt.

title: EPIC: DDL Identifier Quoting Safety — consistent SQL identifier escaping across all crates

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Background

Multiple locations across the schema and introspection crates construct SQL DDL statements by interpolating identifier names (table names, column names) directly into SQL via format!(). While some locations use sanitization (sanitize_table_name, sanitize_identifier) or quoting (quote_ident), the approach is inconsistent:

1. **sqlmodel-schema/src/lib.rs drop_table()**: Recently fixed to use quote-escaping, but the fix is ad-hoc (manual replace)
2. **sqlmodel-schema/src/migrate.rs**: Uses sanitize_table_name() (strips to alphanumeric+underscore) — effective but lossy
3. **sqlmodel-schema/src/introspect.rs**: Uses sanitize_identifier() for PRAGMA/SHOW commands — necessary since these don't support parameterization
4. **sqlmodel-schema/src/create.rs**: Uses quote_ident() — the gold standard approach
5. **sqlmodel-session/src/flush.rs**: Uses double-quoting for table/column names in DML

## The Problem

There is no single, consistent identifier-quoting utility used across all crates. The create.rs has `quote_ident()` but other files roll their own ad-hoc escaping. This is a defense-in-depth issue:
- Table/column names come from Model trait impls (compile-time static strings), so SQL injection risk is low
- BUT if dynamic models or user-provided table names are used, the inconsistent quoting becomes a real vulnerability
- Code duplication means bugs in quoting logic get fixed in one place but not others

## Strategy

1. Create a shared `quote_ident()` utility in sqlmodel-core (or sqlmodel-query)
2. Audit and replace all ad-hoc quoting/sanitization with the shared utility
3. Add a `sanitize_identifier()` for contexts where quoting isn't possible (PRAGMA, SHOW)
4. Add tests covering edge cases: embedded quotes, unicode, empty strings, reserved words

## Why P2

The current code is safe for the common case (Model-derived static strings). The risk exists only for dynamic/user-provided identifiers. Important to fix but not urgent.

title: Implement Session.is_modified() for dirty checking
description:
## Description

Check if an object has pending changes.

## Python Behavior

```python
user.name = 'New Name'
session.is_modified(user)  # True

session.is_modified(user, include_collections=False)  # Check attrs only
```

## Rust Implementation

```rust
impl Session {
    pub fn is_modified<M: Model>(&self, model: &M) -> bool {
        let pk = model.primary_key_value();
        if let Some(state) = self.get_state::<M>(&pk) {
            return state.is_dirty();
        }
        false
    }
    
    pub fn modified_attributes<M: Model>(&self, model: &M) -> Vec<&str> {
        // Return list of changed attribute names
    }
}
```

## Dirty Tracking

Need to track original values:
```rust
struct ObjectState {
    original_values: HashMap<String, Value>,
    pending: ObjectPendingState,
}

enum ObjectPendingState {
    New,
    Clean,
    Dirty { changed: HashSet<String> },
    Deleted,
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Returns true if object has unsaved changes
- [ ] Returns false for clean objects
- [ ] Works with new (pending) objects
- [ ] Can check collections separately
- [ ] modified_attributes() returns changed field names

## Testing Requirements

### Unit Tests (crates/sqlmodel-core/src/session/dirty.rs)
- [ ] Test is_modified for unchanged object
- [ ] Test is_modified for changed field
- [ ] Test is_modified for relationship change
- [ ] Test is_modified for new object
- [ ] Test is_modified for deleted object

### E2E Tests (tests/e2e/session_dirty.rs)
- [ ] Load object → is_modified=false
- [ ] Change field → is_modified=true
- [ ] Flush → is_modified=false again
- [ ] is_modified with nested objects
- [ ] Specific field dirty check

- [ ] DEBUG: Dirty state changes
